About the team:

Our Borrowing (lending) business is growing rapidly across both our existing products and the planned launch of new initiatives. We aim to create a genuine feel-good factor when it comes to personal credit, and we’re looking for driven, analytical and creative individuals to help us achieve this goal.

We’re great believers in powerful, real-time analytics and empowering the wider business. All our data lives in one place and is easy to use. Over 90% of day-to-day data-driven decisions are supported through self-serve analytics in Looker, giving analysts the headspace to focus on solving high-impact business problems.

Our Credit Platform squad builds the shared infrastructure that powers lending decisioning across Monzo. We develop the core credit valuation (NPV) infrastructure, decisioning capabilities and data foundations that enable our Product Credit teams to develop, evaluate and deploy lending strategies across products and markets. As we scale internationally, our platform is at the heart of delivering consistent, scalable credit capabilities globally. You'll lead a team of five Credit Analysts, shaping the evolution of our platform, pushing the boundaries to unlock the next generation of lending capabilities and drive efficiencies.

Join a team where your ideas can rapidly transform into reality, leveraging our cutting-edge technology and agile ways of working. Credit Platform is a cross-functional squad bringing together Credit, Product, Engineering and Data expertise to build shared capabilities that power Borrowing across Monzo. 

How you’ll contribute:
• Shape our Credit Platform: Define the roadmap for Monzo's Credit Platform, evolving the shared infrastructure that enables Product Credit teams to develop, evaluate and deploy lending strategies across our retail and business lending products in the UK and new global markets.
• Build Credit Valuation Infrastructure: Lead the evolution of the infrastructure that supports Monzo's credit valuation capabilities, including our NPV modelling framework, ensuring it is scalable, reliable and enables Product Credit teams to optimise lending economics.
• Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team: Hire, coach and develop a high-performing team of Credit Analysts, fostering a culture of technical excellence, ownership and continuous improvement while delivering platform capabilities with broad organisational impact.
• Partner Across Monzo: Work closely with Credit, Engineering, Product, Machine Learning, Data and Risk teams to build platform capabilities that accelerate experimentation, simplify strategy deployment and improve the speed and quality of credit decisioning.
• Influence Through Technical Leadership: Represent the Credit Platform across Monzo, translating complex technical concepts into clear recommendations for senior leaders and helping shape the future direction of our lending platform.

• You are a technical and strategic credit leader with extensive experience in unsecured lending.
• You understand lending economics inside out, with deep experience in NPV modelling and the infrastructure and frameworks that enable effective credit decisioning
• You are highly motivated by fast-paced environments, enjoy ambiguity, designing frameworks from scratch, and delivering meaningful change.
• You are an exceptional cross-functional leader who thrives when partnering with Engineering, Product, Risk, Machine Learning and Credit teams to deliver shared platform capabilities.
• You have a track record of leading and developing analytical talent, and you are excited by the prospect of leading a high-impact team.
• You have strong analytical and data capabilities backed up by technical coding skills (SQL is a must-have; Python and Looker experience is a plus).

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

 

📍London, Cardiff or Distributed | 💰 Dependant on experience + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits | Hear from the team 

⭐Our Tax team

We're looking for an experienced, hands-on and enthusiastic Senior Director of Global Tax to lead the Global Tax team at Monzo, and our wider finance team.

You’ll be leading our growing Tax team of 10+ individuals, and will be reporting into the Group Financial Controller (with a close partnership with the MBL Chief Financial Officer and wider Executive team).

A large part of the role involves advising on the tax implications of all new business developments, ensuring we’re both set up for compliance and optimised wherever possible and appropriate. Given the stage Monzo is currently at in its growth journey, these will be many and wide ranging, from customer products to treasury strategies, group reorgs to mobility proposals, systems implementations to international expansion.

🔑 Key responsibilities of the role...
• Global tax strategy: Defining how Monzo approaches tax across the UK, Europe, and future markets. You will set our tax risk appetite and prepare reporting for our Audit and Risk Committee.
• International expansion: Structuring cross-border expansion across Europe and future regions, advising on market-entry structures, permanent establishment risks, and local compliance.
• Transfer pricing: Establishing, documenting, and defending our global transfer pricing strategy and intragroup financing arrangements.
• Total tax ownership: Overseeing group Direct Tax, Indirect Tax (VAT), Employment Tax, Transfer Pricing, and Operational Customer Taxes across all locations.
• Tax authority relationships: Acting as the primary liaison with HMRC and international tax authorities, proactively managing tax audits, and overseeing statutory regimes including Senior Accounting Officer compliance.
• Product and commercial advisory: Working directly with product managers, engineers, and treasury to understand what they want to build (from savings pots to complex lending products) and ensuring the tax treatment is clear from day one.
• Leading the team: Mentoring and leading our tax team, fostering a culture of technical excellence, autonomy, and commercial focus.
• AI and automation: Designing a tech-enabled tax operating model that embeds AI, workflow tools, and automation across our compliance, reconciliations, and contract reviews; scaling our output as volumes grow while keeping the team focused on high-judgement strategic work.

🤩We’d love to hear from you if...
• You’re a qualified tax professional or accountant (CTA, ACA, ACCA, ADIT, or international equivalent).
• You’ve led an in-house tax team at scale, ideally within banking, fintech, or a regulated multinational.
• You’re an empathetic, effective people leader with a strong track record of coaching individuals and fostering a positive, high-performing environment.
• You bring practical experience with cross-border tax issues, international structuring, and transfer pricing.
• You understand operational and customer taxes common to financial services (such as FATCA/CRS, withholding taxes, and interest reporting).
• You are excited by modern technology, data, and AI, with a clear view on how tools can automate workflows, reduce human error, and modernise routine tax tasks.
• You can explain complex tax positions to non-tax stakeholders, including product leads, commercial teams, and auditors.
• You’re comfortable with ambiguity: we move fast, build things that haven't been built before, and you’ll frequently make calls without a standard blueprint.
• What we’re doing at Monzo excites you!

🙌 What’s in it for you

💰 Dependant on experience + Incentive Awards tied to your performance

📍This role can be based in our London or Cardiff offices. We're also open to distributed working within the UK (with the expectation of some travel to our London office).

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team. 

📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.

🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup. 

➕ Plus lots more! Read our full list of benefits.

Our average process takes around 4 - 5 weeks but we will always work around your availability.

About the Role 

This role is for a Senior Engineering Manager where you’ll be a manager of managers. You will be leading across multiple teams in an org of around 20-30 people. We’re expanding and your role as the Senior EM will be to grow and build new squads as needed. Your direct reports will include Tech Leads, Senior Engineers and 2-3 Engineering Managers.

Senior Engineering Managers at Monzo are part of cross-functional, autonomous teams and groups. Our teams are mission driven, and typically include Product Managers, backend, web and mobile engineers as well as data scientists, designers and subject matter experts relevant to that mission. Teams are organised into groups, and then collectives - we aim to keep our line management structure as shallow as possible, and for teams to directly own decision making relevant to their work.

Senior Engineering Managers are accountable for the technical and delivery outcomes for their area - that means supporting and developing best in class engineering talent, as well as creating an inclusive team environment for people to do their best work. You’ll be responsible for structuring, organising, supporting and challenging your team to deliver on their mission.

You can read more on the expectations of Senior Engineering Managers in our Progression Framework.

Is this role right for you?

While this is not a role which requires hands-on-coding, we are looking for an experienced manager who has a strong technical and delivery background and has worked as a software engineer in previous roles.

We recognise that Senior Engineering Managers lead in different ways, we’re looking for someone who is adept at:
• Delivery and Execution: Enjoys taking accountability for delivery across your squad(s), collaborating with the Technical Lead and Product Manager.
• Engineering and Operational Excellence: Actively fosters a high bar for engineering excellence within your teams. You’re accountable for the technical outcomes your teams deliver alongside individual engineer performance and growth, so holding a high bar (and clearly articulating your expectations) is key.
• People Leadership: Has experience directly managing at least 2-3 Engineering Managers and leading orgs of around ~20 engineers. You can support, coach and develop them through their career with regular 1:1s and continuous feedback.
• Technical Influence: Partners with senior engineers to drive technical initiatives that raise the bar for our engineering practices.
• Stakeholder Relationships: Builds strong stakeholder relationships with other teams, and creates a focus space for engineers to do their best work.
• Organisational Wide Impact: Collaborates with the wider engineering organisation to contribute to company-wide best managerial and technical practices and standards.

We consider your application across all open EM roles at Monzo independent of which role you've applied for, so if you've recently applied to a similar role at Monzo and have been unsuccessful, please wait 6 months before applying again.

How we work 💻:

Locations Flexible Working : 

Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. 

We value meeting in person but there’s no pressure to come into the office, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs. ✨

Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches treat Thursdays 🍽️. Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.

Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life.

At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance. 

You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency. 🕒✨

Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼

The interview process:

After an initial informal recruiter call you go through two main stages
• Initial Call (1 hour) You'll meet with one of our Senior Engineering Managers or Engineering Directors. They'll ask you about your previous experience, in particular people leadership, product delivery and technical leadership. They’ll ask example based questions (‘Tell me about a time when…’)
• Loop Stage (3 hours 30 mins) The Loop stage consists of 3 x 60 min interviews that take place over 1-2 days (depending on your availability) and one 30 minute reverse interview (more details below).

The Loop is one stage and the interviews in this stage are:

- Team and Org Management (1 hour)
An example based interview with 1-2 of our engineering leaders. They’re interested to hear examples from your previous experience on the teams you’ve led, how you’ve shaped and partnered with product, and the impact you had.

- System Design (1 hour)
You'll partner with a Staff or Principal Engineer on a technical whiteboarding exercise.

- Behavioural (1 hour)
Similar to Team and Org Management, this is an example based interview with 1-2 Engineering Leaders. This interview focuses on your people leadership style and core behaviours as an Engineering Manager.

- Chat with an Engineering Leader (30 mins)
At Monzo, we believe interviews are a two-way street. This will be your opportunity to ask us any questions about Monzo, engineering leadership or our teams – whatever’s on your mind. 

All things going well, you'll have completed the hiring process 🚀

Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability. You’ll have the chance to speak to our recruitment team throughout the process.

📍London/Cardiff/UK Remote | 💰£108,700 - £140,000 + equity + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits ✨

Our Financial Crime Fraud Collective ⭐

We’re all about building trust and keeping our community safe while helping Monzo grow. The Financial Crime Fraud Collective is at the heart of this work. As a Senior Fraud Risk Manager, you’ll lead the charge in keeping fraudsters at bay so our customers can bank with total confidence!

You’ll get to work across current accounts, business banking, international accounts, and more. While you’ll be managing people and programs, you should also be excited to roll up your sleeves and get hands-on.

We need a crack team of crime fighters to help us stay one step ahead as we continue to grow. 

🔑 You’ll play a key role by...

Helping to lead our fast-growing global Fraud Disputes Risk team and work alongside leaders across our cross-functional Fraud Squads. We’re looking for a proactive, collaborative leader who really knows fraud risk management inside and out - spanning several of our authorised fraud, unauthorised fraud, first-party fraud, and disputes specialisms

You’ll build great relationships with our Product, Engineering, Data, and Operations teams to design smooth, effective fraud controls, investigation processes, and reporting. You’ll also champion a positive team culture and make sure key fraud initiatives stay on track.

Your Core Focus Areas include:
• Fraud Strategy Operational Execution: Join squad leadership to turn our big-picture fraud vision into practical roadmaps for our UK and EU Banks. You’ll strike the perfect balance between smart protection controls and a seamless customer experience.
• Control Framework Fraud SME: Be our go-to expert on fraud typologies and prevention tools, overseeing end-to-end design and rollout of strong controls.
• Threat Intelligence Performance Analytics: Embed data and threat monitoring to catch new fraud trends early, turning insights into quick control improvements.
• Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Ops to keep initiatives aligned and moving forward.
• People Leadership Capability Building: Coach, mentor, and grow a fantastic fraud risk team while supporting everyone’s personal and professional development.

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…
• You have strong experience leading fraud strategy and risk teams, ideally in a fast-moving, regulated environment.
• You know UK EU fraud regulations inside out.
• You’re skilled at building tech-driven fraud strategies that scale across operations.
• You have a proven track record of delivering end-to-end projects and large-scale change programs.
• You stay plugged into industry trends and can quickly respond to new fraud risks.

Now, we’re redesigning how customer operations work by bringing together intelligent automation, human expertise and world-class technology.

We’re looking for a Staff Technical Program Manager to lead complex company wide programmes driven by the Operations collective. You’ll turn ambitious ideas into clear plans, bring a large and varied group of partners with you and help teams deliver lasting change.

This role is about more than keeping work on track. You’ll shape how we work across the collective, influence domain and collective leaders across Monzo, connect technical delivery to operational outcomes and make sure change works for the people who use it every day.

What you’ll do

Lead programmes that cut through all operational domains at Monzo

You’ll lead high-impact programmes from strategy through to measurable outcomes. These may cover AI-powered customer support, tools that help our Customer Operations teams, or the platforms and processes behind millions of operational decisions.

Build strong partnerships at every level

You’ll work with a large and varied group of partners. This could include frontline Operations teams, subject matter experts, product and engineering teams, risk and compliance partners, senior leaders and executives.

Drive change, not just delivery

You’ll help the whole collective adopt new ways of working. You’ll understand how changes affect people, processes and technology, then build that into the programme from the start.

Key

Responsibilities:
• Lead end-to-end planning and execution of major product or platform programs that cross multiple teams and markets
• Manage cross-collective programmes:
• Define programme roadmaps and milestones, set priorities, manage trade-offs, identify and manage the critical path and risks, ensure alignment with the business goals and ambition

• Drive effective decision making to remove blockers

• You can work effectively with a diverse range of people and working styles to get stuff done, and are able to thoughtfully and constructively challenge and influence the people you work with
• You can make complex work easy to understand without losing the important detail
• You understand how functionality comes together (across products and platforms) to deliver value for users, and can proactively identify and mitigate delivery risks, and can propose and drive a technical solution
• You are comfortable personally diving deep into the data to make good decisions in complex situations where there’s often no “right answer”
• You can influence across teams even when you don’t manage them directly and can influence senior leaders, resolve disagreement and build alignment without relying on authority.
• You’ve driven organisation-wide change and can show how you supported adoption, not only delivery

You don’t need to match every point. If you’re excited by the role and believe you could have an impact, we’d love to hear from you.

What makes this role different

Most companies are adding AI to existing support processes. We’re redesigning the operating model itself.

You’ll help shape how intelligent automation and human expertise work together in a highly regulated environment. The programmes you lead will affect how teams across Operations work and how millions of customers get help.

You’ll have the scope to influence strategy, the responsibility to turn it into action and the chance to build ways of working that scale.

Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles.

2010. • Supporting the ongoing development and maintenance of our Operational Risk Management Framework (ORMF), policies, standards and associated ICT, Security and Resilience policies and risk appetite metrics.
• Co-ordinating second line assurance reviews and risk deep dives into critical operational and technology areas, providing actionable recommendations and insights.

jobs.title: Product Manager / Director, Institutional Liquidity & Growth
jobs.description:
OKX will be prioritising applicants who have a current right to work in Hong Kong, and do not require OKX's sponsorship of a visa.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

 

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. 

 

Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

 

About The Opportunity

We are looking for a Senior Institutional Liquidity Product Manager to own the management and improvement of liquidity across OKX's spot, margin, futures, perpetual swap and options markets.

You will work closely with institutional traders, market makers, HFT firms and quantitative teams to identify liquidity gaps and develop market-structure, product and commercial solutions that improve execution quality and market competitiveness.

This is a strategic and hands-on role combining market microstructure expertise, quantitative analysis, product delivery and commercial ownership. You will partner with Quant, Data, Engineering, Risk, Relationship Managers , Operations and external liquidity providers to turn order-book data and client trading behaviour into measurable improvements in spread, depth, slippage, trading volume, market share and resilience during stressed markets.

What You’ll Be Doing 

Liquidity Strategy, Analytics and Delivery
• Analyse institutional client needs, market-maker and HFT trading behaviour, market trends, competitor liquidity, fee structures, order types and liquidity programmes to identify opportunities for differentiation.
• Own the liquidity product roadmap across spot, margin, futures, perpetual swaps and options, including monitoring capabilities, order types, market structure, maker protection and liquidity improvement initiatives.
• Translate quantitative analysis and institutional trading requirements into clear product specifications and solutions. Work closely with Quant, Data, Engineering, Matching Engine, Risk and Relationship managers teams to deliver scalable solutions from problem definition through launch.
• Define targets, baselines, guardrails and post-launch measurement for each liquidity initiative. Use controlled or phased rollouts where appropriate, evaluate causal impact and ROI, and continuously adjust the roadmap based on data and client feedback.

Institutional and Market Maker Engagement
• Understand participants' market-making, hedging, arbitrage, inventory-risk and latency-sensitive strategies, and translate these needs into product and programme requirements.
• Partner with Institutional Relationship Management teams to onboard and engage liquidity providers, communicate product and programme changes, gather structured feedback and improve participation in priority markets.

What We Look For In You
• Proven experience in liquidity management, electronic trading or market structure within a crypto or traditional exchange, market maker, HFT firm, proprietary trading firm, quantitative fund or institutional trading platform.
• Strong understanding of institutional and HFT trading strategies, including market making, cross-venue arbitrage, price discovery, hedging, inventory and risk management, adverse selection, toxic flow and latency-sensitive execution.
• A quantitative background in mathematics, statistics, computer science, financial engineering or a related field is strongly preferred.
• Hands-on ability with SQL and Python, with experience analysing large-scale order-book, order and trade data. Experience with Level 2 or Level 3 market data is highly valued.
• Deep knowledge of market microstructure, order books, matching, tick size, maker/taker economics, order types, execution quality and liquidity dynamics across spot and derivatives.
• Front-to-back knowledge of crypto, FX, equities, fixed income or listed derivatives, with the ability to apply that knowledge to new products and market structures.
• Strong product execution and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to drive cross-functional delivery across Quant, Data, Engineering, Risk, Finance, Sales and Operations from problem definition to measurable outcome.
• Able to communicate credibly with traders, quants, engineers, senior executives and external partners.
• Fluent in English and Mandarin.
 

Perks Benefits
• Competitive total compensation package
• L D programs and education subsidy for employees' growth and development
• Various team building programs and company events
• Wellness and meal allowances
• Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants
• More that we love to tell you along the process!

Please note that Hong Kong is a group-level service hub, and OKX does not carry on a business of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong.

This is a hands-on, sourcing-first role focused on building and owning talent pipelines across the US, LATAM, and APAC — with the heaviest emphasis on APAC, where our fastest hiring growth is happening and where deep market knowledge is hardest to buy.

You will spend the majority of your time proactively identifying, engaging, and converting passive talent — not processing inbound applications. You will map markets, build long-term talent communities, and become the person hiring managers come to when they need to know who’s out there. If you are energized by outreach that actually lands, by knowing a market better than anyone else in the room, and by building pipelines before the req even opens, this role is for you.

What You’ll Be Doing
• Proactive Sourcing (Core Focus): Own top-of-funnel sourcing across US, LATAM, and APAC. Build and execute multi-channel sourcing strategies using LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean and X-ray search, GitHub, Behance, Dribbble, Telegram, Discord, WeChat, Maimai, BOSS Zhipin, referrals, alumni networks, and crypto-native communities.
• APAC Pipeline Building: Serve as the sourcing engine for APAC hiring. Develop deep talent maps across key hubs — Singapore, Hong Kong, mainland China, Japan, Malaysia, Australia, and India — and build region-specific outreach strategies that account for local platforms, languages, notice periods, and compensation norms.
• Talent Mapping Market Intelligence: Produce competitor org maps, talent availability reports, and compensation benchmarks by region. Translate market data into practical guidance that shapes role scoping, level calibration, and hiring plans.
• Candidate Engagement Conversion: Write and test outreach that gets replies. Own the candidate experience from first touch through handoff, running screens that assess motivation, mobility, and fit while keeping candidates warm through long hiring cycles.
• Pipeline Ownership Nurture: Build and maintain evergreen pipelines and talent communities for recurring and hard-to-fill roles. Keep silver-medalist and passive-candidate pools active so we are never starting from zero when a req opens.
• Stakeholder Partnership: Partner with recruiters, hiring managers, and regional HR teams across time zones. Run intake and calibration sessions, share pipeline reviews, and set realistic expectations grounded in market reality.
• Sourcing Data Reporting: Track and report on sourcing funnel metrics — outreach volume, response rate, screen-to-submit, submit-to-onsite, and pipeline health by region. Use the data to redirect effort toward the channels that convert.
• Employer Brand in Market: Represent OKX to passive talent. Support regional recruiting events, meetups, and community engagement, and help position OKX as the destination employer in crypto across every market you cover.

What We Look For In You
• 3+ years of full-lifecycle recruiting or dedicated sourcing experience, with a demonstrable track record of building pipelines from scratch rather than working inbound applicant flow.

jobs.title: Director of Corporate Development
jobs.location: Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY
jobs.description:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

Robinhood is looking for a Director of Corporate Development to help accelerate our roadmap by identifying, vetting, and executing acquisitions, strategic investments, and other transactions. In this role, you will develop a deep understanding of Robinhood's strategic priorities and market landscape, and partner with GMs and senior leadership to identify high-potential opportunities across our existing and future product verticals and geographies. You will help build Robinhood's network of founders, investors, and bankers, and develop relationships that may lead to acquisitions or strategic investments.

You will work closely with deal sponsors and cross-functional leaders across Robinhood on all aspects of M A, including business case construction, valuation analysis, deal structuring, negotiation, due diligence, execution, and post-close integration. You will present opportunities to company leadership and the Board of Directors, facilitate key decisions, and provide post-acquisition performance updates. The ideal candidate is strategic, relationship-oriented, analytical, and results-oriented, and thrives at a public company that still operates like a startup.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA or New York, NY offices, with in-person attendance expected 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. 

What you’ll do
• Analyze Robinhood's strategic landscape, gather competitive and industry intelligence, and develop the business case and rationale for key M A opportunities, advocating for them internally.
• Manage transactions end to end, including sourcing, valuation, negotiation, diligence, and closing, and partner with integration teams to deliver a seamless post-close transition.
• Lead deal evaluation meetings and drive decision-making with objectivity, diplomacy, and effectiveness.
• Cultivate relationships with founders, venture capital firms, and investment banks to build a proactive pipeline of future acquisitions and strategic investments.
• Collaborate with business sponsors and leaders across Legal, Finance, Compliance, Product, and Engineering to build clear business and financial cases and execute deals.
• Present opportunities and recommendations to senior leadership and the Board of Directors, and report on post-acquisition performance against the original deal thesis.
• Help build scalable processes, playbooks, and best practices that shape the operating system of Robinhood's Corporate Development team.

What you bring
• 10+ years of experience in corporate development, investment banking, venture capital, private equity, or other investing roles, ideally within fintech, financial services, or consumer technology.
• Track record of sourcing, leading, and closing complex technology acquisitions or strategic investments, ideally including in-house corporate development experience.
• Exceptional analytical skills, including company valuation, financial modeling, and structured problem solving.
• Ability to reason from first principles, using data and analysis to draw sound conclusions, with a bias toward action: analyze fast, decide, and either move forward or move on.
• Strong interpersonal skills and a track record of building strong working relationships with founders, investors, bankers, and executives.
• Executive presence and outstanding written and verbal communication, including experience presenting to senior leadership and boards.
• Resourceful, persistent, and able to thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
• Familiarity with Robinhood and our industry. You enjoy managing your money on your phone!

What we offer
• Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career.
• Performance-driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching.
• Best-in-class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents.
• Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more.
• Employer-paid life disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits.
• Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
• Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager, Checking & Savings
jobs.description:
Employee Applicant Privacy Notice

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.

We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.

The role

We're seeking an analytical, execution-oriented Product Marketing Manager to drive engagement and retention marketing for SoFi Checking and Savings, the foundation of our deposits business and our largest driver of member growth. This role focuses on our existing member base: deepening the relationships we already have, growing and retaining balances and direct deposits, and bringing dormant accounts back to life.

Your core KPIs will be deposits and direct deposits, with a specific focus on growing and retaining balances across our existing member base. You'll own the promotions and offers that ladder to those goals, working directly with the technical teams that build and implement them. You'll work alongside our Lifecycle Marketing team on engagement and retention campaigns, and partner closely with product and engineering on product-led experiments that turn accounts into everyday banking habits. This includes driving ongoing account utilization as well as reducing churn and reactivating dormant members.

Analytical rigor is central to this role. Segmentation, audience development, and offer testing are primary levers for driving deposit and direct deposit growth, and we're looking for someone with the quantitative depth to identify opportunities within the member base and the judgment to prioritize the ones worth pursuing.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with a meaningful piece of the business to drive. You'll be the day-to-day marketing owner of this segment of our business, working in close partnership with the Product Marketing lead for Checking Savings. You'll collaborate with product, engineering, data science, lifecycle, channel owners, our in-house creative studio, finance, and compliance.

What you’ll do:
• Drive day-to-day engagement and retention marketing for Checking Savings, with core KPIs on deposits and direct deposits across our existing member base
• Grow and retain balances and direct deposit relationships by identifying the highest-leverage member segments, sizing the opportunity, and building the plan to move them
• Own the promotions, sweepstakes, and offers tied to your KPIs, from offer construction and setup through launch, compliance review, and post-campaign analysis, working directly with the technical teams that build and implement them
• Develop sophisticated segmentation and testing programs, designing audience and offer tests that identify and unlock incremental value across the member base
• Partner closely with Lifecycle Marketing to design, launch, and optimize engagement and retention campaigns across email, push, in-app, and other owned channels
• Work with product and engineering on product-led experiments: in-product prompts, feature surfacing, and flows that drive direct deposit and balance growth among established members
• Reduce churn and reactivate dormant members through member segmentation, targeted offers, and disciplined testing
• Build the measurement plan and own the readout: define success up front, read results with an eye toward incrementality, and turn findings into concrete recommendations for the next cycle

What you’ll need:
• 4+ years of product marketing, growth marketing, lifecycle marketing, or closely related experience, preferably in fintech, banking, or another regulated consumer category
• Analytical Thinking: Strong quantitative skills and comfort in spreadsheets and Business Intelligence tools. You can build a segmentation, run a cohort or retention analysis, size an opportunity, read a test result, and clearly explain what happened and why
• Strategic Thinking: Ability to connect day-to-day execution to business outcomes, prioritize where it matters, and make a reasoned case for a recommendation
• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Proven experience working closely with cross-functional teams, especially Product and technical/engineering partners. You can translate marketing needs into requirements a technical team can build against
• Experimentation: Experience designing and running tests in campaigns, in product, or both and distilling results into insights others can act on
• Project Management: Ability to manage multiple concurrent campaigns, dependencies, and deadlines without losing the details
• Communication: Write clearly and concisely; can brief a creative team and present a readout to partners with equal ease
• Initiative Bias for Action: Eagerness to roll up your sleeves to get things done (even the unglamorous things)
• Bachelor's degree required

Nice to have:
• Experience marketing banking or deposit products, particularly around direct deposit or balance growth
• Experience with segmentation and audience targeting against a large customer base
• Experience building and running promotions, sweepstakes, or offer and bonus mechanics
• Working familiarity with SQL and Business Intelligence tools such as Tableau
• Experience operating in a regulated environment alongside legal and compliance partners

Compensation and Benefits

The base pay range for this role is listed below. Final base pay offer will be determined based on individual factors such as the candidate’s experience, skills, and location. 

 

To view all of our comprehensive and competitive benefits, visit our Benefits at SoFi page!

Head of Financial Crime Operations Transformation (6 Month Fixed Term Contract)

Location: Southampton, Cardiff & Manchester

Reporting to: Director of Specialist Banking Operations

Closing date: Friday, 17th November at 5pm

About Starling 

At Starling, we are on a mission to provide people with a fairer, smarter, and more human alternative to traditional banks. We are building a leading digital bank, driven by fast technology, fair service, and honest values. Our vision is to create a banking industry that serves everyone, which we accomplish by developing best-in-class proprietary technology, offering an exceptional customer experience, and establishing a strong, sustainable business.

Our five core values – Listen, Keep It Simple, Do The Right Thing, Own It, and Aim for Greatness – are at the heart of everything we do, guiding our strategy and shaping our culture. We're a branchless, largely paperless bank, committed to responsible banking, sustainability, and fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive.

Working Hours: You will work a 37.5 hour week, with shifts between 9am - 5:30pm Monday - Friday.

Hybrid working: All Starling colleagues spend a minimum of 10 days per month in the office, with flexibility to work the rest from home. You will also be expected to travel to other office locations depending on business needs.

The Opportunity:

The Head of Financial Crime Operations Transformation holds accountability for Starling Bank’s financial crime interim operational delivery and transformation across multiple teams, including Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Counter-Terrorist Financing (CTF), Customer Due Diligence (CDD/EDD).

As an Experienced People Leader (PL6) in the First Line of Defence, this role leads a team of senior professionals and team managers, influences the transformation of the strategic direction and ensures robust governance aligned with departmental strategy and the Bank's Risk Appetite.

What You'll Do:

AML, CTF & Due Diligence Operations
• Oversee the Operations transformation and operational delivery for AML, CTF, CDD, and EDD across customer segments in line with agreed SLAs.
• Ensure alert handling and case reviews are responded to in a high-quality, timely manner, maintaining resourcing to handle workload demand and manage operational KPIs, OKRs, and KRIs.
• Lead the continuous improvement of the control environment to focus teams on taking a risk-based approach and reducing false-positive alerts.
• Maintain awareness of specific financial crime typologies unique to SME customers and partner closely with SME leadership and commercial teams to build, develop, and align financial crime capabilities and operating models specifically for SME customers.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management
• Partner effectively across 2nd Line Risk, Compliance, Product, Engineering, and Data to embed new initiatives and regulatory updates

Operational Leadership & Efficiency
• Proactively identify opportunities to optimise processes, drive continuous improvements, and improve customer outcomes across Financial Crime Operations.
• Deliver consistent communication across teams and engage with operational managers to create an empowered problem-solving culture

Functional Governance
• Navigate complex organisational challenges, including change management, and resolve significant team or functional conflicts while making risk decisions with departmental impact.

What You'll Bring:
• Deep subject matter expertise in UK Financial Crime regulatory guidelines, MLRs, JMLSG, PEPs, and Sanctions.
• Technical competency in understanding models, data, MI, statistical analysis, and operational workflows.
• Proven track record of managing and transforming financial crime operations and risk frameworks within regulated banking.

Behaviours & Competencies:
• Accountable, resilient, and customer-focused leadership style that role models Starling Group values and makes difficult decisions with full transparency.
• Analytical mindset with the ability to champion simplicity across functions, encourage external input and disruptive thinking, and raise the bar for strategic performance.
• Excellent communication and listening skills, creating a safe environment to share feedback, surface issues, and resolve conflicting requirements across functions.

Why Join Starling?
• Make an Impact: Work on projects that directly shape the future of banking and improve the financial lives of our customers. Starling is technology-led, and you'll have the freedom to accomplish your goals in innovative ways.
• Culture of Excellence: Be part of a collaborative, empowered, and forward-thinking team. We encourage experimentation, ownership, and a relentless focus on "doing the right thing.”
• Growth and Development: We are committed to your professional growth, offering opportunities to learn new technologies, take on new challenges, and own interesting things from day one.
• A Bank That Cares: We're a Living Wage employer, committed to flexible working, and dedicated to creating a fair, open, and safe working environment with compassion and inclusion at its core.
• Comprehensive

Benefits:

We offer a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package, including:
• Company-enhanced salary sacrifice pension scheme (7% employer contribution)
• Private Medical Insurance with Vitality including mental health support and cancer care. Partner benefits include discounts with Waitrose, Mr&Mrs Smith and Peloton.
• 25 days holiday (plus take your public holiday allowance whenever works best for you)
• An extra day’s holiday for your birthday
• Life Insurance at 4x your salary.
• 16 hours of paid volunteering time a year.
• Ability to buy or sell annual leave.
• Generous family-friendly policies.
• Annual leave is increased with length of service, and you can choose to buy or sell up to five extra days off
• Incentivised refer a friend scheme
• Perkbox membership giving access to retail discounts, a wellness platform for physical and mental health, and weekly free and boosted perks
• Access to initiatives like Cycle to Work, Salary Sacrificed Gym partnerships and Electric Vehicle (EV) leasingOur Commitment to Equality

Starling is an equal opportunity employer, and we’re proud of our ongoing efforts to foster diversity & inclusion in the workplace. Individuals seeking employment at Starling Bank are considered without regard to race, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, medical condition, ancestry, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. When you provide us with this information, you are doing so at your own consent, with full knowledge that we will process this personal data in accordance with our Privacy Notice. By submitting your application, you agree that Starling Bank will collect your personal data for recruiting and related purposes. Our Privacy Notice explains what personal information we will process, where we will process your personal information, its purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over our use of your personal information.

We use AI tools to support various parts of our recruitment process, helping our team manage applications and assessments more efficiently. These tools are strictly used for support and do not replace human judgment with all final hiring decisions being made by our team. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please reach out to us.

jobs.title: Junior Technical Project Manager - Engine by Starling
jobs.description:
At Engine by Starling, we are on a mission to find and work with leading banks all around the world who have the ambition to build rapid growth businesses, on our technology. 

Engine is Starling's software-as-a-service (SaaS) business, the technology that was built to power Starling Bank, and a year ago we split out as a separate business. 

Starling Bank has seen exceptional growth and success, and a large part of that is down to the fact that we have built our own modern technology from the ground up. The Engine technology platform is now available to banks and financial institutions all around the world, enabling them to benefit from the innovative digital features, and efficient back-office processes that has helped achieve Starling's success.

Our people are at the very heart of Engine and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment that is all about building things, creating new stuff, and disruptive technology that keeps us on the cutting edge of fintech. We operate a flat structure to empower you to make decisions regardless of what your primary responsibilities may be, innovation and collaboration will be at the core of everything you do. Help is never far away in our open culture, you will find support in your team and from across the business, we are in this together!

The way to thrive and shine within Engine is to be a self-driven individual and be able to take full ownership of everything around you: From building things, designing, and discovering to sharing knowledge with your colleagues and making sure all processes are efficient and productive to deliver the best possible results for our customers. jobs.title: Senior Legal Counsel, Governance & Company Secretarial
jobs.description:
Job description

You will serve as the principal governance advisor and strategic partner to the Boards, local management and executive committees of Wise’s Belgian and Dutch entities and their branches, which operate under the supervision of the National Bank of Belgium (NBB) and the De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) respectively. You will help ensure our corporate governance and operational resilience continue to meet the highest standards of governance discipline.

In this high-impact role, you will be responsible for sustaining and enhancing our subsidiary governance framework, supporting operational resilience, and navigating complex regulatory environments. You will act as the key liaison between local management and subsidiary Boards and the Group, ensuring that governance is not just a process, but a strategic enabler of our global scale-up.

You will advise the subsidiary Boards and executive committees directly and operate with a high degree of autonomy and mandate across multiple regulated entities and two regulators.

What you’ll do: Provide a full governance and company secretarial service to the relevant Wise entities. This includes:
• Regulatory and legal advisory: Act as trusted legal advisor to the Boards and local management on regulations affecting Wise’s European entities - including NBB and DNB supervisory expectations, and fit-and-proper and governance requirements. Advise on regulatory authorisations, variations and notifications, support supervisory engagement and regulatory correspondence, and translate EU and Belgian/Dutch regulatory change into practical board-level action. Provide independent legal judgment on the regulatory dimensions of new products, licences and group restructurings.
• Corporate governance ownership: Act as the primary governance advisor for multiple complex and regulated subsidiaries. Lead the end-to-end lifecycle of board and executive committee management, including agenda setting, driving high quality reporting and meeting minutes, tracking actions and maintaining statutory records.
• Entity governance and regulatory compliance: Managing the annual board calendars to secure timely approvals, renewals, compliance attestations, statutory filings, and mandatory regulatory evaluations. Monitor changes in the legislative and regulatory landscape, advising the Board and senior management on the impact of new requirements and best practices.
• Stakeholder management: build and maintain strong, credible working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including executives, non-executive directors and external service providers. Influence and constructively challenge senior decision-makers - including demanding and strongly-held personalities - presenting complex governance issues clearly and steering them towards pragmatic solutions that balance growth objectives with regulatory expectations.
• Governance maturity: Drive the maturity of our subsidiary governance as we expand through continuous process improvement and enhancing governance frameworks that adapt to a rapidly growing, global subsidiary group.

jobs.title: Group Regulatory Affairs Lead
jobs.description:
As a Regulatory Affairs Lead, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and executing a new global capability within the Group Core Compliance function. Today, Wise holds over 80 regulatory licences across the UK, Europe, North America, APAC, MEA and LATAM. To sustain our global growth and further elevate our regulatory relationship management, we are establishing a dedicated, centralized Regulatory Affairs function.

Reporting to the Director of Group Core Compliance, you will serve as the single source of truth for the status and strategic trajectory of our regulatory relationships globally. You will work closely with regional Compliance Officers, Risk, Legal, Government Relations and Banking & Expansion teams to establish a centralized view of our global regulatory priorities, providing clear visibility into how these are managed across markets and proactively identifying and resolving any resulting intra-group conflicts or competing interests.

We are looking for a strong stakeholder manager and problem solver who thrives on turning ambiguity into scalable structure. You will bridge the gap between regional Compliance Officers, Group executive leadership, and functional partners (Legal, Risk, Banking & Expansion, Government Relations, Product), ensuring Wise engages with supervisors around the world with one aligned and proactive voice.

 

Your Mission:
• Global Relationship Oversight: Establish enterprise-wide visibility over Wise’s supervisory footprint. Maintain a real-time overview of regional regulatory owners, active supervisory touchpoints, open inquiries, inspections, and regulatory commitments (including remediations) across all operating entities.
• Regulatory Relationship Strategy: In collaboration with regional Compliance Officers and functional partners, anticipate supervisory shifts, thematic review trends, and administrative changes in key markets. Help leadership formulate proactive engagement strategies before risks materialize.
• Regulatory Information Governance: Own the framework for tracking all material regulatory correspondence, bilateral engagements, information requests (RFIs), and regulatory notifications. Eliminate regional blind spots to ensure Wise speaks to supervisors globally with a unified narrative. Translate complex initiatives into clear, consistent external regulatory communications.
• Executive Strategic Reporting: Design data-driven systems that will produce Management Information (MI) for the Director of Group Compliance, executive leadership, Boards and Risk Committees. Strategic reporting will clearly articulate relationship health, emerging issues, and supervisory trends. Translate complex regulatory interactions into actionable reports and advice that can be used to make decisions quickly.
• Supervisory Read-Across & Lessons Learned: Partner with regional Compliance Officers and Product Compliance to evaluate material supervisory inquiries, examination findings, and enforcement precedents across jurisdictions. Ensure critical lessons learned are systematically cascaded to protect parallel licenses.
• Cross-Functional Information Sharing: Drive the agenda and operational cadence for cross-functional information sharing to align on high-impact supervisory developments, market intelligence, and collective remediation without duplicating formal committee governance - exercising strict discretion around confidential topics.
• Incident Response: Act as an advisor for Core Compliance during complex, regulatory incidents, ensuring aligned briefing for regional Compliance Officers, prompt factual verification, and coordinated global regulatory messaging across impacted jurisdictions.

This role will give you the opportunity to:
• Build a function: Take a developing concept and design the global operating model, engagement standards, and data from scratch.
• Influence executive strategy: Shape how leadership and regional Compliance Officers navigate key regulatory engagements and evolving multi-supervisor coalitions.
• Gain unmatched global breadth: Work across a diverse regulatory landscape - collaborating daily with teams across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific, LATAM and MEA.
• Champion a data-driven approach: Move regulatory relations beyond traditional narrative memos by embedding quantitative metrics and structured trend analytics into our supervisory governance.

A bit

about you:
• Proven Track Record: Significant experience (10+ years) in Regulatory Affairs and Relations or Compliance within a financial institution or regulatory authority.
• Supervisory Expertise: In-depth understanding of how regulators operate, examine, and communicate. Proven track record managing complex regulatory interactions, audits, thematic inquiries, and executive briefing processes.
• Strategic Thinker: You can connect the dots and build systems. You have experience implementing structured tracking mechanisms, reporting cycles, and relationship management frameworks across multi-entity, cross-border corporate structures.
• Executive Presence & Influence: High emotional intelligence with outstanding written and verbal communication skills. You can distill voluminous, ambiguous regulatory dialogue into succinct executive summaries and comfortably challenge senior stakeholders on regulatory risk.
• Autonomous: You’re comfortable with ambiguity and have a clear bias for action. You can take high-level objectives, work with the Director of Group Core Compliance to define your own milestones, and build collaborative alliances across separate teams.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Fincrime Reporting
jobs.description:
When Wise’s investigation teams find suspicious activity, we have a legal obligation to report it to Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs) around the world — quickly, accurately and in the format each country requires. Case volumes keep growing as Wise expands into new products and countries, and every FIU has its own rules, formats and submission channels. Without technical leverage, reporting would only scale by adding more people — an expensive route that makes consistency and quality hard to maintain.

The FinCrime Reporting team is the interface between Wise’s FinCrime teams and external FIUs. When AML, Fraud or KYC investigators escalate a case, we determine where it must be reported, gather the right data from across Wise, generate a report that meets local requirements, submit it, and manage what happens next — including keeping funds frozen while law enforcement decides whether a transaction can go ahead. Our goal is to automate this end to end, so reports are faster, more accurate and fully auditable, and our operations specialists can focus on the cases that genuinely need human judgement.

Scope of Responsibilities

FinCrime Reporting is looking for a full-stack Product Engineer to help us build the systems and tools that turn financial crime investigations into high-quality suspicious activity reports. You’ll own components and medium-sized projects across back-end services and the back-office tools our specialists use every day, such as:
• The rules engine that decides which FIUs a case must be reported to, so more cases can skip manual review.
• Data pipelines that gather transactions, customer and case context, and calculate the figures in each report correctly and consistently.
• LLM-assisted narrative generation — including the input data, evaluation, hallucination checks and validation that make generated reports accurate and trustworthy.
• Back-office tools that help reporting specialists review, edit and approve reports quickly, with the right information in one place.
• Automated report submission to FIUs through APIs, SFTP, email and web portals.
• System controls for funds-freezing and other regulatory processes, with a complete audit trail.

 

What will you be doing?
• Design and build reliable, full-stack systems for suspicious activity reporting — from back-end services and data to the back-office interfaces our specialists use.
• Own your work end to end: design, implementation, deployment, and ongoing support in production.
• Partner with Product, Operations, Compliance and Data Analysts to understand how reporting works in practice, remove manual steps, and measure the impact of your work.
• Build automation and bring AI capabilities into production, with attention to correctness, evaluation, traceability, and appropriate human oversight.
• Write well-tested, maintainable code, and improve reliability, security, and technical quality through code reviews, documentation, and knowledge sharing.

Technologies you’ll work with

Our back-end stack is Java, Spring Boot, and Kafka, with SQL databases. Our back-office front end is built with React and TypeScript on Next.js. Services run in Docker containers on Kubernetes in AWS, and our LLM workflows run in Python on Wise’s internal AI platform. You’ll work with distributed services, asynchronous processing, and integrations with external government systems.

We design for scalability, observability, privacy, security, reliability, and cost.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer - Servicing Platform
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
The team you’ll be working with: Mitigation Platform Squad

At Wise, we’re on a mission to make financial services faster, simpler, and more accessible for everyone. To achieve our mission, we also need to safeguard our platform against financial crime and ensure our customers’ money is safe. The Mitigation Platform Squad plays a critical role in this by providing a highly scalable platform to orchestrate which information we need to request from our customers, and then have automations and Servicing Agents to review it. We are developing the infrastructure that provides teams at Wise with insights into the operational cost and risk associated with their ownership of the Wise product. The infrastructure also enables automation of Servicing processes through a rich API in a distributed environment, and it is the core connection between customers and our Servicing agents.

What does our squad look like?

We’re a full stack Squad, with Designers, Product Managers, Analysts, Backenders and Frontenders, with three teams, each owning part of our domain: Ingress to Mitigation domain, Collection, Case Assignment, Case Handling To deliver impact faster, we engage with other teams at Wise, so we deliver a platform with the right complexity and adaptability that gets more impactful for Wise on every release. Collaboration is at the heart of what we do — we value ownership, knowledge sharing, and a commitment to building stable, scalable systems while embracing fast-paced learning and iteration.

What we expect from you

As a Senior Staff Engineer, you'll be embedded in one team at a time, being instrumental in building and maintaining robust and scalable systems. You’ll collaborate closely on feature implementation and issue resolution, as well as discovering the main problems in the space, driving the long-term technical strategy around your ownership, balancing immediate business needs with sustainable architecture and long-term scalability. You'll also play a key role in cross-team collaboration, essential for building and growing our platform for other Wise teams and iterating over the platform's vision. This includes documenting at the appropriate abstraction level to scale the adoption of our developments. We're looking for a proactive individual with a strong foundation in backend technologies, a passion for writing clean and efficient code, and a desire to learn and grow within a supportive environment.

jobs.title: Lead Data Scientist - Treasury Liquidity
jobs.description:
About

the Role:

You will work closely with cross-functional teams to develop data-driven solutions that enhance our liquidity management and operational efficiency.

Here’s how you’ll be contributing:

Liquidity management
• Work closely with Treasury operations to develop supply and demand forecasts and incorporate them into the real-time money movement processes across a multi-region portfolio of products and currencies.
• Conduct rigorous data analysis to support liquidity efficiency initiatives, ensuring a balance between sufficiency and excess.
• Collaborate with engineering teams to implement models within the treasury's operational backoffice, ensuring scalability and operational efficiency.

Liquidity Risk modelling and analysis

jobs.title: Staff Design Researcher - Support
jobs.description:
We’re on the lookout for a Staff Researcher to join our Support Experience team in London! You'll be part of Wise’s global mission to build an open, fair and human financial system. Because people without borders need money without borders.

Your mission:

As a Staff Researcher, you’ll shape how we understand and improve the end-to-end support experience. You’ll work across methods to uncover what customers need when resolving problems, what builds or loses their trust, and where self-service, AI and human support should each play a role.

Your work will span the whole support journey, including the Help Centre, Wise Assistant, human support and the underlying products and processes that determine whether customers’ problems are resolved. You’ll help teams understand what makes support interactions feel helpful, how experiences should work when AI cannot meet a customer’s needs, and what a successful handover to human support looks like.

This is a Staff-level individual contributor role for someone who sets research direction rather than waits for a brief. You’ll define the questions worth answering, choose the right methods and turn evidence into product and service strategy that influences decisions beyond your immediate team.

You’ll also join a community of more than 20 researchers in London. Although our researchers are embedded across different teams and squads, they regularly come together to learn from and support one another.

Here’s how you’ll make an impact:
• Setting priorities and research direction: Identify the most important questions to answer and connect your research priorities to team and business goals.
• Leading complex qualitative and quantitative research: Design and deliver rigorous generative and evaluative studies for ambiguous, high-impact problems, combining qualitative evidence with behavioural, product and operational data where it strengthens decision-making.
• Defining what good looks like: Evaluate support and AI-enabled experiences from the customer’s perspective, then help teams develop meaningful principles, frameworks and measures of quality.
• Shaping self-service, AI and human support: Help teams understand which problems customers expect to solve themselves, where AI can help, when customers need a human and how these routes should work together.
• Improving conversational experiences: Establish what makes AI and human support interactions clear, helpful and trustworthy across different customer needs and situations. Turn evidence into clear recommendations that influence what we build now and how the wider support ecosystem should develop.
• Connecting now, next and future: Balance the long-term vision for Support with what teams need to learn today, adapting your research plans as customer needs, technology and the problem space evolve.
• Influencing senior leaders: Work as a strategic partner to Product, Design, and Data Science, navigating different priorities and helping senior stakeholders reach well-informed decisions.
• Leading with guts: Set ambitious goals, challenge assumptions and champion research quality, our customers and a human-centred approach to product development.
• Bringing sound judgement to AI: Help teams understand how people use and build trust in AI, what happens when it does not work, and how AI-powered experiences should be evaluated and improved.

You’ll operate as a peer to Design, Product, Engineering, Data Science and Operations, bringing rigour, clarity and sound judgement to complex decisions. You’ll resolve ambiguity, align teams around shared evidence and think systemically about how support experiences connect across channels, products and operational processes.

About you:
• You have 6+ years of experience delivering product research in a technology environment, including work on complex, ambiguous and interconnected experiences.
• You have deep expertise in mixed methods research, including generative and evaluative methods, and can combine qualitative evidence with behavioural, product and operational data.
• You have strong service research skills and can investigate experiences across multiple channels, teams and underlying systems rather than treating each interaction in isolation.
• You have experience researching AI-enabled or conversational experiences, including how people develop trust, respond to failures and move between automated and human experiences.
• You use strong judgement to choose the right methods, moving between open-ended exploration, journey-based research and focused evaluation as the problem evolves.
• You can evaluate experiences from the customer’s perspective and help teams translate qualitative evidence into clear principles, frameworks and measures of success.
• You build strong partnerships across Product, Design, Engineering, Data Science and Operations, and have a track record of influencing senior and executive-level decisions.
• You communicate evidence clearly, create momentum without sacrificing rigour and help others improve the quality of their research.
• You can shape research and product strategy across multiple teams while championing customer needs and human-centred design.
• championing rigour, customer needs and human-centred design.

Not ticking every box? That's okay. If this role excites you and you're keen to grow into it, we'd still love to hear from you! Research shows that some people hesitate to apply unless they meet every single requirement, and we don't want to miss out on great candidates because of it.

 

As a heads up, this role probably isn't for you if:
• Your experience is primarily market research and/or academia
• You're not comfortable navigating the complexity of overseeing multiple product areas in a fast-paced environment

jobs.title: Engineering Lead - Fincrime
jobs.description:
The AUP (Acceptable Use Policy) team is part of Fincrime. We design, build, and operate the preventative and detective controls that monitor transactions and customer activity. If someone tries to use Wise for prohibited activities, we detect it, review it, and take action.

Join us as we shift our strategy from "Policy-First to Risk-Driven" to drive growth. We want to enable all legal activities and minimise friction for legitimate customers, while surgically targeting and neutralising genuinely illicit, high-risk behaviours.

As the Engineering Lead, you will lead a highly collaborative, cross-functional squad, alongside data scientists, analysts, compliance managers, and designers.

How we work:

We operate with high autonomy, low control, and a belief that the best ideas win. We don’t just hand you a roadmap; you will partner directly with your Product Manager, Compliance Lead, and Lead Data Scientist to define both the product and technical vision for the team.

What will you be working on?
• Risk Detection: Close coverage gaps and scale our detection systems by integrating advanced Machine Learning models and building robust controls to spot AUP violations.
• Supercharge Operations: Architect automated workflows and intuitive internal tooling to reduce the cost per case and median handling times for our operations analysts.
• Own the Architecture: Keep our services highly available, resilient, and secure. You’ll ensure we have the right monitoring, observability, and decoupled architectures to scale alongside Wise's massive global volume.

jobs.title: Partner Risk Monitoring Specialist

You will be responsible for monitoring our banks and online platforms partnering with Wise at Wise Platform. This position offers the unique opportunity to influence Wise’s mission and establish partnerships that facilitate instant, borderless money for more people.

Your mission

Wise Platform helps financial institutions and large enterprises leverage Wise’s infrastructure to offer their customers world class payments products through their own platforms. Wise Platform is a start-up within a scale up. We’re a cross functional team across sales, account management, product, engineering, compliance, analytics and many other functions. We’re based across the world – from London to Singapore, Austin and beyond. 

Your primary mission will be to monitor the compliance activity of our banks and online platforms, assessing that partners onboard customers to our platform according to their compliance policies, Wise’s requirements and these meet our regulatory obligations.

Job

• Perform ongoing monitoring measures applicable to Wise Platform partners in accordance with internal policies and procedures
• Assessing customers’ risks and applying risk-based approach methodologies
• Perform ongoing risk monitoring on complex and high risk customers, document and provide thorough analysis on potential risks and apply appropriate mitigation measures by analyzing their business activities, compliance programs and controls
• Assess the customer’s potential reputational and financial crime risk to Wise from Sanctions, PEP, and adverse media perspective

jobs.description:

the role:

For our customers, using Wise is as simple as sending money from A to B. Yet behind our app and website is a complex engine of currencies, routes, products and features, generating terabytes of data each day.

The Data Products and Insights squad is at the core of systems that store, process, and leverage data, machine learning models, and generative AI capabilities. Ultimately, this provides insights and innovative ML and AI driven solutions that serve as key drivers for business growth.

Your mission will be to lead the teams building and maintaining a platform that enables everyone at Wise to leverage petabyte-scale data to power our product and to enable timely, intelligent decisions for our teams.

You will guide the sustainable growth of this critical function, lead other engineering leads, senior engineers and have the opportunity to shape multiple teams across our analytics platform.

Your input will directly affect how Wise builds and scales large-scale data and analytical capabilities across the company, enabling teams to move with speed and confidence while maintaining reliability, security and operational excellence.

How we work: 

We operate with a belief in automation, programmatic implementation, and reusable design. We’re looking for people who can step back and think holistically about the ecosystem, but also follow through and help implement the design; drawing on the resources across the rest of the Platform Tribe.

As we grow, it is imperative to protect our customers’ money and navigate complex regulatory requirements world-wide. You will have a focus on running and maintaining services and libraries, making sure we have the right observability and service management elements in place, with an eye for high-availability, assessing and reducing engineering load and devising more effective ways for the team to look after its cloud-based platform.

We need to sustain this growth by continuously iterating on the services we run, with a focus on availability, security, and ease of use. We’re looking for an engineer with relevant experience who can understand and respond to complex requirements and deliver simple solutions to help our teams achieve our mission with speed and confidence.

You are an experienced leader, confident in problem-solving and guiding engineering teams through the complexities of project delivery using both agile and traditional methodologies. You have experience growing more junior leaders and staff+ engineers.

Great communication skills and the ability to build consensus - you’re comfortable making a case for what you believe we should be doing.

Experience being a self-starter, self-motivated and collaborative.

The mindset to solve problems from scratch.

Comfortable taking ownership of vendor negotiations and explaining costs to the business.

Willingness to give and take regular feedback - regular feedback is part of our culture.
