jobs.title: Finance Systems Change Programme Lead
jobs.description:
The role

Wise is investing significantly in its finance systems, processes and controls to support the next stage of growth as a dual-listed global technology company.

We are looking for an experienced Finance Systems Change Programme Lead to establish, mobilise and lead our Finance Systems Change programme.

This role will be responsible for creating the structure, governance and delivery model required to successfully execute a multi-year finance systems change agenda, including finance systems modernisation, ERP transformation, finance data architecture, process standardisation and control automation.

Working across Finance, Product, Engineering, Data and external partners, the Programme Lead will ensure that strategic objectives are translated into an executable programme with clear ownership, governance and measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Programme Mobilisation & Governance
• Establish and lead the Finance Systems Change Programme.
• Define programme governance, workstreams, decision forums and reporting structures.
• Create and manage executive reporting for Steering Committees, Finance Leadership and other stakeholders
• Ensure alignment across Finance, Product, Engineering, Data and Controls functions.

Change Delivery
• Coordinate delivery across multiple change workstreams including:
• ERP transformation
• Finance systems modernisation
• Finance data architecture
• Reporting transformation
• Process standardisation
• Control automation
• AI usage

jobs.title: Influencer Senior Manager (NorthAm)

jobs.title: FinCrime Investigator - AML Investigations
Executive Assistant to Product Leads

jobs.title: Global Complaints Senior Lead

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Java - AML Handling
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Safeguarding Controller - APAC

jobs.title: Senior People Technology Engineer (Workday Time & Absence)

jobs.title: Associate, Transaction Monitoring
jobs.description:
YouTrip is the leading and fastest-growing multi-currency payment platform in Asia Pacific. In 2018, we pioneered the region's first multi-currency digital wallet. Now, YouTrip is the #1 multi-currency digital wallet trusted by millions across the region, processing over US$15 billion in total payment value annually. 

Our consumer and business propositions – YouTrip and YouBiz – empower individuals and businesses with inclusive, accessible, and affordable financial solutions. You Will
• Conduct end-to-end transaction investigations from the detection of unusual activities, to the analysis and documentation and submission of Suspicious Matter Reports (“SMR”) for lodgment to the relevant authorities.

jobs.title: SOC Analyst, Security Operations
jobs.description:
Who we are 

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

 

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

 

Your mission

Security is fundamental to the trust millions of customers place in Bitpanda every day. As an Cyber Security Engineer, you'll help protect our platform by detecting threats, responding to incidents and continuously improving the security of our cloud-native environment. Working alongside experienced security engineers, you'll build detections, automate repetitive tasks and investigate security events that help keep our infrastructure, applications and customers safe.

What you'll do
• Build and improve detections. Develop, test and tune detection rules in Elastic Security (ES|QL/KQL), helping improve detection coverage, reduce false positives and ensure meaningful threats are identified quickly.
• Investigate security events and hunt for threats. Respond to security alerts, participate in incident response, perform proactive threat hunting across AWS, Elastic and Datadog, and contribute to improving investigation and response processes.
• Automate security operations. Build scripts, API integrations and SOAR workflows that reduce manual effort, improve investigation quality and help the Security team operate more efficiently.
• Help secure our cloud platform. Monitor AWS security events, investigate suspicious activity, contribute to system hardening and security tooling improvements, and support initiatives that strengthen Bitpanda's overall security posture.
• Contribute to a strong security culture. Work closely with engineers across the business, support compliance activities including ISO 27001, PCI DSS and DORA, and help promote security best practices throughout the organisation.
• Keep millions of users safe, no matter the time of day. As part of this commitment, you'll participate in a weekly rotating on-call schedule alongside the rest of the team.

Who you are
• You have 2–4 years of experience in information security, security engineering or security operations, with exposure to incident response, SIEM, threat hunting or cloud security.
• You enjoy solving technical security problems and have experience writing scripts or automating workflows using APIs or security tooling.
• You have a solid understanding of AWS or another major cloud platform, networking fundamentals, system hardening and security monitoring. Experience with Elastic Security, ES|QL or KQL is a big plus!
• You're curious, proactive and eager to learn, taking ownership of your work while seeking opportunities to improve both security and operational efficiency.
• You're passionate about keeping millions of users safe, no matter the time of day; This role has on call responsibilities that rotate through the team on a weekly basis.

What’s in it for you
• Flexibility to work where you thrive – Enjoy the freedom of our Hybrid working model, combining onsite collaboration and remote work, with an additional 25 days per year to work from a city or country of your choice.
• Reward for your impact – Receive a competitive total compensation package aligned with Bitpanda’s pay-for-impact policy, including participation in our stock option plan.
• Support for your mental wellbeing – Access confidential coaching, counselling, and mental health resources whenever you need them through OpenUP.
• Time to recharge – On top of your standard annual leave, prioritise your wellbeing in 2027 with 3 additional days of paid time off to rest, reset, and recharge, available once you’ve been with us for 6 months.
• Continuous learning and growth – Grow your skills and stay ahead in your career with unlimited access to Udemy’s library of online courses at your own pace.
• Exclusive perks and rewards – Enjoy discounts, rewards, and perks from partners worldwide across lifestyle, wellness, tech, and travel.
• Support during life milestones – Take advantage of up to 8 additional weeks of gender-neutral new parent leave to welcome and bond with your new addition to the family.
• Fuel and focus on-site – Pandas in Vienna, Bucharest, Barcelona, and Berlin can enjoy free onsite dining, with freshly prepared lunches and snacks to keep you fueled and focused all day long.
• Recognition for your contributions – Celebrate milestones and achievements with recognition and rewards for your Tenure at Bitpanda.
• Show your Bitpanda pride – Access exclusive Bitpanda-branded merchandise and gear to represent.
• Connect and celebrate with your team – Join unforgettable company events, from our Winter Party in Vienna to gatherings worldwide, fostering fun, connection, and celebration

 .…and even more location-specific benefits designed to make life at Bitpanda even more rewarding wherever you are.

 

Above all, you will have the opportunity to learn and grow as part of Bitpanda’s incredible journey towards being Europe’s future #1 investment platform.

Bitpanda is committed to fostering a fair and equal environment based on trust and mutual respect. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is paramount to our success and we are committed to building a team that represents a wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

* These benefits may be adjusted at Bitpanda’s discretion and do not apply to our internships and exceptions to our Hybrid Working policy apply to teams with shift schedules or for folks whose roles require them to be in-office (think: Workplaces team or IT).

jobs.title: Commercial Account Executive
jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Sales at Brex

The Sales team is the driving factor behind revenue for Brex and every member of our team directly affects our bottom line. We focus on generating new opportunities, acquiring new customers, and building even stronger relationships with our current customers. Our winning culture recognizes big team wins and celebrates individual accomplishments. We ensure that top performers are recognized and have built a competitive environment to motivate and unify the team.

What you’ll do

As a Commercial Account Executive, you’ll fuel Brex’s growth by winning net-new revenue from small to mid-sized businesses. In this high-volume, fast-paced role, you’ll prospect, build strong partnerships, and close deals by showing the unmatched value of Brex’s all-in-one Financial Operating System—Corporate Card, Expense Management, and Travel.

Where you'll work

This role will be based in one of our Brex offices — San Francisco, Seattle, New York, Vancouver, or Salt Lake City. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work.

Responsibilities
• Full-Cycle Sales Execution: Own the end-to-end sales process from outbound prospecting to discovery, product demos, and closing deals.
• Pipeline Generation Management: Consistently source and qualify leads to maintain a strong, reliable pipeline.
• Value-Based Selling: Clearly communicate ROI and business value by understanding each prospect's goals and aligning Brex’s solutions to their needs.
• Customer-Centric Problem Solving: Build trust through insight and service, helping prospects navigate challenges and unlock growth.
• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Sales Development, Product, and Underwriting to create a smooth and impactful buyer experience.

Requirements
• 1+ years of closing experience in B2B SaaS sales, ideally in a high-volume or new business-focused role
• A high-performing SDR/BDR background with a strong track record of sourcing and qualifying opportunities due to high self-prospecting requirements in role
• Strong ability to communicate value and ROI to small or mid-sized business stakeholders
• Consistent quota attainment and a history of top-tier performance
• A proactive, self-motivated approach with a focus on results and customer impact

Bonus points
• Familiarity selling financial software (Expense Management, ERP, AP Automation, T E, Accounting Software, Banking, etc.)

Compensation

The expected OTE range for this role is $172,890 - $192,100. The starting wage will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. The OTE figure listed here includes base salary and commissions, which may or may not be earned depending on performance. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

Engineering at Brex

Engineering at Brex is about building systems that scale with speed and intention. Our teams operate with high autonomy and deep collaboration, own outcomes end to end, and push for excellence from architecture to deployment. It’s an environment where engineering is a craft and builders grow by solving meaningful technical problems.

What you’ll do

The Identity and Access Management team builds and maintains secure, user-friendly authentication and authorization systems that protect users, safeguard company assets, and provide a seamless access experience for developers. The team owns critical platform capabilities including login methods, step-up authentication, our custom authorization platform, account delegation flows like Copilot, Pro Access login, embedded partnerships authentication, and core vendor integrations.

As a Staff Engineer on IAM, you will lead projects and initiatives to improve the security, reliability, and developer experience of our authentication, authorization, and identity platforms for customers, partners, and internal systems. You will scope and drive projects with clear impact, work cross-functionally with the broader engineering organization, help define the team’s technical quality, and help evolve the identity platform as Brex invests in signed identity propagation, delegated and agent identity, fine-grained authorization, stronger auditability, and enterprise-ready customer authentication experiences.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our Vancouver office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require Monday, Wednesday and Thursday to be designated in office days. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities
• Design, build, and operate backend systems and APIs for authentication, authorization, identity context, and audit-related workflows.
• Lead engineers across the organization on initiatives end to end, from technical design and implementation through rollout, measurement, and operational support.
• Improve login and access experiences across SSO, MFA, step-up authentication, delegated access, and enterprise identity flows.
• Build and extend authorization systems that support custom roles, resource-aware access control, and secure defaults for product teams.
• Lead creation of durable, identity-aware audit trails and attribution for user, service, delegated, and agent-driven actions.
• Partner closely with engineers across Brex to make IAM integrations secure by default and easier to adopt through clear patterns, tooling, and shared libraries.
• Mentor engineers on the team to deliver high-quality code and produce operational improvements that raise the bar for reliability and maintainability across the team’s systems.

Requirements
• You have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience building reliable production backend systems.
• You have experience leading complex projects and mentoring other engineers.
• You have strong API design fundamentals, rigor around testing, code quality, and documentation.
• You understand core IAM concepts such as authentication, authorization, sessions, tokens, MFA, SSO, OAuth, SAML, OIDC, or RBAC.
• You communicate clearly, collaborate well across teams, and are effective in cross-functional technical discussions.
• You care about operational excellence and know how to improve system reliability, reduce toil, and maintain high-quality services over time.
• You have strong product and engineering judgment and can balance security, usability, and developer experience.

Bonus points
• You have worked on identity and access management, authentication, authorization, or audit systems in a production environment.
• You have hands-on experience with Okta, Oso, SSO, SAML, OIDC, OAuth, or WebAuthn.
• You have experience building enterprise-facing admin controls, authorization platforms, delegated access flows, or audit trails.
• You have worked on platform teams that provide shared infrastructure, paved roads, or secure-by-default frameworks for other engineering teams.

Compensation:

The expected salary range for this role is $240,000 - $300,000 CAD. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors, including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, Tooling (Product)
jobs.description:
About the Company

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Tooling

The Role:

Principal Software Engineer (Product)

As a Principal Product Engineer, you'll set technical direction for the customer-facing platform that defines how millions of users experience Gemini — onboarding, compliance, customer support, and the systems that hold the customer journey together. This is a role for an engineer who operates at the level of the technology itself: someone accountable for company-level initiatives, who drives the hardest technical challenges across organizational boundaries, and who creates the architectural vision that other teams build against. 

You'll work across backend, web, and mobile, but your leverage comes less from what you build directly than from the direction you set, the leaders you grow, and the frontier you push. We treat AI-assisted development and automation as first-class — an agentic SDLC pipeline where agents plan, implement, and review work through our harness under human gates. As a Principal, you're expected to shape where that frontier goes, define the patterns and operational guidelines other engineers adopt, and advance how the whole organization builds. If you're energized by owning ambiguous, company-critical technical bets and multiplying the engineers around you, we'd love to talk.

This role is required to be in person twice a week at our New York City, NY office.

Responsibilities:
• Own the technical vision and architecture for the customer-facing platform, designing for scale and reliability with a multi-year horizon and anticipating needs before they arrive.
• Review critical designs across organizations and drive the designs for projects involving the hardest technical challenges at the company; act as a key driver of demos and technical direction beyond your own team.
• Be accountable for one or more core company initiatives spanning onboarding, compliance (KYC/identity), and customer support — carrying them from ambiguity through production and long-term operation.
• Identify strategic direction in technology and product, proposing and adopting architecture and platform approaches that advance it; tie technical bets clearly to company objectives.
• Plan and deliver large, complex, cross-org programs with interdependencies across teams and systems, spanning months to years; identify the problems worth solving and advocate for their prioritization.
• Define patterns, operational guidelines, and engineering practices for your vertical(s), and extend process improvements across teams and command pilot units.
• Provide critical technical guidance proactively — raising the security, reliability, and quality bar across the organization, and debugging or contributing to the most complex parts of a system when needed.
• Act as a technical multiplier: mentor and develop engineers and future leaders, share knowledge, delegate to grow others, and lead initiatives across domains, including outside your core area of expertise.
• Drive the organization toward a strategic vision for strong systems, sustainable practice, and healthy engineering culture; play a critical role in recruiting and bar-raising.

Minimum

Qualifications:
• 12+ years of software engineering experience building and operating complex production systems at scale.
• Recognized expertise in one or two core technical domains, with a track record of being accountable for company-level systems or initiatives end to end.
• A history of driving architecture and design for the hardest technical challenges across multiple teams or organizations.
• Demonstrated ability to set technical vision with company-level impact and to bring an increasingly strategic mindset to engineering decisions.
• Fluency across multiple layers of the stack (backend services plus web and/or mobile) and willingness to go deep wherever a problem requires.
• Proficiency in a typed language (e.g., TypeScript, Scala, Java, Go) and comfort with JavaScript/TypeScript on web and mobile surfaces.
• Experience building consumer-facing applications with strong product and UX sensibility.
• Fluency in using AI coding tools and automation, and a point of view on how to advance an agentic development practice.
• A record of acting as a technical multiplier — developing engineers and leaders, influencing prioritization across teams, and leading cross-domain initiatives.
• Excellent communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical issues to diverse audiences and build alignment across organizations.

Preferred

Qualifications:
• Experience in the crypto or fintech industry, or as a user of crypto products.
• Deep experience with onboarding, identity/KYC, compliance, or customer support tooling.
• Experience architecting and operating AI agents or agentic workflows in production at scale.
• Familiarity with React/React Native and cloud/microservices architecture.
• A record of driving product and technical strategy with data and experimentation.
• Experience representing engineering externally (talks, writing) or in cross-company technical collaboration.

It Pays to Work Here

 

The compensation benefits package for this role includes:
• Competitive starting pay
• A discretionary annual bonus
• Long-term incentive in the form of a new hire equity grant
• Comprehensive health plans
• 401K with company matching
• Paid Parental Leave
• Flexible time off

Salary Range: The base salary range for this role is between $192,500 - $275,000 in the State of New York. This range is not inclusive of our discretionary bonus or equity package. When determining a candidate’s compensation, we consider a number of factors including skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

In the United States, we offer a hybrid work approach at our hub offices, balancing the benefits of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Expectations may vary by location and role, so candidates are encouraged to connect with their recruiter to learn more about the specific policy for the role. Employees who do not live near one of our hubs are part of our remote workforce. All employees, however, are required to onboard in-person at one of our office locations.

At Gemini, we strive to build diverse teams that reflect the people we want to empower through our products, and we are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. Equal Opportunity is the Law, and Gemini is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. If you have a specific need that requires accommodation, please let a member of the People Team know.

jobs.description:
About the Role

Mercury is seeking a Business Continuity Management (BCM) Lead to build and lead an enterprise-wide continuity program as we prepare to become a bank. As part of the Risk team, this leader will establish practical standards, clear accountability, and tested capabilities to maintain critical services and recover effectively from disruptions, with direct visibility to the CRO and senior leadership.

This role fills the need for a dedicated leader to coordinate BCM across the organization. The ideal candidate combines deep continuity and resilience expertise with the judgment to build a proportionate program in a fast-moving environment, working effectively with Engineering, Operations, Product, Information Security, Legal, Compliance, and business teams.

The BCM Lead will own the enterprise framework, coordination, oversight, and reporting. Business and technology owners will remain accountable for their continuity plans and recovery execution.Because this is a new program, the Lead will be hands-on in the initial build: facilitating the first round of BIAs and plans side by side with owners, running exercises, and driving identified gaps through remediation. This leader will also work closely with Engineering on technology disaster recovery and with relevant teams on incident response, crisis management, and third-party resilience.

Key Responsibilities
• Develop and implement Mercury’s enterprise BCM framework, policies, standards, governance, and operating model, with a prioritized implementation roadmap aligned to bank-launch readiness and critical services.
• Partner with business owners to identify critical services, conduct business impact analyses (customer, financial, operational, and regulatory), and map dependencies across people, processes, technology, facilities, and third parties, including single points of failure.
• Establish recovery time objectives (RTOs) and recovery point objectives (RPOs), where applicable, with business and technology owners; challenge gaps between objectives and recovery capabilities.
• Set standards for continuity plans and recovery procedures, and facilitate and support accountable owners in developing actionable plans and alternative operating arrangements.
• Coordinate business continuity with technology disaster recovery, incident response, and crisis management, with clear activation criteria, escalation paths, and communications responsibilities.
• Design and lead a risk-based exercise program, from tabletop simulations to end-to-end recovery tests, and drive lessons learned, remediation tracking, and verification that gaps are closed.
• Partner with Third-Party Risk Management and vendor owners to assess critical provider recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements, and concentration dependencies.
• Embed continuity considerations into new products, material business changes, and technology implementations.
• Establish metrics and reporting that give management and relevant committees visibility into readiness, testing outcomes, material gaps, and overdue remediation.
• Build and lead a growing BCM team, including hiring and developing analysts as the program scales over the next year.
• Deliver role-based training and promote awareness of continuity responsibilities across the organization.
• Support regulatory examinations and bank-launch readiness reviews with accurate documentation and evidence of recovery capability.

Qualifications
• 10+ years of experience in business continuity management, operational resilience, disaster recovery, or a related discipline within a fintech, financial institution, technology company, or other highly regulated environment.
• Demonstrated experience building or materially enhancing an enterprise BCM program, including governance, implementation, testing, and reporting.
• Strong skills in business impact analysis, critical-service identification, dependency mapping, and recovery objective development.
• Experience developing actionable continuity plans and leading exercises that test recovery assumptions and expose gaps.
• Sufficient technical fluency to work with Engineering on cloud services, system dependencies, data recovery, and technology disaster recovery.
• Working knowledge of third-party risk management, including assessing critical vendor recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements and concentration risk.
• Proven ability to drive cross-functional remediation through influence, with a clear view of where BCM oversight ends and business or technology ownership begins.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain readiness gaps and tradeoffs to senior leadership.
• Experience managing a team of Business Continuity analysts.

Preferred Qualifications
• Familiarity with banking supervisory expectations for business continuity, and operational resilience.
• Experience operating in a company-building or bank-building environment.
• Familiarity with recognized continuity standards, such as ISO 22301, and BCM tools for plan management, exercises, and issue tracking.
• Relevant professional certification, such as CBCP or MBCI.

Leadership Attributes
• Pragmatic, first-principles builder who turns ambiguous needs into clear priorities and designs a program that fits Mercury’s operations and scale.
• Takes ownership and follows through from identified gaps to demonstrated recovery.
• Collaborative, low-ego, and effective across the three lines of defense.
• Calm under pressure and able to facilitate clear decisions during disruptions.
• Able to challenge constructively, distinguish material gaps from theoretical concerns, and avoid over-engineering.

jobs.description:
In 1851, a New York bookkeeper named George D. Lyman observed the same absurd ritual each afternoon: porters carried bags of coins and bundles of checks bank to bank down Wall Street, settling by hand, a fortune exposed to error and theft. Lyman's fix: send everything through one central office and settle the net. On October 11, 1853, in the basement of 14 Wall Street, 52 banks cleared $22.6 million in a single sitting. Money between banks had stopped being an event and became seamless infrastructure.

A century and a half later, the hard part is unchanged: moving money once is easy; making it work every time, for hundreds of thousands of businesses, across every rail, is hard. The bank account is where a company's financial life happens - payroll clears or it doesn't; a wire lands or a deal slips; the month closes clean, or someone loses a weekend to it. Mercury is building a business banking* product at a scale better than anything else in the market.

Business Banking is the heart of Mercury. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving deposit and payment growth, and owning business performance.

jobs.description:
In 1967, John Shepherd-Barron reached his bank minutes after closing and could not get at his own money. In the bath that evening, he thought of a chocolate bar dispenser and swapped the chocolate for cash. On 27 June, outside a Barclays branch on Enfield High Street, an actor named Reg Varney drew £10 from the world's first cash machine. It took a four-digit code (originally six, until his wife told him nobody remembers six). The bank's hours had stopped being the customer's problem.

Nearly sixty years later, the bar has moved, but the test hasn't: a personal financial product is judged on whether it fits the life of the person using it. People do not read documentation, forgive a confusing screen, or care how the ledger works. They want one place that makes sense of everything — spending, saving, planning, investing — and that anticipates rather than reports: where they stand, what deserves attention, what to do next. Mercury is building personal banking* to that standard.

Personal Banking is how Mercury earns a place in someone's financial life. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving growth and engagement, and owning business performance.

About

the role:

As Mercury continues its rapid growth trajectory, navigating an increasingly complex regulatory, partner, and product landscape is critical. Compliance is not only a requirement, but a competitive advantage that enables Mercury to move faster, build trust, and launch innovative products responsibly. 

Nowhere is that more true than in AI. We believe we have a path to lead the US banking* industry into the AI era, and that how we choose to build and deploy AI will define our success over the next three years. 

We are building first-party agentic products, headless and agent-accessible banking through our API and MCP, and the internal platforms that let us build with AI at speed. Core to all of it is great governance—these systems must run on one trusted system of access, logging, and data controls that meets the requirements of our banking ambitions.

We are seeking a Lead Compliance Risk Manager to serve as the compliance advisor for Mercury's AI products. This is a new, high-visibility role and the first dedicated compliance advisory seat covering AI at Mercury. You will be the leading authority on AI product compliance risk for the Compliance Team—shaping how we build, how we govern, and how we explain ourselves to our partners and regulators.

You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Legal, and Operations to ensure Mercury's AI products are compliant-by-design from concept through launch and scale. You will also help define the AI governance framework itself: the standards, controls, escalation paths, and documentation that allow a bank-partnered fintech to deploy agentic capabilities responsibly and at pace.

How this role fits alongside our other AI roles: this is a product compliance advisory role. Our Data AI Governance team owns enterprise governance frameworks, responsible-AI standards, AI use case intake and inventory, and risk classification; Model Risk Management owns model inventory, tiering, and validation. You will be a close partner to and a major consumer of both—running our AI products through their processes, applying their standards to real product decisions, and bringing them the product-level detail they need to see. You will also help extend our existing product compliance playbooks to cover AI features, in partnership with your manager and the rest of the Product Compliance team. Your mandate is the products, not the program. 

In this role, you will:
• Serve as the subject matter expert and primary compliance advisor for Mercury's AI and agentic products, including Command, our API, and agentic access methods such as MCP and CLI.
• Work closely with cross-functional risk and product teams to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a way that meets all relevant financial partner, regulatory compliance obligations, and our AI governance standards.
• Ensure all processes and products under your area of responsibility comply with applicable rules and regulations. Stay up to date with changes to applicable regulations, supervisory guidance, and emerging AI-specific law, and implement necessary updates to impacted products to maintain compliance.
• Support expansion for new product launches by scoping, defining, and communicating product and compliance requirements.
• Work cross-functionally to drive remediation efforts for products within your defined scope.
• Support the compliance function in defining and achieving departmental initiatives, maintaining relevant policies and procedures, developing documentation solutions, and liaising with auditors.
• Mentor and provide strategic guidance to compliance colleagues as AI capabilities spread across every product domain, and contribute to building a strong culture of compliance across Mercury.
• Work closely with our Risk team, which owns AI governance, as Compliance’s AI product expert to contribute product-level guidance to ongoing AI governance updates.

Core

responsibilities:
• Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Operations, and Legal to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a manner that meets all relevant regulatory, financial partner, and network obligations.
• Advise product and engineering teams throughout the product lifecycle—discovery, design, evaluation, launch, and iteration—to ensure AI products are compliant-by-design rather than reviewed after the fact.
• Identify, assess, and document compliance risks specific to AI and agentic systems—including inaccurate or fabricated output, unauthorized or over-scoped agent action, inadequate consent and disclosure, unexplainable decisioning, disparate impact, data leakage across customers or organizations, prompt injection and third-party agent risk, and insufficient audit trail—and work cross-functionally to design pragmatic mitigation strategies.
• Define the compliance requirements for the platforms AI is built on, in partnership with the teams that own them: the LLM gateway all internal traffic routes through, the internal app platform, agent orchestration frameworks, and the data access and governance layer.
• Establish and refine AI-specific compliance standards for the department—what evidence a launch requires, what must be logged, what requires human review, what must be escalated, and what is out of bounds—and ensure those standards evolve as the organization and the technology grow.
• Support new product launches and expansions by scoping, defining, and communicating compliance requirements clearly and early, including for co-marketing and distribution partnerships with third-party AI platforms.
• Monitor regulatory, supervisory, and industry developments relevant to AI in financial services, assess impact, and drive implementation of required changes.
• Own and oversee multiple concurrent high-impact AI compliance workstreams, holding project owners accountable for results and ensuring each aligns with department and company objectives.
• Support remediation efforts for products within scope, including root cause analysis, corrective action planning, and execution tracking.
• Partner with executive leadership, partner bank compliance teams, and external advisors to guide high-level decisions on AI direction, presenting data-driven recommendations.
• Contribute to the broader Compliance function by supporting policy development, documentation standards, audit preparation, and examiner interactions.
• Help build and reinforce a strong culture of compliance across Mercury through collaboration, education, and influence—including raising the AI fluency of the Compliance team itself, and developing scalable tools, templates, and frameworks others can reuse.

You should have:
• 8+ years of experience in a compliance advisory, product compliance, or regulatory risk role, ideally within fintech or financial services, with a track record of being the recognized authority in your domain.
• Demonstrated experience advising on AI, machine learning, or model-driven products in a regulated environment—or comparable experience standing up a new compliance domain where no playbook existed.
• Working knowledge of the regulatory and supervisory framework relevant to AI in banking, including UDAAP, fair lending and ECOA/Reg B, FCRA and adverse action, Reg E and payments authorization, BSA/AML, GLBA and privacy, marketing and disclosure requirements, recordkeeping, complaint management, model risk management expectations, and third-party and vendor risk management guidance.
• Familiarity with emerging AI-specific regimes and frameworks and the ability to form a practical view on their application—such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, state AI and automated decisioning laws.
• Technical fluency to engage credibly with engineers on model behavior, evaluation and testing, agent permissioning and tool scoping, logging and observability, and data access controls—and to know which questions actually surface risk.
• Deep experience partnering with product and engineering teams on regulatory and compliance matters across the product lifecycle, including on fast-moving launches with external dependencies.
• Proven ability to own highly ambiguous, large-scale compliance problems and to create and execute a strategy to address them, without waiting for precedent.
• Experience designing compliance frameworks that span multiple product lines or departments, and improving systems and processes so that compliance posture evolves alongside business growth.
• Demonstrated success operating with senior stakeholders, including executives, partner banks, auditors, or regulators, and presenting data-driven recommendations that drive decisions.
• Strong project management skills, including the ability to define problems, create execution plans, manage several high-impact initiatives at once, and drive outcomes.

• Experience mentoring mid-level compliance professionals and raising the capability of a team, not just delivering your own work.
• Comfort operating independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, with sound judgment on when to move and when to escalate.
• Curiosity, adaptability, and genuine interest in engaging with frontier technology and the regulatory challenges that come with it.

About

the role:

Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank. 

Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit. 

Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.

What you’ll do:
• Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.
• Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.
• Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.
• Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.
• Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.
• Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose.
• Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use.
• Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution.
• Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals.
• Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.
• Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.
• Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.
• Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.
• Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk.

What we’re looking for:
• 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development, quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting.
• Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred.
• Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2.
• Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models.
• Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can explain model risk to a data scientist and to a regulator, or translate your findings and recommendations to guidance for the 1LOD product/business teams, and use different language for each.
• Exceptional attention to detail across documentation, code base, testing artifacts and quantitative analysis provided by 1LOD.
• Sound judgment and a practical, risk-based mindset: you can distinguish significant model risk from lower-risk matters and have the confidence to challenge model owners constructively, including senior stakeholders.
• High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort building processes in a fast evolving environment, where priorities evolve quickly, new ad hoc requests emerge regularly, and role boundaries are intentionally broad. You can operate effectively without tightly-defined scope, find the highest-leverage work, and get it done.

Preferred

qualifications:
• Experience helping build or materially enhance a model risk management program.
• Familiarity with bank regulatory examinations, charter readiness, or the implementation of risk programs within a growing financial institution.
• Knowledge of Haskell

What success looks like:
• Mercury maintains a complete and reliable view of its material models and aggregate model risk.
• Critical models receive timely, technically credible, and risk-based independent review.
• Model limitations, performance concerns, and remediation needs are clearly understood and acted upon.
• Model owners view Model Risk as a rigorous and constructive partner that improves decisions without creating unnecessary friction.
• Mercury’s Model Risk Management program is scalable, practical, and ready to withstand regulatory and independent assurance review.

Open call for Founders / Founding Teams (Product Management / Engineering roles) 

In 1973 at Xerox PARC, Bob Metcalfe sketched a way for many computers to share a single wire — borrowing the throughput math from his study of Hawaii's ALOHAnet — and he and David Boggs built it and measured it until it held. Behind Ethernet was a two-person team that turned a contested idea into the measured standard now carrying almost all the world's wired traffic.

At Mercury, we’re looking to accelerate several of our AI products that our customers love like Command, CLI, and MCP. We’re building for ambitious people of all kinds, and are a company made of founders and small technical teams trying to change the world - as part of that, we’re taking open applications for founders or small technical teams (Eng+) that want to work together on building the AI products of the future. This isn't a fixed role. We expect the nature of work is changing, and small teams of people paired with AI product surface and autonomy to build can create 10x outcomes. Apply as a small team or as an individual 

Here are some things you’ll do on the job:
• Find the problem. Work close enough to customers that you spot what matters before anyone assigns it to you — then decide it's worth building.
• Build and automate the workflow end to end using Command, CLI, MCP, and the rest of our AI stack.
• Ship to customers fast — quick understanding, tight iteration, deploy.
• Measure the impact honestly, then do the next one. Kill what didn't move; double down on what did.
• Run as an autonomous team — pick the target, ship the thing, own the outcome.

You should:
• Have shipped something real - a product, a tool, a company, or an open-source project people actually use.
• Be dangerous across the stack: PMs who can prototype, engineers with product taste.
• Have strong opinions about AI products and the judgment to recognize fast when one of them is wrong.
• Hands experience building AI products with AI, and knowledge about RAG, evals, agent harnesses a plus
• Move fast and measure. Expect most experiments to fail and treat that as the price of finding the ones that don't.
• Care about craft where it's impactful and resist polishing what isn't.
• Communicate clearly and own outcomes - we want real business impact, customer time/pain saved, and a path to scaling what works

Learn more about what we're building:
• Mercury Command — Complete financial work end-to-end with AI. Tell Mercury what to do in natural language; it stages the action and executes with your approval.
• Mercury MCP CLI — Give your AI agents direct access to verified financial data, or work with your Mercury account straight from the terminal.
• The bank of the future knows your business — Immad on what we're building toward and why now is the moment.

What happens next?

Submit your application and our recruiting team will follow up. We're genuinely open to connecting with founders and teams at any stage — whether you're a strong fit for something we're actively building toward right now, or this is the start of a longer relationship we pick back up when the opportunity is right. If you're building, we want to know you.

jobs.title: Senior Customer Support Service Delivery Program Manager
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In 1931, electrical draftsman Harry Beck looked at London’s Underground map and saw a system that had become too complicated to understand.

The maps at the time tried to represent the city geographically. Beck realized that wasn’t what riders actually needed. What mattered was how the system connected: which lines went where, where you could transfer, and the simplest way to get from one place to another. So he redrew the network around those relationships instead. His design became the foundation for the modern Tube map and changed how people navigated London.

Mercury’s Customer Experience organization has its own increasingly complex network.

As Mercury grows, the right place for support work will keep changing. Some new or complex work may benefit from starting in an incubation team before we know how it should scale. From there, it might move into Core Support, remain specialized, transition to an outsourced partner, or become increasingly supported by AI-powered tooling. The challenge is knowing where work belongs at each stage of its lifecycle, when it’s ready to move, and how to make those transitions without compromising the customer experience.

For the first 9–12 months, a significant majority of your work will focus on our growing BPO partnership. You’ll identify opportunities to expand the work we deliver through that partnership, build the operational and financial case for doing so, align CX leadership around those recommendations, and lead approved transitions from initial scoping through stabilization.

Over time, the scope will broaden. You’ll apply the same thinking across our wider service delivery ecosystem, helping us evaluate when work should enter an incubation model, when it is ready to graduate, and whether its next home should be Core Support, a specialized team, an outsourced partner, AI-powered tooling, or another model as our capabilities evolve.

You won’t be the sole decision-maker on where work lives. Your role is to develop the recommendation: bring together the data, customer impact, operational realities, and tradeoffs; build a compelling case; and help CX leadership reach a well-informed decision. Once a direction is approved, you’ll own the program that turns it into reality.

This is a role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. You should be equally energized by building a strong argument for how our service delivery model should evolve and by working through the operational details required to make that change succeed.

In this role, you will:

jobs.description:
In 1954, architect Eero Saarinen designed a radically modern bank branch for Irwin Union in Columbus, Indiana. With glass walls, no private offices, and a floor plan that invited openness, it embodied a new kind of transparency in finance. The building was surrounded by trees, furnished by Herman Miller, and featured rustic brick flooring. Today, that space is a conference center, and that spirit of design-forward thinking in banking* feels all but extinct.

Mercury believes that level of care and craft in design has been lost in modern finance, and we’re building products that bring it back. Cards and credit are built on complicated systems and inherited conventions, but our customers shouldn’t have to experience that complexity. We believe thoughtful design can turn something traditionally transactional into an experience that feels simple, intuitive, and distinctly Mercury.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Cards Credit team. You’ll tackle complex product problems, question inherited assumptions, and shape experiences that help startups spend less time banking and more time building.

In this role, you’ll:
• Own meaningful Cards Credit product problems from initial framing through shipped experience, partnering closely with Product and Engineering to understand the problem and shape what we should build.
• Turn complicated systems, requirements, and edge cases into experiences that feel remarkably simple and intuitive.
• Work across the entire design stack, from framing problems and exploring concepts to workflows, detailed interactions, visual design, prototyping, and final implementation.
• Explore broadly and design from first principles, questioning inherited patterns and assumptions when a better answer may exist.
• Bring a high level of interaction and visual craft to the Cards Credit experience, from the structure of a workflow to the details of hierarchy, typography, motion, and state.
• Collaborate with Mercury’s Brand team on physical cards and related products, creating a cohesive experience between the objects our customers hold and the product experiences surrounding them.
• Develop a deep understanding of our customers, communicate the reasoning behind your decisions clearly, and work through tradeoffs with your partners to arrive at the strongest solution.

What you’ll bring:
• A strong portfolio of product work demonstrating exceptional product thinking, interaction design, and visual craft.
• An ability to understand complicated systems and turn them into simple, thoughtful product experiences.
• Deep curiosity about why a problem exists before deciding how to solve it, with a willingness to question assumptions and work from first principles.
• Real ambition for the work itself. You want to do the best work of your career here, and you’re energized by being surrounded by people who hold themselves to the same bar.
• A high bar for craft and the judgment to know where additional thought and detail meaningfully improve an experience.
• Comfort navigating ambiguity and taking ownership without waiting for every requirement to be defined.
• A habit of exploring multiple possibilities, prototyping ideas, and changing direction when a stronger solution emerges.
• Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to articulate your thinking, explain tradeoffs, and build conviction with Product and Engineering partners.
• Deep care for customers and an ambition to create products that don’t just function well, but genuinely make their lives better.

You don’t need a background in banking, fintech, cards, or credit. We care much more about whether you’ve demonstrated the ability to understand complicated problems and turn them into simple, thoughtful product experiences.

Complexity can be learned. The instinct to find its essence is harder to teach.

In the days after the 1906 earthquake and fire destroyed most of San Francisco, the city's banks stayed shut, their vaults too hot to open for weeks. Amadeo Giannini, who ran the small Bank of Italy, did the opposite. He set up a makeshift desk on the wharf, a plank laid across two barrels, and began lending. Most of his customers were shopkeepers, fishermen, and tradespeople who had lost everything, including any papers proving who they were. So Giannini lent on a signature and a handshake, betting on the people in front of him. Those loans helped rebuild the city block by block, and, the story goes, every one of them was paid back.

That's the promise of a business loan: capital, offered fairly and fast, to people with the will and the plan to build something. More than a century later, too many growing businesses still hit a version of the closed vault: slow processes, opaque decisions, and paperwork that arrives too late to matter. 

At Mercury, we're building lending products that give growing businesses fast, fair, transparent access to the capital that lets them say yes when it counts. In 1949, as Diners Club tells it, Frank McNamara finished dinner in Manhattan and found his wallet at home in another suit. His wife came down and paid. He returned to the same table the following February and settled the bill with a piece of cardboard, honored at twenty-seven restaurants and carried by two hundred people, most of them his friends. A year later there were 42,000.

McNamara solved two problems at once. Acceptance: enough restaurants to make the card worth carrying, and enough diners to make it worth accepting. And credit: thirty unsecured days of it, on nothing but a signature. The networks settled acceptance decades ago. What is left is the credit, and the question of why someone carries this card rather than another one. That is this role.

Mercury is building its first consumer credit card. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to define what it is, ship it, and grow it from a first cohort into a portfolio. The scope is the credit account itself: the acquisition and application funnel, the approval experience and the underwriting decisions behind it, how the line moves over time, what the rewards are worth, and the experience of carrying the account day to day.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Mercury Command
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In 1965, an engineer in Scotland was given a mundane task with a tricky problem to it - banks wanted to close on Saturdays and still serve customers, but they didn’t know how to solve the authentication of the right user. James Goodfellow, working at Smiths Industries, uncovered the insights that you needed something you have (a card) and something you know (a PIN). Because someone told him they could only remember 4 digits instead of his proposed 6, today over 3 million ATMs use a card+4 digit PIN over 60 years later. 

Like the ATM, Mercury is building technology that pushes forward financial interfaces for the long term. Command is Mercury's LLM-powered financial assistant, launched to all customers in June
2026. It lets users understand their finances and take action in plain language, from asking about cash flow to sending payments, issuing cards, and managing invoices. With the product now in customers' hands, the work is to evolve it, extend its capabilities, and find new ways to leverage LLMs to give Mercury customers a more powerful banking* experience.

What you'll do

Ship new capabilities users love:
• Design and ship new Command skills, the domain-specific instruction sets that teach the model how to handle workflows like sending money, managing invoices, and understanding cash flow
• Design and build agentic workflows in Command, defining the architecture for how multi-step agent interactions should work as we extend what the product can do on a customer's behalf
• Work with backend teams to define tool schemas for new capabilities, shaping the data contracts between Mercury's business logic and the model
• Own new capabilities end to end, from the system prompt to the frontend component that renders the response

Own the LLM layer:
• Maintain and evolve Command's prompt architecture: the system prompt, skill loading system, session context, and the policy and compliance layers underneath
• Tune model behavior: reasoning effort, prompt caching strategy, fallback chains, and the streaming patterns that make the product feel fast
• Stay current with how models are evolving and bring that knowledge back to how Command is built

Build quality in:
• Write and expand Command's eval harness, adding cases that cover new capabilities and scoring rubrics that detect regressions before users do
• Partner with product and compliance teams to define what "working correctly" means for each new capability, then build the tests that prove it
• Own the reliability and quality of what you ship, from initial design through post-launch monitoring

This list is illustrative. Command is a product in motion and priorities will shift as we learn. The right person will help choose the next highest-leverage work.

The ideal candidate
• Has 7 or more years of software engineering experience, with deep technical expertise building and scaling LLM-powered applications in production
• Has gone beyond shipping a first version: you have scaled an LLM-powered product, dealt with the reliability and performance problems that come with real usage, and made it better over time
• Has experience designing agentic systems and has opinions about how to architect multi-step workflows that are reliable, explainable, and safe to run on behalf of real users
• Has built eval infrastructure and can write cases that actually measure whether the product works, not just whether the model outputs something plausible
• Understands the real tradeoffs in LLM deployments: latency, cost, compliance, and what breaks in production that doesn't show up in demos
• Has opinions about what makes an AI product trustworthy, not just impressive, and can build toward that bar
• Is comfortable with TypeScript and willing to learn Haskell for backend tool work, or already comfortable with both
• Can work across the full stack of an AI product, from the system prompt to the streaming frontend
• Has a track record of mentoring engineers and raising the technical bar of their team

When the Tarr Steps, a footbridge assembled of heavy stones in Exmoor National Park in England, washed away in a flood in 1942, the Royal Engineers rebuilt it. Then it washed away again in

You'll bring this ethos and teach others how to live it too.

The backbone of any technology org is its infrastructure, come join the team giving that skeleton superhuman abilities. The Infrastructure team at Mercury is an enablement lever for the rest of the business, building scaleable, secure and maintainable foundations for the rest of the org to build on top of.

Infrastructure is currently building out more platform features to make it easier for agents and humans to deploy code. This means security by default, observable by default and easy to use and operate. We do all this while not compromising on speed, and ship to prod all day, every day, which is a testament to the strong foundations this team has built.

We are looking for an engineer to join our team to help build out the “platform” even further! We maintain everything from networking to container orchestration, and work with product teams to enable any AWS needs they have. We want someone who is passionate about building maintainable systems, is obsessed with quality and making sure the sharp edges are filed off, and is extremely helpful when diving into problems with our product counterparts.

Someone who is just as happy debugging a strange Linux problem as they are helping a product engineer understand why their service behaves differently in production.

Some of the technology you’ll work with

Our infrastructure is built primarily on AWS, including systems like EC2, RDS, OpenSearch, ECS, and EKS. We like to use the right tool for the job and bias towards cloud native open source tooling

We use Terraform extensively to manage infrastructure as code, GitHub and GitHub Actions for version control and delivery, and Prometheus, Grafana, OpenSearch, and OpenTelemetry to understand what is happening in production.

We’re also increasingly building agentic infrastructure: systems that let AI agents safely interact with our infrastructure, and frameworks that give both agents and the humans operating them the right guardrails.

You do not need to arrive knowing every tool we use. We care more about strong fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to go deep.

As we gear up for the next stages of Mercury's growth, you will:
• Build our “Infrastructure Platform” to support the growing needs of the Engineering Organization

• Deliver key infrastructure projects, break-down complex initiatives, and define our infrastructure strategy through detailed RFCs and technical specifications

Must haves:
• You have 2+ years of experience with AWS
• You have a keen interest in cloud native open source technologies, and feel comfortable contributing code upstream to these technologies
• Strong knowledge of low-level operating system foundations (linux, file systems, containers, etc)
• You have demonstrated ability in technical writing, with at least 2 years of experience creating detailed technical documentation, RFCs, and tech specs that clearly communicate complex ideas

The ideal candidate should:
• Be used to operating in regulated environments such as HITRUST or SOC2, ensuring compliance and security
• Have 2+ years of experience working in massive terraform environments, with many engineers contributing code in a scalable way
• Have 2+ years of experience writing code. We are building an Infrastructure Platform from scratch and there is plenty of code to write to support that

The Infrastructure team sits in an interesting place at Mercury: close enough to production that the details matter, and broad enough that a good abstraction can make hundreds of engineers faster.

There is a lot left to build.

If you like infrastructure that is secure by default, observable by default, pleasant to use, and designed for people who want to ship, we’d love to hear from you.

jobs.title: VIP Growth Manager (VIP增长经理)
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Opportunity

The VIP Growth Manager will serve as a central strategy and operations partner for the VIP business. Through data analysis, user insights, and cross-functional collaboration, this role will support VIP Relationship Managers and regional teams with growth strategies and initiatives.

The ideal candidate should possess strong analytical thinking and communication skills, with the ability to identify growth opportunities from user behavior and business data, translate insights into actionable plans, and collaborate with relevant teams to drive execution and continuous optimization.

 

VIP增长经理将作为VIP业务的核心策略与运营伙伴，通过数据分析、用户洞察及跨部门协作，为VIP客户关系经理（RM）及各区域团队提供增长策略与项目支持。

我们希望候选人具备较强的分析思维和沟通能力，能够从用户行为及业务数据中识别增长机会，将洞察转化为可执行的业务方案，并协同相关团队推动落地和持续优化。

 

 

What You’ll Be Doing 

Business Insights Strategy
• Identify structural problems and opportunities in the data, such as churn signals among high-value users, differences in service needs across client segments, and the marginal return on resource allocation, and turn them into actionable strategies.
• Write business insight reports for senior management that shape VIP benefits, resource allocation, and team playbooks.

Data Monitoring
• Build and maintain the VIP core metrics framework with daily monitoring; when a metric moves unexpectedly, find the root cause and recommend actionable next steps.
• Automate recurring analyses and reports as dashboards or scheduled jobs (for example weekly and monthly reports, incentive plan results, and anomaly alerts) to reduce repetitive manual data pulls.
• Work with the Data Warehouse and BI teams to standardize metric definitions and build data tables, so the data stays accurate and traceable.

Incentive Plan Design Execution
• Design and strategise incentive plans for VIP business teams, covering metric selection, target breakdown, weighting, and payout linkage.
• Track how the incentive plans are carried out, deliver results weekly and monthly, and update the plan criteria as the business changes (for example VIP tier threshold adjustments or new market launches).

Middle Office Capability Building Cross-functional Collaboration
• Document SOPs, metric definitions, and methods for VIP growth, and drive alignment and reuse across regions.
• Act as the middle office hub between RM teams, regional markets, Product, Risk, and Finance, taking strategies through its entire lifecycle.
• Gather feedback from frontline teams and users, combine it with business data to find common needs, and help improve the product experience, service processes, and operating tools.

业务洞察与策略制定
• 从数据中识别结构性问题及业务机会，例如高价值用户的流失信号、不同客户群体的服务需求差异，以及资源投入的边际回报等，并将分析结果转化为可执行的业务策略。
• 面向管理层撰写业务洞察报告，为VIP权益设计、资源配置及团队业务打法提供决策依据。

数据监控与分析
• 搭建并持续维护VIP业务核心指标体系，进行日常数据监控；针对指标异常波动及时定位根因，并提出明确、可执行的后续建议。
• 将周期性分析及报告自动化，通过数据看板或定时任务完成周报、月报、激励方案结果分析及异常预警等工作，减少重复性人工取数。
• 与数据仓库及商业智能团队协作，统一指标定义并建设相关数据表，确保数据准确、口径一致且全程可追溯。

激励方案设计与落地
• 负责VIP业务团队激励方案的设计与策略制定，包括指标选择、目标拆解、权重设置及激励结果挂钩机制。
• 跟踪激励方案的执行情况，按周、按月输出结果，并结合业务变化持续调整方案标准，例如VIP等级门槛调整或新市场上线等。

中台能力建设与跨部门协作
• 沉淀VIP增长相关的标准操作流程、指标口径及工作方法，推动不同区域之间统一认知、共享经验并复用成熟打法。
• 作为连接客户关系经理团队、区域市场、产品、风险及财务等团队的中台枢纽，推动业务策略从制定到落地的全流程闭环。
• 收集一线团队及用户反馈，结合业务数据识别共性需求，协助优化产品体验、服务流程及运营工具。

 

What We Look For In You
• Bachelor’s degree or above, with 3–5 years of experience in user growth, strategy operations, business analytics, client operations, or a related field.
• Strong data analysis skills; proficient in SQL and able to pull and analyze data independently.
• Insight is the core requirement: able to find the key issue in the data, tell correlation from causation, and reach clear conclusions with deliberate trade-offs, rather than simply listing numbers.
• Structured thinker with strong business sense; able to break ambiguous business problems into analytical frameworks and turn them into operational actions.
• Strong drive to get things done and good at cross-team communication; able to win business stakeholders over to insights and drive execution.
• Experience using AI tools to improve analysis and productivity is a plus.
• Fluent in written and spoken English and Chinese; Chinese is used as a working language.
• 本科及以上学历，具备3–5年用户增长、策略运营、商业分析、客户运营或相关领域工作经验。
• 具备较强的数据分析能力，熟练使用SQL，能够独立完成数据提取与分析。
• 业务洞察能力是本岗位的核心要求：能够从数据中识别关键问题，区分相关关系与因果关系，并在充分权衡的基础上得出清晰结论，而非简单罗列数据。
• 具备结构化思维和较强的业务敏感度，能够将模糊、复杂的业务问题拆解为清晰的分析框架，并进一步转化为可落地的运营动作。
• 具备较强的结果推动能力和跨团队沟通能力，能够获得业务相关方对分析结论的认同，并推动方案执行落地。
• 有使用AI工具提升分析效率及工作生产力经验者优先。
• 具备流利的中英文书面及口头沟通能力，能够使用中文作为工作语言。

jobs.title: 保険事業開発（生命保険・運用再保険企画）
jobs.description:
PayPayについて/About PayPay

2018年にサービスを開始してから約8年でユーザー数7500万人を突破したフィンテック企業であるPayPayは約50の国と地域から集まった多様なメンバーで構成されています。

AIを含む最新技術とデータを駆使し、圧倒的なスピードでサービス開発と事業成長を実現します。 日本のキャッシュレス決済、またそれを使用した金融ライフプラットフォームとしての普及を一気に推進することにプロフェッショナルとして情熱を持って取り組み、ユーザーの為に新しい価値創出を共に推進する仲間を募集します。

 

業務について

▼PayPay金融事業統括本部の紹介

PayPayをNo1のフィンテック企業に。という全社のミッションを達成するため、PayPayアプリの上でお金にまつわるすべて（「つかう」以外に「ためる」「ふやす」「かりる」「そなえる」「かんりする」）のユースケースを創り上げていく実行部隊です。
スマホファーストな金融サービスのUIUXを発明していくことにもなりますので、大手金融機関での新規事業開発を経験されていた方や、商社やネット企業で実績を上げてこられた方、海外での新規事業に携わっていた方など経験やスキル・視点は様々なメンバーで構成されています。
現状の金融サービスをより良くしていきたいという強い情熱を持った人と一緒に働きたいと思っています。

組織構成：20代後半～40代後半の総勢80名ほどで構成されております。

■チームの紹介

PayPayにおける保険サービスの新規事業企画・立ち上げや、ほけんミニアプリのサービス運営を行っています。
私たちのミッションは、保険のデジタルプラットフォーマーとなり、ユーザーにとって最も利便性の高いデジタル保険サービスを提供することです。

▼関連コンテンツ
• PayPayでツクル金融のミライ_Vol. 01
• PayPayでツクル金融のミライ_Vol. 02
• PayPayでツクル金融のミライ_Vol. 03
• PayPayでツクル金融のミライ_Vol. 05
• その仕事はユーザーファーストか？業界の常識を超えた「金融」サービスへの追求
• 「ユーザーのための保険」へPayPayが業界を変えていく

▼募集の背景
PayPayほけんミニアプリは2026年7月末時点で加入者数が累計1,000万件に到達し、サービス開始4年で急速に成長しております。これまで「誰でも手軽に加入できる保険体験」を軸にサービスを拡大してきましたが、
直近ではT D保険グループとの包括的業務提携を発表し、生命保険事業への本格参入という新たなフェーズを迎えています。
 
 今後は、単なる保険販売に留まらず、
 ・PayPayならではの巨大なユーザー基盤を活かした生命保険事業モデルの確立
 ・T Dフィナンシャル生命の銀行窓販事業とPayPayを掛け合わせた、新たな価値創出・成長戦略の構築
 ・中長期で持続的に成長するための事業ポートフォリオ設計と実行
 といった、事業戦略レベルでの意思決定と推進が求められています。
 
 本ポジションでは、運用・再保険の中長期的な戦略企画や、資産運用を軸とした商品開発等に携わっていただき、PayPayと生命保険事業のシナジーを具体的な事業・サービスとして形にしていただくことを期待しています。

▼業務内容

PayPayにおける生命保険事業の立ち上げ・成長フェーズにおいて、T Dフィナンシャル生命とのシナジー創出領域を中心に、事業戦略と一体となった意思決定に携わっていただきます
• PayPayとのシナジー創出/中長期の事業企画
• 資産運用、再保険、ALM等についての戦略企画
• 資産運用を軸とした生命保険領域における新規事業/新サービス開発

▼本ポジションの魅力
• チャレンジ・失敗を推奨されている会社風土の中で、様々な0→1の事業開発を経験できる
• 7500万人を超えるユーザーに対してサービスを届けることができ、自身の仕事で世の中にインパクトを与えられる
• 他部門（プロダクト開発・マーケティングなど）との連携により、ユーザーファーストなサービス開発をする上での知見が豊富に得られる
• 経験豊富かつ多様性のあるチームの中で、事業開発における様々な視点を学ぶことができる

必要な経験/スキル
• 保険会社における経営企画、営業企画
• 当局（金融庁等）への認可申請や、法令等への対応・折衝経験
• 金融事業での勤務経験3年以上かつ卓越した成果を上げた経験
• 金融事業に関わる法令等の知識
• 戦略の立案や事業計画の策定経験
• 社内外のステークホルダーとのコミュニケーションスキル

あると望ましい経験/スキル
• 経営管理またはリスク管理経験
• 事業推進およびプロジェクトマネジメント経験
• 外部パートナー/顧客との交渉経験
• マーケットリサーチ経験
• ビジネス英語力（TOEIC800点以上）

PayPayが求める人物像
• PayPay 5 sensesに当てはまる方

待遇・条件

雇用形態
• 正社員

勤務地
• Hybrid Workstyle
※所属組織のルールおよび業務指示に応じて出社対応頂きます。

勤務時間
• スーパーフレックス制（コアタイム無し）
• 原則：午前9時～午後5時45分（実働7時間45分＋休憩時間 1時間）

給与

• 経験、スキル、業績、貢献度に応じ当社規定により決定

ベネフィット

jobs.description:
At Engine by Starling, we are on a mission to find and work with leading banks all around the world who have the ambition to build rapid growth businesses, on our technology. 

Engine is Starling's software-as-a-service (SaaS) business, the technology that was built to power Starling, and two years ago we split out as a separate business. 

Starling has seen exceptional growth and success, and a large part of that is down to the fact that we have built our own modern technology from the ground up. This SaaS technology platform is now available to banks and financial institutions all around the world, enabling them to benefit from the innovative digital features, and efficient back-office processes that has helped achieve Starling's success.

We are on a mission to find and work with leading banks all around the world who have the ambition to build rapid growth businesses, on our technology. We are looking for future leaders to come and join our team, to build client relationships, and work with them to understand their needs and how we can solve them with Engine’s technology.

Who are Engine by Starling

Engine by Starling is transforming the banking landscape with our cutting-edge core banking software. Originally developed to power Starling, our cloud-native SaaS platform is now enabling banks and financial institutions globally to modernize operations and deliver exceptional digital banking experiences. 

We are headquartered in London with offices in Dublin, Sydney and Dubai. We've recently launched in North America where we are establishing an East Coast HQ, as well as our presence in Canada. 

This role will ideally be based in the New York metropolitan area or Charlotte, NC, our preference is that you're located within a commutable distance. 

About the role

We are seeking entrepreneurial, versatile and adaptable individuals, who enjoy the challenge of a varied and collaborative role.
