jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

This is a fully remote role, for a US-licensed attorney, preferably based on the West Coast, to join Payward’s world class in-house legal department, reporting to the Global Head of Labor & Employment.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Serve as a senior member of the Labor and Employment (L&E) legal team, sharing the day-to-day workload with the Global Head of L&E and the broader team

 - Work with executive leadership, existing employment counsel, Payward Experience (PX), and other teams to develop L&E practices for rapidly growing global/worldwide workforce

 - Advise the company on worker classification issues, employee separations, executive compensation agreements, compensation plans, and wage-and-hour matters

 - Advise the company on risk mitigation for trade secret matters, and restrictive covenants

 - Support employment and labor due diligence for M&A transactions and advise on post-closing workforce integration, including harmonizing employment terms, policies, and compensation and benefits programs across acquired employee populations

 - Provide expert strategic input to the business and recruiting teams on expanding Payward’s global footprint, including EOR and direct employment decisions, transitions between EOR, direct employment, and contractor models for new markets and acquired workforces, global mobility, contingent workforce, and the related worker classification risks

 - Work closely with the PX team and business leaders to craft on-point policies and procedures, and to develop and deliver related manager and employee training, for a successful global/worldwide workplace

 - Advise on data privacy issues affecting employees and candidates

jobs.description:

Kraken’s Consumer Creative & Design team owns end-to-end creative execution for Kraken Consumer and Krak. Our disciplines cover performance ad creative, 2D and 3D design, motion design, AI video creative and web design, turning growth strategy into creative that converts across paid, owned and organic surfaces. We work closely with Product Marketing, Performance Marketing, Content & Social, Lifecycle and our regional leads, holding the line on brand and messaging quality on everything that ships.

 
 

THE OPPORTUNITY

As our Senior Performance Video Creative, you concept, produce and ship paid video for Kraken and Krak. You ideate, generate, edit and ship, and you treat gen AI as a core production method rather than a novelty. You take a project from idea to a finished, approved, multi-market asset set, and you bring a real feel for what people stop on, share and screenshot.

You report to the Creative Lead, Consumer Creative & Design, who gives you direction, feedback and cover in reviews. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. Senior here means craft and speed leadership: you set the bar for paid video on the team, work with AI-enabled processes, collaborate closely with other Krakenites in and outside the team, and are the person others come to with video questions.

 

 - Own paid video for Kraken Consumer across product launches, campaigns, promotions and always-on activity.

 - Build for channels like Meta, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Reddit and X. You know what wins where, and you build to each platform’s specs and native feel.

 - Concept and cut performance video so campaigns ship as complete cross-format sets.

 - Produce AI-generated and AI-assisted video, and know when AI is the fastest route to a great ad and when it isn’t. Keep your tooling current as the models change, and build repeatable workflows the rest of the team can reuse.

 - Bring ideas to briefs rather than executing them literally. Pitch culturally timely, internet-native concepts that nobody asked for, including experimental ones alongside BAU work, and build the winners into creative pillars we can keep using.

 - Version and localize video at scale across markets, languages, formats and regulatory requirements. In a typical month you’ll have roughly a dozen workstreams in flight at once, most spanning several formats and several markets.

 - Build creative with testing in mind. Performance Marketing owns test design, cadence and readouts. You own the creative response: reading the results, forming a point of view on why a variant won, and turning that into the next round of hooks, concepts and cuts.

 - Flex into AI-assisted paid static when a campaign calls for it, working from the team’s brand baselines.

 - Partner with Product Marketing, compliance and regional teams to get work approved without losing the idea.

 - Hold a high craft bar on your own work and keep your files clean enough for other people to build on.

 
 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years in performance video creative at a high-volume in-house team or performance agency, ideally in fintech, crypto, gaming or another regulated category.

 - A portfolio submitted with your application. Paid video above all, with the brief or objective alongside the work and the result where you’re able to share it. Include two or three full video cuts, at least one AI-generated or AI-assisted piece with a short note on what was tooling and what was you, and one concept you tested where you can talk us through what the data said and what you changed.

 - Real video skills, from concept to finished, sound-designed cut.

 - High-level command of gen AI video and image tooling, with shipped work to show for it.

 - Platform-native instincts across Meta, TikTok and YouTube. You can explain why the same idea needs a different build on each one.

 - Experience inside a structured creative testing program. You’re fluent in the metrics your creative moves (thumb-stop rate, hook rate, CTR, CVR, CPA and ROAS), you can tell a real winner from low performers, and can translate test results into a creative decision.

 - Fluency in internet and meme culture, with comedic instincts and a feel for what’s about to feel dated.

 - Speed without sloppiness. Comfortable with fast turnarounds, several review rounds and late changes.

 - Comfort working inside regulatory constraints, with work that survives risk warnings, disclaimers and market-specific requirements.

 - A solid copywriting instinct for scripts and on-screen text. Plain language, value first, no hype and no jargon.

This role ensures Legal operates as a strategic, data-driven partner to the business rather than a reactive cost center.

This leader will also be responsible for Legal’s financial, resourcing, and demand management foundations—ensuring the right work is done by the right resource at the right cost, with predictable outcomes as the organization scales.

 
 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Serve as DRI for Legal Operations, Legal Technology, and Legal AI strategy, execution, and governance.

 - Own Legal’s operating model across workflows, processes, resourcing, and service delivery.

 - Own budget planning, forecasting, accruals, and cost modeling with Finance.

 - Manage legal billing and outside counsel.

 - Lead resourcing, capacity planning, headcount modeling, role design, and make/buy/automate decisions.

 - Manage the legal technology stack (CLM, matter management, AI tools, knowledge management, intake, spend management).

 - Enforce centralized ownership, standardization, and compliance across legal technology.

 - Evaluate AI tooling, drive build-vs-buy decisions, translate requirements into technical roadmaps, ensure secure deployment, measure ROI, and lead integrations.

 - Establish metrics, dashboards, and controls for workload, demand, spend, cycle times, efficiency, risk, and outcomes.

 - Design and operate intake, triage, and demand-management frameworks, including prioritization models, service tiers, SLAs, and self-service pathways.

 - Optimize vendor and contractor management, spend controls, billing review, performance measurement, and work allocation.

 - Design, implement, and adopt AI-enabled legal workflows at scale.

 - Evolve the Legal knowledge management strategy (playbooks, templates, decision trees, guidance) for reuse and automation.

 - Prioritize operational, process, and technology initiatives based on impact, risk reduction, and ROI.

 - Lead change management, training, and adoption for new processes, technologies, and AI systems.

 - Ensure compliance with regulatory, security, privacy, and compliance standards.

 - Maintain operational controls to reduce legal, regulatory, and model risk.

 - Enable attorneys to focus on legal judgment, strategy, and advisory work.

 
 

WHAT YOU BRING

You report into engineering and partner closely with the Payward security, CISO, and compliance functions.

 - Run offensive assessments against our own platforms. Pentest the web apps, APIs, backend services, and on-chain components, and build the tooling to do it repeatedly rather than once.

 - Continuously assess posture. Threat-model new and existing systems, review architecture and key-management flows, and maintain a living view of the risks and their mitigations.

 - Review code for security. Be a default reviewer on changes touching auth, cryptography, custody, signing, and fund movement across our chains.

 - Harden the platform. Improve secrets handling, IAM and least-privilege, dependency and supply-chain hygiene, and detection and logging for security-relevant events.

 - Secure custody and signing workflows. Review and harden transaction signing flows, MPC and HSM integrations, signer permissions, admin roles, approval policies, and break-glass procedures.

 - Contribute to product engineering. Pick up regular backlog work in TypeScript so you stay close to the codebase you are defending.

 - Support incidents. Help with detection, triage, response, and post-mortems, and feed the lessons back into the program.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - An engineer first. You write and review production code comfortably, TypeScript and Node.js in our stack, and you understand systems deeply enough to break them.

 - Strong application and infrastructure security fundamentals. The OWASP-class vulnerability landscape, authn and authz, injection, SSRF, supply-chain risk, and secure design. You have done real offensive work in pentesting, vuln research, or red-team.

 - Applied cryptography and blockchain security. Symmetric and asymmetric primitives, hashing, signatures, and key management, plus the security model of EVM, Solana, and ideally TON or Tron. You can read a smart contract and reason about how it fails.

 - Ownership. You can take an ambiguous security item, an audit, a questionnaire, or an incident, and drive it to closure without being managed through it.

 - Clear communication. You can explain a risk to engineers, to a CISO, and to an auditor, and tailor the message to each.

 - An automation instinct. You do not want to catch the same issue manually twice, so you turn findings into tests, alerts, controls, documentation, or platform improvements.

 - Risk judgment. You can tell a theoretical issue from a material one, and communicate severity, likelihood, impact, and remediation tradeoffs clearly.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience commissioning or remediating third-party smart-contract audits.

 - Familiarity with custody and signing infrastructure such as HSMs, MPC, and ForDefi-style providers, and with on-chain transaction security.

 - Cloud security depth in GCP or AWS, IAM, and container and runtime hardening.

 - Detection engineering and security observability, including SIEM and log-based detections.

 - Develop and maintain Python and SQL pipelines for transaction data preparation, feature engineering, and detection workflows

 - Evaluate detection rules and analytical models across coverage, alert quality, threshold sensitivity, and the impact of proposed changes

 - Design reproducible evaluations on historical data that account for limited labels, class imbalance, and shifts in customer behaviour over time

 - Own testing, deployment, scheduling, monitoring, and operational support for detection workflows, including investigating data quality issues, pipeline failures, and unexpected changes in detection results

 - Execute historical backfills with clear validation and traceability, and maintain reliable downstream alert delivery and integrations with compliance systems

 - Be at the forefront of data innovation by experimenting, testing hypotheses, and translating insights into action, while incorporating software engineering best practices into pipelines and dashboards.

 - 7+ years of experience in data analysis, data science, and data management within the fintech, crypto, financial services, or gambling industry, gained in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

 - Experience working with compliance, fraud, funding, finance, and customer support teams and analyzing large datasets, engineering features, and applying statistical methods to practical business problems

 - Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience building and supporting production data or analytical systems

 - Hands-on experience using dbt or similar tooling to model and organize high-fidelity data for reporting and decision-making

 - Experience setting up and managing data pipelines with a strong understanding of workflow orchestration, plus strong software engineering practices including version control, automated testing, code review, and CI/CD

 - Solid statistical foundation; ML exposure is a strong plus

 - Proficiency with BI and data visualization tools (e.g., Hex, Tableau, Power BI, or similar) to build executive-facing dashboards

 - Ability to investigate production issues independently and communicate technical findings and uncertainty to non-technical stakeholders

 - You believe wholeheartedly in the values outlined in Kraken's Tentaclements document

 - A degree in a field emphasizing analytical rigor, such as analytics, software engineering, statistics, or economics

 - Based in Canada, the US, or Brazil, and fluent in English

 - Fraud detection, AML, anomaly detection, or other risk applications

 - Experience with Athena, Trino, Kafka, and Kubernetes alongside the core Airflow/dbt/S3 stack

 - Working with sparse or delayed feedback from investigations to evaluate and improve detection

jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken is on a mission to build the most trusted bridge between crypto and traditional finance. The Financial Systems Engineering team connects activity across products, payments, banking, and digital assets to the data, ledgers, controls, and applications Finance relies on. Our engineers bring expertise in data engineering, complex transaction flows, financial systems, and reconciliation. We partner with Treasury, Accounting, Tax, FP&A, Product, Risk, Security, Compliance, and platform engineering to make financial data reliable, explainable, and auditable.

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Report to the CFO and lead the engineering vision for Kraken’s financial systems, translating Finance priorities into a clear technical strategy and delivery roadmap

 - Assess the current landscape, including fragmented data, processes, and technical debt. Define a target architecture and phased transformation plan based on evidence, business needs, and sound engineering judgment

 - Lead, coach, and grow a team of specialists across financial systems, data engineering, integrations, and ledger-related services. Establish clear ownership and develop technical leaders

 - Set standards for the completeness, quality, lineage, and ownership of financial data, from source events through transaction and balance records, reconciliation, accounting, and reporting

 - Contribute to architecture decisions for ledgers, subledgers, financial data models, APIs, and integrations across fiat and crypto activity. Determine what should be standardized and where distinct product flows need governed treatment

 - Partner with Accounting and Treasury to improve account and legal entity attribution, financial controls, reconciliation, exception handling, and the traceability of records across internal and external systems

 - Lead modernization and migration without disrupting close, reporting, fund movements, or other critical Finance operations. Define validation checkpoints and criteria for retiring legacy processes and systems

 - Establish end-to-end testing, documentation, observability, release controls, and incident response practices that account for the financial impact of upstream changes

 - Partner with Product, platform engineering, Risk, Security, Compliance, Tax, and Legal on system boundaries, access controls, resilience, regulatory needs, and auditability

 - Evaluate build, buy, and integration options; review consequential designs; and communicate architectural decisions, sequencing, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to Finance and Engineering leaders

WHAT YOU WILL TACKLE FIRST

In your first year, you’ll build the foundations for a more reliable, scalable Finance architecture:

 - Move key reconciliations from a monthly to a daily cadence, with clear ownership and a process for resolving exceptions

 - Reduce the time needed to find the root cause of reconciliation breaks from weeks to days

 - Map and validate the source tables and transformations that actually feed financial statements, establishing lineage and ownership

 - Complete the UAT data lake connections needed to test financial data flows end to end before changes reach production

WHAT YOU BRING

 - Significant software engineering and technical leadership experience, including leading experienced teams through complex financial systems or data architecture change

 - A strong track record of hiring, coaching, and developing specialists while creating clear ownership, high engineering standards, and effective cross-functional partnerships

 - Deep understanding of ledgers, subledgers, double-entry concepts, reconciliation, settlement, and the path from an operational event to an auditable financial record

 - Experience with crypto or digital asset infrastructure and the challenges of connecting on-chain activity, internal balances, custody or wallet flows, and traditional financial systems

 - Strong technical judgment in distributed systems, data engineering, APIs, event-driven processing, and integrations across complex platforms

 - Experience defining a target architecture and delivering a transformation roadmap across fragmented or legacy systems while sustaining production reliability

 - Experience designing for data completeness, accuracy, lineage, reconciliation, access control, and auditability

 - Sound judgment in production operations, including incident response, monitoring, debugging, change management, and reliability improvements

 - Ability to partner with senior Finance and Engineering leaders and translate financial, operational, and control needs into a practical engineering roadmap

 - Ability to lead experts and make informed architecture decisions without needing to be the deepest specialist in every domain; clear communication of priorities and tradeoffs to executives and technical teams

 - Experience with Rust, TypeScript/Node.js, or Python; finance applications such as NetSuite, Kyriba, or BlackLine; and SOX or SOC control environments is valuable

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken's engineers build a lot of software. Developer Platform AI builds the AI systems they use to do it: agents that write and review code, simple access to the best models in the tools they already use, and the infrastructure that connects AI to our internal systems.

This is a small team with a lot of reach. The tools you ship will change how engineers across Kraken work every day, and you'll see that happen directly. The work spans agent platforms, code review, LLM routing and cost controls, MCP integrations with tools like Slack, Jira and GitLab, and the security and observability that make all of it safe to run.

If you want to work on applied AI with real users from day one, this is that job.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - LLM traffic doesn't behave like normal API traffic. Requests are long-running, streaming and expensive. One prompt can cost a few cents or a few dollars. One team's burst can burn another team's budget. Providers change their rate limits, failure modes and pricing without warning. Running this well is a problem few companies have solved, and it's the job.
 
 - Own the reliability of the platform engineers depend on: the AI Gateway, the agent runtime and the connections to internal tools. Set the SLOs, own the error budgets and decide what happens when they're spent.
 
 - Design resilience across model providers: routing, failover, retries, rate limiting and graceful degradation when a provider is slow, throttling or down.
 
 - Make LLM traffic legible. Build observability that shows latency, errors, token usage and cost by team, model and use case, so engineers can see what their workloads cost and where they're spending their time waiting.
 
 - Treat capacity and cost as one problem. Routing decisions affect both latency and spend, and you'll own the tradeoff directly.
 
 - Work with Security, Finance and AI governance to put access controls, budgets, audit logging and data handling into the platform, not into a spreadsheet next to it.
 
 - Lead incident response and blameless post-incident reviews. Turn what breaks into fixes that stay fixed.
 
 - Automate operations with infrastructure as code, safe deployments and progressive rollouts, so the platform gets more reliable as it grows rather than more fragile.
 
 - Mentor engineers and raise the operating standard across the team.
 
 This is a Staff role. You'll set the technical direction for how the platform runs, not just keep it running. The platform is small enough that your decisions shape it directly, and used broadly enough that they affect every engineering team at Kraken.
 
 

SKILLS YOU SHOULD HODL

 - Extensive experience in site reliability, infrastructure or platform engineering, with a track record of owning high-traffic, business-critical services in production

 - Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes, a major cloud provider and infrastructure as code such as Terraform

 - Strong command of SLOs, observability and incident management, and the judgment to know which reliability work actually matters

 - Proficiency in Rust or Python, and comfort reading and changing a production service's code

 - Experience with API gateways, reverse proxies or traffic management: load balancing, rate limiting, failover and caching

 - Experience operating multi-tenant internal platforms, including authentication, authorization and per-tenant cost controls

 - Staff-level influence: you set direction across teams, write clear design documents and bring other engineers with you

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience operating LLM gateways or integrating LLM provider APIs at scale: streaming, token-based rate limiting, model routing and caching

 - Experience serving models yourself, including vLLM or Ray: GPU scheduling, batching, autoscaling and cost per token

 - Experience building Kubernetes controllers or operators with controller-runtime or kubebuilder

 - Experience with Consul and Vault for service discovery, configuration and secrets

 - Experience with model evaluation pipelines for catching quality regressions before and after rollout

 - Familiarity with coding agents and agent harnesses, and running them safely in sandboxed environments

 - Experience with cost attribution, budgeting or FinOps for usage-based services

 - Background in security-sensitive or regulated environments such as financial services or crypto

 - Contributions to open-source gateway, proxy or observability projects

jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform.

We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference.

 - Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks.

 - Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete.

 - Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises.

 - Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance.

 - Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams.

 - Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions.

 - Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 8+ years operating and evolving production database estates at scale. You have assessed inherited systems, set technical direction and delivered improvements with engineering teams, and can explain how those decisions held up over time.

 - Strong understanding of high availability, replication and distributed database failure modes. You can explain consistency and availability trade-offs and reason about transaction boundaries and reliable event delivery, including transactional outbox patterns.

 - Deep, recent hands-on MariaDB expertise, including InnoDB, MVCC and transaction isolation, locking, query optimisation, binary logs and MariaDB GTID replication. You can explain the mechanisms and diagnostic evidence behind your decisions.

 - Personal ownership of MariaDB incident diagnosis, performance tuning and tested restore or point-in-time recovery. You can explain what you did, how you established data integrity and what remained uncertain.

 - Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, Rust or a comparable language. You have personally built and maintained production software or automation for database workflows such as provisioning, failover, online schema changes and self-service operations, using version control, code review and delivery pipelines, with tested failure handling.

 - Strong low-level Linux, Kernel, storage and networking fundamentals, with the ability to investigate problems beyond the database process.

 - Clear written technical judgment and demonstrated delivery across teams without reporting-line authority. You help stakeholders make sound database design and lifecycle decisions, and develop experienced engineers through shared delivery.

 

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience operating databases in containerised, hybrid on-premises/cloud or multi-region environments. Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code or GitOps, including their operational trade-offs.

 - Experience with database proxies or load-balancing layers (MaxScale, HAProxy, ProxySQL, or similar).

 - Experience with PostgreSQL, Vitess, TiDB, ScyllaDB, ClickHouse or internal database platforms; operational knowledge of Kafka, Redis/Valkey or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.

 - Experience in regulated environments or contributions to database engines, operators and other infrastructure software.

It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken’s world-class Security Team is growing. As we continue to scale and mature our information technology controls program, we are seeking a senior professional with a strong background in risk management to help build and operate a program designed for enterprise scale.

Kraken is seeking a Senior Risk Analyst to join the Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (SecGRC) team. Reporting to the Senior Manager of Security Risk Management, this role is a key contributor to the execution and maturation of Kraken's Security Risk Management program. You'll conduct rigorous risk assessments, produce high-quality analysis, and help build the operational infrastructure that makes the program run — all in close partnership with program leadership. This role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful and lasting impact both within Kraken and across the broader industry.

The ideal candidate is deeply analytical, process-minded, and energized by turning ambiguous risk signals into clear, repeatable, and scalable workflows. Entrepreneurial spirit and comfort with iterating quickly is a must. This is a fully remote role.

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Execute security risk assessments end-to-end — scoping, data gathering, analysis, findings documentation, and communicating results to stakeholders — in alignment with program methodology set by leadership

 - Support the development and continuous refinement of risk assessment templates, workflows, and process guides that make the program consistent and scalable

 - Maintain risk registers and ensure identified risks are tracked accurately and progressing through mitigation, remediation, or acceptance workflows

 - Assist in building and maintaining Key Risk Indicators (KRI) tracking and risk reporting outputs, translating raw data into clear, well-structured deliverables for review by senior leadership

 - Partner with technical teams including Vulnerability Management, Application Security, and Blue Team to gather risk-relevant data and incorporate operational findings into assessment work

 - Identify opportunities to streamline and automate risk processes and bring those recommendations to program leadership for prioritization

 - Contribute to the documentation and upkeep of risk program standards, procedures, and guidance materials

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Compliance, Internal Audit, Engineering, and Legal to ensure risk findings are well-contextualized and properly actioned

 - Support audit preparedness activities and risk-related reporting as directed by program leadership

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years of experience in information security risk management, cybersecurity governance, or GRC

 - Hands-on experience conducting risk assessments and owning findings documentation — not just supporting assessments, but running them

 - Strong working knowledge of risk management frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27005, PCI DSS, or DoCRA

 - Demonstrated ability to build repeatable processes — you've taken something ad hoc and made it structured and scalable

 - Strong data analysis skills; able to clean, interpret, and present risk data clearly and accurately

 - Experience contributing to KRI tracking and risk reporting for internal stakeholder audiences

 - Familiarity with GRC tools such as AuditBoard, Archer, OneTrust, or ServiceNow GRC

 - Proficient in Google Workspace; SQL and/or Tableau experience a strong plus

 - Excellent written communication — your deliverables are clear, well-organized, and don't require heavy editing

 - Self-directed and comfortable operating in ambiguity; you take direction well and run with it

 - Bachelor's degree or above in IT, Cybersecurity, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field

 - CISM, CRISC, or ISO 27001 credentials a plus; experience in fintech or regulated industries preferred

jobs.title: Security GRC Analyst, Mergers & Acquisitions
jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

We are looking for a Security GRC Lead to own security governance, risk, and compliance across Payward's acquisitions. You will be the accountable owner for bringing each acquired company from its own control environment into ours, working with the M&A Technology Team from diligence through to either full platform migration or steady-state coverage under our central program.

Payward acquires and integrates companies continuously, across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory regimes. Every target arrives with its own controls, its own maturity level and its own audit history, and every one enters our financial statement audit scope on a timeline set by the deal rather than by readiness. Today that work competes for the same people who run controls for the parent company. This role exists so that it has a dedicated owner.

This is a build role to uphold the repeatable process for assessing an acquired company against our security baseline, mapping its controls into our compliance frameworks,and setting remediation milestones a newly acquired team can realistically hit. You will then run it, deal after deal, and you are accountable for the work getting done.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Assess each acquisition target against Payward's security baseline, during diligence where deal timelines allow and immediately post-close otherwise

 - Map the acquired company's existing controls to Payward's control framework, and identify gaps against the external frameworks the entity falls under once in scope

 - Score control maturity at the entity level and document the basis for each score

 - Define remediation milestones that are achievable for the acquired team's size and maturity, sequenced by risk reduction rather than by framework order

 - Track milestones to closure and report status to Security GRC leadership and the M&A Technology Team

 - Recommend the endpoint for each entity: full migration onto Payward platforms, or uplift to a maturity level the central program can absorb

 - Load acquired-entity risks into the enterprise risk register and keep them current

 - Prepare acquired entities for inclusion in external audit scope, including evidence collection and walkthrough support

 - Act as the Security GRC point of contact for acquired-entity leadership, finance, and internal audit

 - Maintain policy coverage for acquired entities, including building entity-specific policy libraries where the parent policy set does not apply cleanly

 - Feed recurring findings back into the diligence process, so later deals are assessed against known patterns

 - Document the onboarding process so that it is repeatable and not dependent on one person

 

WHAT WILL YOU DO

 - Target Assessment
 
 - Review target security posture during diligence: control environment, identity and access management, infrastructure, third-party dependencies, and prior audit or examination history
 
 - Produce a written assessment of each target against the Payward security baseline, separating the risks that matter to the deal from those that matter to steady-state operations
 
 - Give the M&A Technology Team and deal sponsors a clear read on what integration will cost in control remediation terms

 - Control Mapping and Framework Onboarding
 
 - Map acquired controls to Payward's framework and to the external frameworks the entity becomes subject to
 
 - Identify which parent-company controls extend to the entity as they are, which need an entity-specific variant, and which have no equivalent at all
 
 - Build the entity's policy library where the parent policy set does not cover it

 - Remediation and Milestones
 
 - Set milestones the acquired team can meet, each with a date, an owner, and a stated risk reduction
 
 - Sequence work so that the highest-risk gaps close first rather than the easiest ones
 
 - Run the cadence for tracking remediation and escalating overdue or material risks Prepare proposed risk acceptances, including the rationale and compensating controls, and present them to leadership for decision

 - Program Integration
 
 - Prepare entities for external audit inclusion and support fieldwork
 
 - Keep acquired-entity risk visible in the enterprise risk register and in Security GRC reporting
 
 - Hand each entity over to central GRC coverage once its maturity supports it, with the handover documented
 
 - Integrate 3rd parties and vendors into Payward

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5-7+ years in security governance, IT risk, or compliance, including regulated financial services, fintech, or virtual asset environments

 - Direct experience onboarding an acquired company into an existing controls or compliance program. This is the core of the role

 - Working knowledge of SOX/ICFR IT general controls and what external auditors accept as evidence

 - Experience with at least two of ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, and PCI DSS, including mapping controls across frameworks

 - Ability to assess control maturity and set remediation plans the receiving team completes, including teams below Payward's maturity level

 - Hands-on delivery: you write the scope, collect the evidence, and close gaps yourself when needed

 - Sound judgment on priorities with incomplete information, and the sense to escalate decisions that need leadership

 - Ability to build working relationships with control owners in IAM, infrastructure, and engineering

 - Ability to translate control gaps into risk language that deal teams and executives can act on

 - Strong project management across cross-functional, distributed teams

 - Preferred
 
 - CISA, CRISC, CISM, CISSP, or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer
 
 - M&A or post-merger technology integration experience
 
 - Familiarity with PKM

 

WHY THIS ROLE

 - You will own a domain end to end rather than supporting someone else's. There is no incumbent process and no one else doing this work today

 - Acquisitions are one of the fastest-moving parts of the business, and security integration sits on the critical path for each one

 - You will work directly with deal teams, acquired-company leadership, external auditors, and Security GRC leadership, with visibility into how acquisitions are evaluated and closed

 - Payward is preparing for public company reporting, which means the controls you put in place at acquired entities are the ones external auditors will test

 - The scope of this role grows with the acquisition pipeline, across jurisdictions and regulatory regimes

 - You will join a remote-first, international team

jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Consumer Growth builds mobile and web experiences that help people become Kraken customers, fund their accounts, invest, earn, access new products, build wealth and stay lifelong clients. Product, engineering, design, data, and lifecycle marketing build together.

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own growth in viral, KOL- and creator-referred new transacting users (NTUs). Set aggressive NTU targets backed by a credible growth model, then beat them. Build and scale sharing, referral, and creator systems that drive 10x, then 50x growth while hitting payback targets.

 - Build sharing people find useful. Create natural reasons to pass on product value, and referral programs with modeled payback incentives, and without relying on aggressive incentives to hit targets. Make both work for the sender, recipient, and business.

 - Own the audience-to-customer journey. Build and test paths from recommendations and creator audiences to product value and a first transaction. Partner with the teams that own onboarding and core product experiences on shared journeys.

 - Own Consumer features and updates for the KOL Platform. Set the Consumer roadmap, ship features and ongoing improvements, and make measurement and commercial tools trustworthy and easy to use. Work with the teams that own KOL and affiliate relationships.

 - Build creator tools across Kraken’s app and web. Help creators, key opinion leaders (KOLs), and power referrers invite their followers and turn their audiences into valuable new transacting customers. Understand their different motivations and build with core product teams.

 - Make acquisition economics work. Own acquisition cost and gross-margin payback against clear targets, including fully loaded incentive, partner, operating, and fraud costs. Use downstream retention and revenue to judge what deserves more investment.

 - Increase virality per new transacting user and per returning user. Test ways to improve send conversion, invites per sender, and invite-to-first-transaction conversion. Improve repeat sharing and loop speed, and prove the gains create incremental valuable new transacting customers.

 - Build measurement you can trust. Validate instrumentation, define hypotheses and guardrails, and run tests that can detect meaningful effects. Separate attributed activity from incremental growth, interpret uncertainty honestly, and check that gains persist as you scale.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - You’ve personally built a product, tool, feature, or experience that spread beyond its initial audience. You can explain why it spread, your contribution, and how it acquired valuable customers.

 - Repeated success beating acquisition targets through referrals, product virality, or creator-led growth. Show the baseline, target, result, timeframe, component rates you improved, and your personal contribution. Bring evidence the gains lasted.

 - Strong growth product sense. You understand sharing psychology and the different motivations of customers, creators, KOLs, and power referrers. You combine customer research, creative product instincts, and strong UX and copy to give people a reason to participate.

 - Analytical independence. You independently investigate behavior with SQL and product analytics, validate instrumentation, and build funnel, cohort, and growth models.

 - Experimentation and commercial judgment. You design reliable tests, interpret uncertainty honestly, and distinguish attribution from incremental growth. You understand acquisition cost and payback, including downstream retention, revenue, and fully loaded incentive and fraud costs.

 - Senior ownership and hands-on execution. You set strategy, make hard priority calls, align teams without relying on reporting lines, and deliver autonomously. You use AI and working prototypes to turn original ideas into experiences people can try.

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building self-service creator or affiliate tools, revenue-share systems, or reliable partner payouts.

 - Consumer fintech, crypto, payments, or experience designing financial promotions and fraud controls.

 - Experience adapting growth journeys across markets, cultures, and regulatory environments.

About Us:

Lunar is a stealth technology company building a new type of software platform for health systems. We are on a mission to revolutionize healthcare with cutting-edge, AI-powered software designed to help every hospital deliver world-class care for their patients. Our platform is already the core backbone of health systems today, transforming clinical and operational workflows at scale with the world’s first AI-native hospital information system.

This next-generation platform is a fundamental rebuild of the information infrastructure that runs health systems. All of it – from doctors, nurses, pharmacists, lab technicians, coders, billers, supply chain, and even patients – Lunar’s software powers everything, soup-to-nuts. We believe that this mission is the moon landing of healthcare – something so consequential and ambitious that most people believe it to be impossible.

Backed by Silicon Valley’s preeminent venture capital firms, we believe in the power of a high performance team of seasoned professionals operating at the peak of their abilities. We value people who are driven, curious, have sound judgement, and care about doing the best work of their careers.

We are looking for a Clinical Workflow Informaticist on the Clinical Applications team to bridge the gap between our clinical users (such as doctors, nurses, pharmacists, physiotherapists, lab technicians) and our technology, ensuring a seamless experience with the Lunar platform. This role will provide expert guidance, training, and support to healthcare professionals, helping them optimize workflows, troubleshoot issues, and maximize the value of our platform in delivering patient care. If that sounds meaningful to you, join us and make an impact on how healthcare is delivered.

Over the next 6 months, here are some ways you can make an impact:

 - Support Clinical Users: Lead onboarding and ongoing support for new clinical users, ensuring they can effectively navigate and utilize Lunar.

 - Streamline Support Processes: Develop support workflows and documentation to improve response times and provide scalable solutions for common clinical user challenges.

 - Gather Product Feedback: Gather feedback from frontline healthcare professionals to identify pain points and collaborate with product and engineering teams to drive usability improvements.

 - Facilitate Feature Adoption: Assist in the implementation of new clinical features by providing real-world insights, testing workflows, and ensuring seamless rollout to users.

 - Hands-on Clinical Insight: Leverage your clinical experience to create solutions that support clinicians in providing better patient care while easing the documentation burden.

Your

Experience:

- Clinical Background: Ideally, you are a Nurse Practitioner (NP), Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (APRN), Registered Nurse (RN) or Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA) with nursing experience, preferably in internal medicine or a hospital setting.

 - Hospital

Experience:

Strong experience in hospital environments, with a focus on internal medicine.

 - Experience Level: A minimum of 1 year of nursing experience, with 2-3 years total experience in clinical settings.

 - Communication

Skills:

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to describe clinical workflows, train users, and collaborate across teams.

 - End-user support

experience:

Prior experience supporting clinicians or end-users with clinical technology, troubleshooting issues, and guiding best practices in a healthcare environment.

 - Attention to Detail: Proven ability to work with precision, especially when configuring clinical templates and order sets that require accuracy and compliance.

On the backend, we've embraced Elixir for its fault tolerance, concurrency, and scalability - essential for handling real-time patient data in mission-critical settings like Emergency Departments, ICUs, and Operating Rooms.

We are looking for a Staff Frontend Engineer who's excited to tackle some of the hardest interface and interaction problems in healthcare - and do it with a small, fast-moving, and deeply mission-driven team. If you care about crafting clean, robust, intuitive interfaces and want to rebuild from scratch the software that clinicians rely on every day, we'd love to talk.

Here are some deep technical problems you may tackle in your first 6 months:

 - Build a clinical design system from scratch: Design and ship a component library and design system that brings consistency, speed, and polish to every screen a clinician touches.

 - Push hospital workflows into the modern age: Rethink and rewire how clinicians move through the software - and turn confusing, click-heavy workflows into fast, keyboard-driven, intuitive experiences that clinicians love, not tolerate.

 - Render real-time clinical data, instantly: Build interfaces that reflect live patient data - vitals, orders, labs, alerts - the moment it changes, with no lag, in environments like the ED, ICU, and OR where a half-second matters. Architect the data layer, caching, and subscription patterns over GraphQL that make that possible.

 - Make interfaces that never fail under pressure: Engineer for accessibility, resilience, and performance so the UI holds up in high-stakes, high-stress settings - including degraded networks and edge cases that would break an ordinary web app.

 - Turn complexity into clarity: Take dense clinical and operational data and shape it into clear, glanceable, decision-ready interfaces for doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and administrators.

 - Define the frontend from first principles: Set the patterns, state management, and rendering architecture - balancing developer velocity against the reliability bar of mission-critical software.

Your

Experience:

- Minimum of 10 years of professional software engineering experience, with deep focus on frontend.

 - Expertise across the frontend stack including TypeScript, JavaScript, React, HTML, CSS, browser internals, rendering performance, state management and building real-time, reactive UIs against GraphQL APIs

 - Comfortable adopting new tools as needed (we use Elixir/Erlang, Phoenix, Postgres and AWS in the backend).

 - Experience with client-side data loading and management: caching, freshness, ownership, and how to optimize push updates

 - Understanding of the browser rendering cycle, how and when the DOM decides what to repaint, and the instinct to profile and optimize for a responsive, data-dense interface.

 - Well-versed in modern React patterns and functional programming principles, including advanced use of custom hooks to build performant, maintainable, and reusable component architectures at scale.

 - Deep fluency with async control flow in JavaScript (Promises, async/await) and a track record of diagnosing race conditions, ordering issues, and unhandled rejections in real-time systems.

 - Strong ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative, and innovative team environment.

 - Exceptional problem-solving skills, with a track record of tackling challenging engineering problems.

jobs.description:
ABOUT MEOW

Meow is business banking built for global crypto companies. FDIC-insured accounts through our banking partners, real yield on idle cash, and support for US and offshore entities. Everyone on the team is exceeding quota, it's time to pour gas on the fire with new tactics across lead generation, closing, and account management.

This is a quota-carrying Account Executive role based in our Soho, NYC office. You'll own deals end to end, from meeting booked to close, selling Meow to founders, CFOs, and treasurers at crypto companies. You'll work outbound, warm intros, and the NYC event circuit, with the product, the customer logos, and the team behind you.

 - Build a pipeline of crypto companies from first touch to funded account

 - Run sharp discovery and pitch Meow to skeptical, technical buyers who care about trust and social proof, not feature lists

 - 2 to 5 years in sales or BD with quota you actually carried and hit

jobs.title: Controller
jobs.description:
About Meow

Meow is a business banking platform that brings checking, corporate cards, global payments, treasury, invoicing, and accounting integrations into a single dashboard. Startups, small and mid-sized businesses, investment funds, and international companies use Meow to run their finances in one place. Banking services are provided by FDIC-insured partner banks; Meow Technologies is a financial technology company, not a bank.

About the role

Meow is hiring a Controller to own finance and financial operations across the company. You'll be accountable for the accuracy of our books, our control environment, our financial audit and SOC 1, payroll and benefits, tax, and the reporting our board and leadership use to run the business.

Today we run lean: outsourced bookkeepers handle day-to-day accounting and the monthly close, and outside CPAs handle tax. You'll direct these partners, decide what to bring in-house, and build the processes, policies, and systems our finance function needs as we grow. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants full ownership of finance at a fast-moving fintech.

What you'll do

Accounting and close

 - Manage our outsourced bookkeepers: set the close calendar, review each monthly close, and sign off on the financial statements

 - Review revenue recognition and other key accounting judgments for accuracy and GAAP compliance

 - Make sure every balance sheet account is reconciled and supported each month

 - Evaluate over time which accounting work should move in-house

Audit and SOC 1

 - Serve as the primary contact for our external financial auditors, preparing PBC lists and schedules and supporting fieldwork

 - Own SOC 1 readiness and the annual examination: document controls, coordinate testing, and remediate findings

 - Design and maintain internal controls, including approval limits, segregation of duties, and finance policies

Payroll and benefits

 - Administer payroll, including approvals, employee records, and accurate tax withholdings and filings

 - Administer health insurance and benefits, including open enrollment, broker and carrier relationships, and employee questions

 - Ensure payroll and benefits are recorded correctly in the books

Tax and corporate compliance

 - Manage outside CPAs on federal and state income tax, R&D credits, Delaware franchise tax, and state registrations

 - Own 1099 filings and keep entities in good standing, including annual reports and registered agents

Reporting and planning

 - Produce monthly management reports and the financials for board meetings and investor updates

 - Own budgeting and forecasting, and track profitability, margins, and cash flow

 - Lead finance diligence for fundraising and strategic partnerships

Finance operations

 - Oversee accounts payable, vendor payments, corporate cards, and expense management

 - Maintain stock compensation accounting, coordinate 409A valuations, and keep the cap table tied to the books

 - Manage corporate insurance renewals, including D&O, E&O, and cyber

 - Own the finance tool stack and automate manual processes

What you'll bring

 - 6+ years of accounting experience, including public accounting and time as a controller or assistant controller at a startup or growth-stage company

 - Strong command of US GAAP, including revenue recognition (ASC 606) and stock compensation (ASC 718)

 - Experience leading a financial statement audit and SOC 1 or SOX controls work

 - Hands-on experience administering payroll and benefits platforms such as Gusto, Rippling, or Justworks

 - Experience managing outsourced bookkeepers or accounting firms

 - Advanced proficiency with QuickBooks Online

 - Comfort working autonomously on a fast-moving team

Nice to have

 - CPA license

 - Experience in fintech, banking, or payments

 - Experience with treasury or cash management

 - A track record of building finance processes from scratch

 - Curiosity about AI systems and hands-on interest in using them to automate and improve Meow's financial processes

Compensation

$180K to $220K base depending on experience plus equity and benefits.

Neo's data science org sits inside products millions of Canadians already use. Data scientists, analytics leaders, and ML platform engineers work as one embedded function: production models, insight that shapes decisions, and the path from prototype to a monitored service. Not a reporting desk. Not a lab on the side.

There's a version of this work that stops at a notebook, a dashboard, or a handoff. Future roles here don't. They run from an ambiguous business question to something that actually runs — through the data, the constraints, and the commercial trade-offs.

At this level you frame the problem, ship the work, and stand behind the result. The people in this pipeline have taken models from working to reliable to material. They know a clever fit from a system the business can trust.

THE WORK

Neo is rebuilding financial services from scratch. We've shipped a full-stack banking platform (credit cards, savings, mortgages, personal loans, cash back) at a pace most financial institutions can't match in a decade. Data science is inside that loop, not adjacent to it.

The problems span credit risk, fraud, marketing and loyalty, executive decisioning, and the ML platform that keeps models alive in production. They run against real financial outcomes for millions of Canadians. Correctness isn't optional. Neither is commercial impact. The work doesn't get easier as we scale.

We don't have a handoff culture. You partner with Product, Engineering, Risk, Marketing, Finance, and operations. Models ship. Insights change decisions. You own the path from prototype to something the company can run on.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - A meaningful surface area with real business impact : risk, fraud, growth, analytics strategy, or the platform that productizes the work

 - The full loop: problem framing, method, delivery, and the validation and monitoring that keep it honest after launch

 - Standards that compound: reproducibility, metric consistency, model governance, and documentation , not one-off heroics

 - Mentorship that raises the bar: code review, experimental design, and developing the people around you

 - Cross-functional alignment. You translate. You don't throw work over the wall.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

If you're a Senior, Staff, or Principal Data Scientist, you own models end to end — design, training, validation, and production. You can defend a validation strategy to a peer who will try to break it, and explain the result to an executive without hiding behind metrics. You mentor. You don't wait for someone else to make the work real.

If you lead analytics, you are not running a service desk. You set the strategy, build the team, and move the company from reactive reporting to insight that changes decisions. You zoom out to company strategy and zoom in to the pipeline and the spreadsheet. You hold the line on metric definitions, experimentation, and quality when the business wants the number yesterday.

If you build ML platforms, you own the path from experiment to production — pipelines, observability, drift, registries, infrastructure-as-code. You make data scientists faster without lowering the bar. You've run production ML on cloud infrastructure, and you treat reliability as part of the model, not a follow-up project.

At every level:

 - Deep technical fluency in Python and SQL, and enough cloud and data-platform literacy to ship, not just present

 - Experience in fintech, lending, payments, or another regulated environment where a wrong number has consequences

 - A track record of taking things from working to reliable to growing — through ambiguity, not around it

 - Low ego, high standards: you do the unglamorous work and hold others to the same

jobs.title: Senior/Staff/Principal Software Developer
jobs.description:
SENIOR/STAFF/PRINCIPAL SOFTWARE DEVELOPER

Calgary, AB — Full-time

 

THE ROLE

Financial software runs underneath the biggest decisions people make. When it's good, it saves real money over years. When it's not, those losses compound just as quietly. Most of it was built to capture value, not create it. Neo is building the alternative.

Neo has been Canada's fastest-growing company three years running. The platform behind that growth is built entirely in-house: 150 services in production, hundreds of pull requests merged every week, tens of millions of transactions processed every month. The engineers here own their services from architecture decisions through to production. There's no QA team to hand work off to, no DevOps team to manage your deploys. You work on what matters. The priorities are real and the autonomy to execute is yours.

This role is for an experienced developer who has shipped real systems at scale, has strong opinions about how to build them, and is ready to be accountable for what goes live. Our stack is GraphQL, Mongo, Node.js, TypeScript, React, and React Native on AWS. If you've spent time at a company where good ideas died in committee and you know you could be going faster, this is the environment those engineers tend to thrive in.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Build and own services and clients end to end: API and schema design, production delivery, long-term technical health.

 - Serve as code owner for one or more repos, setting the standard for quality and architecture in your area.

 - Write thorough automated tests as a core part of how you build, not as a follow-up step.

 - Conduct code reviews that genuinely improve the work: alternative approaches, edge cases, performance, security.

 - Own your services in production: build observability in from the start: alerting thresholds, dashboards, tracing, logging.

 - Anticipate downstream risks to reliability, scalability, and security; raise them and advocate for the work to get on the roadmap.

 - Go beyond the ask: identify missing requirements, write the work that got missed, push back on scope that doesn't make sense.

 - Contribute beyond your squad: drive core tooling improvements, architect shared libraries, and mentor other engineers through deliberate pairing and code review.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You care deeply about what you do and about making banking better for everyone.

 - You've shipped production systems at real scale and can speak clearly about what the hard parts were.

 - You write tests as part of how you build, not after the fact.

 - You're opinionated about architecture, can defend a position, and can change it when the argument is better.

 - You give code reviews that actually move the work forward, not just green-check it.

 - You take production seriously. When something breaks on your watch, you fix it and figure out how to prevent it.

 - You don't wait for a ticket to find the problem. If something is missing or broken, you surface it.

 - You contribute to the people around you: documentation, knowledge sharing, mentorship.

 - You're current on your tech stack and treat AI as a force multiplier. Engineers who leverage modern AI tooling to move faster go further here.

This is not the right role if you want steady state and fully scoped requirements before writing a line. The engineers who thrive here find that kind of environment frustrating.

 

🚀 TOTAL REWARDS

As Neo continues to grow, we’re committed to offering a competitive, market-leading rewards program that reflects the impact our team members make. jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Financial software runs underneath the biggest decisions people make. When it's good, it saves real money over the years. When it's not, those losses compound just as quietly. Most of it was built to capture value, not create it. Neo is building the alternative.

As a Senior / Staff React Native Developer, you will own the experience that millions of Canadians interact with daily. We don't build wrappers or standard CRUD apps; we build ultra-responsive, highly secure, and visually flawless mobile experiences from the ground up. You will set the technical direction for our React Native architecture, bridge the gap between JS and native modules when performance demands it, and mentor engineers who are obsessed with shipping world-class code.

Our engineering teams are small by design. You'll work closely with product and design to turn complex financial mechanics into seamless, high-performance interactions.

WHY NEO

 - Small teams with real ownership: You are not managing a function inside a function. You own your services and clients end-to-end—from architecture decisions and schema design through to production. There is no separate QA or DevOps team to hand work off to; the autonomy to execute is entirely yours.

 - World-class toolset: No compromises on tooling. We treat cutting-edge tech and AI as force multipliers. You get full access to Cursor, Claude with unlimited tokens, CodeRabbit, GitHub Enterprise, Datadog, Snowflake, and AWS. MacBook Pros are standard issue—no justification required.

 - Top-tier compensation: Competitive salaries that beat the top tech companies in Canada. This role is eligible for our Short-Term Incentive Program (STIP) with cash bonuses tied directly to company milestones.

 - Generous equity: All team members receive equity through stock options that are in the money from day one. Over four to five years, total compensation at Neo outpaces what you’d make staying where you are.

 - Unmatched career velocity: Engineers at Neo should be able to walk into a lead or management role at any company in Canada after serious time here. That’s the standard we hold.

 - Proven hyper-growth: Three consecutive years as Canada’s fastest-growing company on the Deloitte Technology Fast 50™. We have raised $400M+ and serve over one million customers on a platform built entirely in-house.

Full relocation support is available for candidates moving to Calgary. We provide comprehensive health benefits from day one, 21 days PTO, and a maternity/paternity leave salary top-up.

 - Ship End-to-End: Write clean, modular, and highly testable code. You own your features from initial architectural design through deployment to the App Store and Google Play.

 - Technical Leadership: Set the standard for mobile engineering excellence. You will lead technical design reviews, champion automated testing (unit, integration, and e2e), and mentor junior/intermediate developers.

 - Minimize Friction: Help optimize processes. Stay close enough to the codebase to maintain absolute technical credibility while operating at a strategic level.

Experience:

You have at least 7 years of software engineering experience, with a heavy emphasis on building and scaling complex production mobile applications.

 - Architecture Mindset: You understand state management at scale, mobile security best practices (storage, biometrics, cryptography), and how to build resilient offline-first or highly cached experiences.

As a full-time team member, you share directly in the upside of one of Canada’s fastest-growing companies. When we win, you win — with real ownership and meaningful long-term wealth-building potential tied to our success.

You've built and scaled systems that handle meaningful transaction volume or data throughput. You've worked in financial services, payments, or another regulated industry where correctness isn't optional. You've had primary technical ownership of systems that matter shaping the architecture, not just implementing against it.

Tech stack is not a filter. We care that you can operate across the full stack, from front-end interfaces to back-end APIs and infrastructure.

We're looking for rare people and we won't compromise on fit to move fast. This posting is intentionally ongoing, we keep a pipeline of exceptional candidates and engage directly when the right opportunity opens.

ROLE DESCRIPTION

Novo is seeking a highly experienced and motivated product manager to own and scale our core banking experience — the accounts, money movement, cards, and program infrastructure that power banking for over 250,000 small businesses. This role is critical to ensuring the reliability, usability, and depth of the products at the heart of Novo, supporting our rapidly expanding customer base and business operations. The ideal candidate is a hands-on product leader who can set product direction for complex, regulated financial products, partner closely with Engineering, Design, Risk, and Compliance, and work hand-in-hand with banking partners to ship reliable, secure, high-quality experiences within a dynamic, regulated fintech environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES

PRODUCT STRATEGY & LEADERSHIP

 - Own the strategy, roadmap, and execution for Novo's core banking products, including deposit accounts, money movement, cards, and the underlying program infrastructure.

 - Balance near-term delivery with the platform and product depth investments needed to support long-term growth and retention.

BANKING PRODUCTS & MONEY MOVEMENT

RELIABILITY, RISK & COMPLIANCE

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL PARTNERSHIP

 - Communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, from individual contributors to the executive team and board.

STRATEGIC PLANNING & EXECUTION

 - Contribute to strategic planning for future product needs and the broader company roadmap.

 - Define and track the product metrics that matter, including activation, engagement, retention, multi-product adoption, and reliability, holding the organization accountable to outcomes.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrable track record of shipping reliable, customer-facing products in a high-growth, regulated environment, ideally involving money movement, payments, cards, deposits, or other financial infrastructure.

 - Strong understanding of banking and fintech fundamentals, including how accounts, money movement, cards, deposits, and partner-bank and program infrastructure work together.

 - Proven ability to partner with and influence Engineering and Design, write clear specs, and ship high-quality software on a predictable cadence.

 - Strong analytical skills and fluency with product and cohort data, with the judgment to know when data is conclusive versus directional.

 - Experience working with Risk, Compliance, and Legal to ship products within regulatory constraints, and a track record of treating security, trust, and reliability as core product requirements.

 - Strong product sense and the ability to give products a clear point of view and value proposition for a defined customer.

 - Proven ability to manage complex cross-functional initiatives and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including leadership.

 - Strong problem-solving skills and a proactive, data-driven approach to product.

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving startup environment.

 - Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or relevant technical background preferred.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on product leader who combines platform and tooling depth with a growth mindset: someone who can own complex product workflows end-to-end, run rigorous experimentation, and is comfortable getting their hands dirty in LLMs. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role at the intersection of product tooling, ecosystem connectivity, and customer activation.

RESPONSIBILITIES

DDA ONBOARDING & ACTIVATION FUNNEL

 - Own the DDA application, signup, and account-opening funnel — driving activation in the first 90 days of a customer's tenure by reducing friction, improving conversion, and getting customers to their first meaningful transaction faster.

 - Run a steady cadence of onboarding and activation experiments using tools like LaunchDarkly, managing incentives, in-product moments, and lifecycle prompts that create compelling reasons for customers to deepen their engagement with Novo.

INVOICE WORKFLOW & TOOLING

 - Own the end-to-end invoice experience creation and scheduling, PDF generation, branding and customization, reminders, dispute handling, payment collection via multiple rails, and reconciliation driving adoption as a core SMB financial tool.

 - Identify and ship improvements that make the invoice workflow more intelligent: smart reminders, automated reconciliation, AI-assisted invoice creation, and workflow automation that reduces manual effort for busy business owners.

INTEGRATIONS & CONNECTED PLATFORM

 - Own Novo's integration ecosystem across revenue (e.g., Stripe, Square), accounting (QuickBooks, Xero), payroll (Gusto), and utilities (Slack, Zapier) deepening existing integrations from basic data sync to richer, bidirectional workflows.

 - Lead the vision for a Novo API strategy that enables LLM and third-party connectivity, allowing customers to query their banking and financial data through external AI assistants and business tools, while identifying new integration opportunities that address core SMB financial workflows.

 - Design, run, and scale a rigorous experimentation program across the platform — covering onboarding flows, invoice tooling, and integration adoption — with clear hypotheses, measurement plans, and ownership of outcomes.

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL PARTNERSHIP & EXECUTION

 - Partner with Engineering, Design, Data, and Marketing to ship platform improvements and productionalize experimental wins into durable, scalable features — running a consistent operating cadence that surfaces friction early and optimizes for the global maximum.

 - Deep familiarity with SMB customer needs, financial workflows invoicing, accounting, payments, cash flow and the small business software ecosystem; recognized as a domain resource who can guide teams on what matters and why.

 - Proven ability to turn customer insight into product decisions: experience running discovery, synthesizing qualitative and quantitative signals, and making prioritization tradeoffs that are defensible with data and grounded in user reality.

 - Strong data proficiencyable to write clear measurement plans, instrument funnels, evaluate experiment results, and distinguish conclusive from directional signals with hands-on experience running A/B tests using modern tooling (e.g., LaunchDarkly, Amplitude, Mixpanel, or similar).

 - Technical acumen sufficient to partner effectively with engineering: comfort with API concepts, integration architecture, and the ability to write clear specs and make informed tradeoff decisions without being the one writing the code.

 - Practical experience using AI tools to accelerate product work generating content, analyzing data, prototyping features with sound judgment about where AI adds real value and where it introduces risk, particularly in a regulated financial services context.

 - Experience shipping in a regulated environment, working with Risk, Compliance, and Legal to meet security, privacy, and financial services standards.

 - Strong communication and cross-functional stakeholder management skills; comfortable presenting to leadership and aligning teams around platform decisions in a fast-paced, ambiguous startup environment.
