 - Experience training, validating, and tuning models, with solid understanding of overfitting, bias-variance tradeoff and evaluation metrics

 - Understanding of the ML model lifecycle, from training and evaluation to deployment and monitoring

 - Ability to write efficient SQL queries and work with analytical data environments

 - Strong communication skills to collaborate with both technical and business stakeholders

 - Passion for building high-quality, production-grade models

NICE TO HAVE

ABOUT THE ROLE 

We are looking for a professional to join our Fixed Income Operations team. This is a strategic position, essential to ensure that investment operations are conducted with fluidity, efficiency, and security, in strict compliance with the best market practices. This professional will act as a link between the business, product, and engineering areas, ensuring the alignment and integration of deliverables with a very innovative vision, we want to do things differently. Their performance will be crucial to maintain high standards of governance, mitigate operational risks, and sustain excellence in all routines. We are looking for someone who is committed to quality and is eager for innovation, contributing to the exponential and sustainable growth of the investment area and to the mission of offering high-quality products and services to our clients.

YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR 

 - Supervise and ensure the correct functioning of operational routines, ensuring fluidity, efficiency, and security in all processes.

 - Partner with leadership to guide and engage the team, promoting an environment of development and autonomy. 

 - Ensure compliance with internal policies and external regulations, addressing regulatory matters and keeping up to date with the rules and requirements of the financial market.

 - Develop and implement efficient operational processes and controls, in collaboration with the engineering team and other stakeholders.

 - Actively participate in defining the area's roadmap, ensuring project alignment with product and engineering teams.

 - Actively participate in risk management and mitigation of potential failures, with a focus on governance and operational excellence.

 - Collaborate with other areas such as Compliance, Legal, and Operational Risk, ensuring integration and adherence to internal processes.

 - Manage the systems used by the area, ensuring correct configuration and access to them, in addition to deeply understanding the functioning of investment systems.

 - Conduct activities related to the settlement and processing of fixed income assets, with an emphasis on private credit, financial events, and custody.

 - Participate in the resolution of operational problems and incident investigations, providing necessary support and information, including in internal and external audit processes.

 - Support the implementation of new financial products, contributing with their technical knowledge in fixed income assets and custody operations.

 - Supervise and ensure compliance with control action plans, ensuring resolution within established deadlines.

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

 - Professional with proven experience in Operations and Fixed Income products.

 - Motivated to have innovation as their main objective.

 - Technology skills and knowledge to be able to boost discussions with product and engineering teams.

 - Programming experience with Python and SQL (will be a plus).

 - Technical mastery in fixed income assets, especially in private credit, and familiarity with the settlement, custody, and financial events processes.

jobs.title: Head of FP&A | Credit Products
jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE TEAM 

Nu's Finance organization is structured into functional areas that together safeguard financial stability, compliance and strategic decision-making. Most core finance functions operate under a dual reporting structure — reporting directly into the global Finance team, with a dotted line to the business they support — which keeps us close to the operation while holding a consistent global standard.

Within Finance, FP&A owns budgeting, forecasting and long-term financial planning, and acts as the analytical partner behind the company's biggest decisions. The team drives profitable growth by improving visibility, forecasting quality, consolidation and analysis of results and key metrics, translating them into insights and recommended actions for senior management. It also defines the performance metrics that create accountability and ownership across FP&A and the business units — tracking them consistently to measure progress, monitor KPIs and drive cost optimization.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

We are seeking a Head of Credit Products FP&A to be the finance owner for Nu's consumer and small business credit businesses across all markets – Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, the United States, and the geographies we enter next. Credit is the engine that powers Nubank's economics, and this role is the person leadership turns to when the question is how that engine actually behaves: what drives revenue, what drives losses, and how the two reconcile into a single view of each product.

The scope covers every credit product we offer, including credit card, personal loans, and other lending products, and it will grow as Nu launches new products and enters new markets. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy and consistent exposure to senior leadership, including the executives who run these businesses. You will be expected to hold a position when the analysis supports it, push back with evidence, and take direct feedback.

This role is about building as Nubank grows including reengineering how we model and forecast our credit businesses, starting with the economics of a single customer and building up to the portfolio P&L. You will also own the position Finance takes on those numbers with the Management Team. Doing that credibly requires deep, hands-on expertise in consumer credit: how portfolios originate, season, revolve, and lose money, and how pricing, underwriting, and funding decisions flow through to the P&L. Experience in Brazil, our largest market, is a plus.

You will lead a team of 15-20 finance professionals, set the standard for their work, and develop a deep talent pool, while staying close enough to the models and the data to challenge them on substance.

You’ll be Responsible for 

 

 - Own the planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting cycles for Credit Card and Lending across all markets, with full accountability for the integrity of the numbers and for the position Finance takes on them with leadership.

 - Forecast and explain the net revenue and the credit economics of each product, from net interest income, funding cost, interchange, and fees to delinquency, provisioning, and loss, so that revenue and credit views reconcile into a single, defensible view of profitability.

 - Build consumer credit P&Ls and forecasting models from first principles, using cohort and vintage analysis to reflect how a portfolio actually behaves, and model how pricing, limit, underwriting, and funding decisions flow through to each product and to Nubank's consolidated P&L.

 - Own the partnership with Risk and loss forecasting, and be the authority across Finance on the drivers of consumer credit performance.

 - Partner with the leaders of the credit businesses and a senior group of General Managers, bringing the finance perspective into growth, pricing, and portfolio decisions early enough to change them.

 - Prepare clear, concise executive materials that explain how the credit portfolios are performing, in support of budget cycles, executive reviews, and company earnings.

 - Build and lead the team: set the talent bar, coach analysts and managers, and create a succession pipeline. Decide where the team's capacity goes between recurring cycles, improvement work, and demands from across the organization.

 - Drive the use of AI, advanced analytics, and automation in planning and analysis, reinvest the capacity it releases into our expanding geographies, deeper analysis, and business partnering, and keep the judgment to review and challenge AI-generated output.

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

Required

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, Business, or a related field. An advanced degree or relevant certification (e.g., CFA) is a plus.

 - Extensive experience in consumer credit, within FP&A, credit strategy, strategic finance, or business analysis at a bank, card issuer, consumer lender, or fintech.

 - Proven track record of building P&Ls and forecasting models for consumer credit products, not only maintaining them.

 - Direct experience with credit card and consumer lending economics, including cohort and vintage analysis, provisioning, and loss forecasting.

 - Experience leading teams responsible for modeling and forecasting the financial outcomes of credit products, and developing the people on them.

 - Experience presenting to and influencing senior leadership on strategic decisions.

 - Experience launching or scaling a credit product or market within a larger financial institution is a plus.

 - Fluent English. Portuguese or Spanish is a plus.

COMPETENCES & ATTRIBUTES

 - Consumer credit mastery: you know how consumer credit portfolios behave across the full lifecycle, from origination and underwriting through seasoning, revolving vs. transacting behavior, interchange and rewards dynamics, delinquency, collections, and charge-off. You can build the P&L for a credit card or a consumer loan product from a blank page, understand how every line interacts, and find what is wrong in a model built by someone else or by an AI tool. Deep expertise in Brazilian consumer credit, gained at a bank, issuer, retail finance company, or fintech that originates and manages its own credit portfolio is a plus.

 - Unit economics and marginal decision-making: a strong command of net interest income and funding cost, interchange, fee income, cohort and vintage analysis, provisioning, and the trade-off between growth and credit quality.

 - Builder mindset: you are comfortable improving models, not only operating them, and building planning processes where none exist yet. You are at ease starting from incomplete information, making assumptions explicit, and revising them as the business learns.

 - Executive presence: you present with clarity and authority to senior executives, hold your ground on substance, and adapt when new information changes the answer.

 - Stakeholder management: you build trust-based relationships with business leaders, Risk, Legal, and Treasury, and influence decisions without formal authority.

 - Technology and AI fluency: you use modern analytics and AI tools to raise the speed and quality of the team's work, and you know where their output needs a human check.

 - Talent development: you raise the bar for the people around you through coaching, direct feedback, and the example you set.

WORK SETUP 

Location

Miami, US
Washington, US

Work model

Expected: Hybrid 2-3 times/week: Our hybrid work model brings us to the office at least twice a week, on strategic days designed to maximize team connection and collaboration. For more details, visit https://building.nubank.com/nu-hybrid-work-model/

 

OUR BENEFITS 

 - Opportunity of earning equity at Nu

 - Medical Insurance

 - Dental and Vision Insurance

 - Life Insurance and AD&D

 - Extended maternity and paternity leaves

 - Nucleo - Our learning platform of courses

 - NuLanguage - Our language learning program

 - NuCare - Our mental health and wellness assistance program

 - 401K Saving Plans - Health Saving Account and Flexible Spending Account

 - Work-from-home Allowance

 - Relocation Assistance Package, if applicable.

jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE ROLE 

We are looking for a Controllership Expert to join Record to Report within Global Service Platform (GSP). GSP provides standardized, cross-functional services that enable the rest of the bank to operate at scale. The Record team processes information from Nubank’s ledgers, translates treasury and product activity into an accounting view, supports daily close and financial analysis, and provides the control foundation for all geographies.

This is an strategic individual contributor role for someone who combines finance and controls expertise with a strong affinity for process, data, and technology. You will act as a central orchestrator across the Record organization, partnering with functional managers and senior stakeholders to manage cross-team projects, establish delivery metrics, and consolidate reconciliation goals and performance.

The role is designed for someone who can operate autonomously, bring structure to ambiguous agendas, and lead through influence without direct people-management responsibility. You will help the leadership team focus on product and service lines by creating a reliable operating system for controls, projects, metrics, and continuous improvement.

This role is based in São Paulo, Brazil, and works across a global organization serving Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, and other Nubank geographies.

YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR 

 - Manage a portfolio of cross-team Record to Report and controllership projects, translating strategic priorities into clear plans, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks, and governance.

 - Track delivery commitments and create the metrics, dashboards, and communication cadences that give leaders a clear view of progress, bottlenecks, risks, and decisions required.

 - Consolidate reconciliation metrics across processes, entities, accounts, and teams, creating common definitions for completion, timeliness, aging, breaks, materiality, root cause, and remediation.

 - Partner with process owners and managers to define reconciliation goals, leading indicators, thresholds, and action plans, and lead recurring performance reviews.

 - Identify recurring breaks, delays, and control gaps and coordinate root-cause remediation across process, data, system, and operational teams.

 - Establish scalable operating mechanisms for controls, close readiness, issue management, and follow-up to reduce dependence on manual tracking and one-off heroics.

 - Work with Finance Platform, Finance Systems, Data, Engineering, Tax, Treasury, FP&A, Internal Audit, Risk, and other partners to improve tools, workflows, data quality, and operational visibility.

 - Translate complex financial and operational topics into concise narratives, viable options, trade-offs, and clear recommendations for senior stakeholders.

 - Clarify accountability and decision rights using practical mechanisms such as RACI or RAPID when work spans multiple teams.

 - Support the evolution of Record’s operating model as new global processes, including tax compliance activities, are brought into the organization.

 - Turn successful improvements into repeatable standards, playbooks, and ways of working that can be adopted across geographies.

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

Required

 - Significant experience in controllership, accounting operations, financial close, reconciliations, controls, risk, finance operations, or a related discipline.

 - A degree in Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field. Other backgrounds may also be considered when paired with strong, relevant experience.

 - A track record of leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from an ambiguous problem statement through implementation and sustained adoption.

 - Strong understanding of processes and controls, with the judgment to balance accounting accuracy, control quality, operational efficiency, and delivery speed.

 - Experience designing metrics, setting goals, analyzing performance, identifying root causes, and turning data into decisions and measurable improvements.

 - Advanced English communication skills, enabling effective collaboration with global teams and stakeholders.

 - Practical familiarity with data analysis using Python and SQL. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you should be comfortable understanding data, working with technical partners, and using these tools to investigate and improve processes.

 - Strong stakeholder-management and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior partners without direct authority.

 - A high degree of autonomy, confidence, and ownership: someone who can take an agenda forward, bring ideas, circulate effectively among managers, and ask for support when a decision truly requires escalation.

 - Comfort working as a senior individual contributor and interested in growing through an expert career path rather than requiring formal people management.

Nice to Have

 - Experience in a technology company, fintech, bank, shared-services environment, or a global organization with complex financial operations.

 - Experience with finance systems, ledgers, reconciliation platforms, workflow tools, automation, or data products.

 - Experience supporting daily or near-real-time close, tax compliance processes, audit readiness, or multi-geography controllership.

 - Product, program, or project management experience, especially in roles that required coordinating multiple teams and turning broad priorities into execution.

 - Experience in reducing recurring exceptions, manual effort, cycle time, or rework through process redesign and automation.

 - A practical, generalist mindset: the ability to move between finance, controls, data, technology, and stakeholder problems while maintaining rigor.

Location

São Paulo, Brazil

Work model

Hybrid

Office requirement

2 days per week at the office.

 

OUR BENEFITS

 - Food/ Meal Card (Vale-Refeição and/or Vale Alimentação)

 - Public Transportation Commuting Benefit (Vale-Transporte)

ABOUT THE TEAM

At Nu, Compliance is a strategic partner—not a tollgate. We view effective Risk Management & Compliance as the engine that maintains agility and empowers rapid, responsible growth across multiple global markets. Our team partners directly with internal clients using a targeted friction approach: we focus on the most relevant regulatory risks and embed compliance directly into product design rather than distributing rules after the fact.

The Global Compliance function serves as the Second Line of Defense, responsible for the full regulatory lifecycle: tracking new regulations, advising product and technology teams, testing controls, coordinating regulatory inspections, and monitoring remediation of regulatory issues.

This role is positioned at a pivotal moment. Nu has received conditional approval for a US National Bank Charter. Reporting to the Head of US Compliance, this individual contributor will independently assess complex regulatory questions, influence product and operational decisions, and lead compliance reviews from planning through reporting and remediation validation. The role also contributes to policy development, compliance risk reporting, and advice on regulatory issues.

Success requires strong regulatory judgment, practical experience evaluating controls, and the ability to turn complex requirements and findings into clear, actionable recommendations. Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced consumer compliance professional to lead product compliance advisory engagements and internal compliance testing and monitoring across Nu’s US consumer banking products, including deposits, credit cards, and personal loans.

Reporting to the US Head of Compliance, this manager-level individual contributor will independently assess complex regulatory questions, influence product and operational decisions, and lead compliance reviews from planning through reporting and remediation validation. The role also contributes to policy development, compliance risk reporting, and advice on regulatory issues.

Success requires strong regulatory judgment, practical experience evaluating controls, and the ability to turn complex requirements and findings into clear, actionable recommendations. You should be comfortable establishing processes, managing competing priorities, and driving work to completion in an evolving business.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an experienced, curious Product Marketing Lead to help define how we launch and grow our product in the US. You’ll be the closest partner to Product and Growth teams on narrative, go‑to‑market, segmentation, and performance. You’ll shape the story, run launches end‑to‑end, and set the standard for how we communicate with customers.

You’ll join a small, ambitious team that values craft, velocity, and genuine collaboration. We test, learn, and iterate quickly — and we use AI heavily to multiply our impact. You’ll have room to drive strategy, roll up your sleeves on execution, and become a defining voice for product marketing in the US.

From day one, Product Marketing is at the table — shaping roadmaps with customer and market insight, defining full‑funnel marketing strategy, and keeping us aligned with long‑term business priorities and product success metrics. This is a high‑ownership role, building something new from the ground up.

This role is based in Miami, Florida.

 
 

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

BUSINESS & OUTCOMES

 - Own key US product marketing outcomes for your area — e.g., awareness, engagement, and adoption — with clear, measurable impact.

 - Turn company and product strategy into sharp positioning, segmentation, and GTM choices: where we play, who we focus on, and how we win in the US.

 - Use market and customer insight (quant, qual, competitive) to evolve our value proposition and influence the roadmap.

 - Translate the product story into high‑impact web and landing experiences, working with Growth and Design so our site, landing pages, and in‑product surfaces tell a consistent story.

LAUNCH & GTM

 - Lead messaging and go‑to‑market for major product and feature launches — from strategy and positioning through planning, execution, and post‑launch read‑outs.

 - Design integrated GTM plans that connect brand, product, lifecycle, and performance channels.

CHANNEL, ACQUISITION & LIFECYCLE

 - Design and run programs across in‑app, email, push, SMS, and emerging channels to drive acquisition, activation, engagement, and retention.

 - Partner with Growth on website and landing experiences — you own the story, messaging hierarchy, and marketing assets

 - Work closely with Growth so our lifecycle journeys feel coherent, on‑brand, and right for US customers.

CUSTOMER, MARKET & PERFORMANCE INSIGHT

EXPERIMENTATION & KPIS

 - Define success metrics and guardrails for launches and campaigns.

CROSS‑FUNCTIONAL LEADERSHIP & ENABLEMENT

 - Serve as a trusted subject‑matter expert, influencing senior stakeholders with data‑driven recommendations and simple, strong storytelling.

 - Build narratives, playbooks, and toolkits that make it easy for leaders and teams to tell the story the same way.

 - Create executive‑ready narratives (decks, one‑pagers, briefings) that clearly connect product, customer, and business impact.

 - High ownership — You take initiative, operate with autonomy, and naturally seek out context, partners, and answers.

 - AI‑native — You use AI daily for writing, research, analysis, and workflow automation and are eager to find new ways to go faster and deeper.

Critically, this role requires a security engineering philosophy grounded in business enablement: the conviction that security done well accelerates what the organization can do, not merely protects it. This means rigorously distinguishing between controls that reduce real risk and those that create the appearance of compliance without reducing exposure, taking genuine ownership of outcomes rather than delegating accountability through policy, and continuously questioning inherited assumptions about what security measures are necessary, sufficient, or proportionate.

 - Designing and maintaining the core identity infrastructure with the durability and operational discipline required at organizational scale: enterprise Identity Provider, PKI and X.509 certificate lifecycle automation, mutual TLS for service-to-service authentication, and credential management systems engineered to remain sound as the organization grows.

 - Translating least-privilege access from a principle into a measurable, organization-wide program — with defined metrics, visible adoption curves, and accountability structures that allow Security and Engineering leadership to track and act on the organization's access risk posture over time.

 - Designing and maintaining a security engineering framework — comprising technical mechanisms, policies, incentives, and assurance processes — that ensures security properties are durable, verifiable, and operationally sound, rather than dependent on individual vigilance or periodic audits.

 - Designing and facilitating large-scale preparedness exercises grounded in realistic attack paths — involving engineering, operations, and executive functions — to identify genuine gaps in IAM controls, not merely satisfy a compliance requirement.

ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for an outstanding AI Engineer with both a passion for design and experience architecting modern AI implementations.

Nu's design and research function is roughly 260 people. Over the past year they have been building their own tooling: something like 100 AI-assisted solutions and 30+ local knowledge repositories, each built inside a business unit to solve that unit's problem. Most of them work. None of them talk to each other.

The Design Center of Excellence exists to turn that kind of local invention into systems the whole function can build on. It has design ops and research ops. It does not have an engineer — which means the CoE can identify a need, specify a tool, and then has no one to build it.

This is that hire: the first engineer in the CoE, and the person who architects the systems that let design at Nu scale. You'll work directly with the designers and researchers who use what you build, and the person who scopes a system is the person who builds it.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

NuBrain — the first priority. A global knowledge system for the design and research function, consolidating the 30+ local repositories that already exist. The hard part is not merging content; it's the context architecture — how retrieval is structured, how token consumption stays sane, and how content reaches people and agents at the moment it's useful.

New tools that enable superlative creative marketing and brand expressions at scale. As Nu scales globally, we are inventing new ways to express our brand in the product and through our marketing. Instead of hiring fleets of marketing designers in every country, we aim to build tools that enable consistent high quality creative expression to be driven centrally.

Canonicalizing what already exists. Roughly 100 AI solutions have been built locally by designers and researchers. Someone needs to understand what they are, decide what becomes standard for the function, and retire the rest before the duplication compounds.

Deciding the shape of the answer. Plugin, MCP server, agent, Claude skill, or a full platform — that call is yours to make and defend. Part of the job is telling the CoE that the tool they asked for should be something else.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Architect and build the systems design at Nu runs on — increasingly agentic ones.

- Sit with designers and researchers, understand the need underneath the request, and turn it into something scoped and buildable.

- Stand up or reuse the infrastructure, write the code, and ship it to the function.

- Instrument what you build. Metrics and observability are part of the deliverable, not a follow-up.

- Own the roadmap for CoE tooling: prioritize, sequence, say no, and keep things moving without a PM behind you.

- Be the technical voice in a design organization — make trade-offs legible to people who don't read code.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

An outstanding, deeply experienced AI engineer. This is an engineering hire first. You've spent years building systems other people build on, and recent years working with AI models on things like token consumption, rate limiting, response latency, MCP servers, and other modern AI engineering challenges.

A track record architecting UX systems. Before AI, you designed and built the foundations of user experience at scale — design systems, component platforms, UI frameworks, front-end infrastructure used by many teams.

A love for design that shows up in your work. Since AI, you've used it to build compelling examples and more sophisticated systems than were possible before. We'd like to see them.

Agentic systems that help design scale. Ideally you've built them — agents, tooling, or infrastructure that let designers do more, faster, and better. This is the strongest signal for the role.

A protagonist. You'll serve a 260-person function as a centralized hub. That means navigating stakeholders, leading projects, and pushing work through an organization that doesn't report to you. You drive the work yourself rather than relying on someone else to run the project.

Evidence you've shipped. Send us GitHub, live tools, demos, and systems you can walk us through. We are not asking for a design portfolio.

BACKGROUNDS THAT TEND TO FIT

- Design systems and UI platform engineers at design-led product companies.

- Engineers at design tooling companies.

- Engineers who have been building AI and agentic tools for designers — in their day job, in open source, or in public.

- Founders and technical leads who were the engineer behind a design-led product.

WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT

- Not a designer who codes. The engineering bar is the bar.

- Not a generalist backend or infrastructure role. UX systems experience is core.

- Not customer-facing mobile product work. This is internal systems and tooling for the design function.

- Not a research or modeling role. (The "design modeling" profile — building the models AI consumes — is a different conversation, later.)

jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

Deputy MLRO (AML Compliance)

ABOUT US

Nu is one of the largest digital financial platforms in the world, with more than 127 million customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. Guided by our mission to fight complexity and empower people, we are redefining financial services in Latin America and this is still just the beginning of the purple future we're building.

Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: NU), we combine proprietary technology, data intelligence, and an efficient operating model to deliver financial products that are simple, accessible, and human.

Our impact has been recognized by global rankings such as Time 100 Companies, Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies, and Forbes World’s Best Bank. Visit our institutional page https://international.nubank.com.br/careers/

ABOUT THE ROLE

Nu Global AG is Nu's Swiss entity, based in Zug. It went live in October 2026 with its AML/CFT and sanctions framework already in place: entity risk analysis, internal directives, customer risk classification, monitoring and screening standards, and MROS reporting. The same team also drives the next steps of Nu's expansion in Europe.

We are looking for a senior AML professional to act as deputy to the Head of AML/CFTP & Sanctions. In 2027 you will take over the day to day MLRO duties of the Swiss entity, so the Head of AML can focus on strategy, and you will help take the framework built in Switzerland to new markets in Europe, adapting it to the new EU AML package (AMLR and AMLD6).

You will join a small, senior team where everyone owns their decisions and does the work themselves. You will work directly with senior management, the first line, our auditors and our regulators.

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Act as deputy to the AML Compliance Officer (MLRO) and stand in whenever needed

 - Run the day to day MLRO activities: escalated cases, decisions on reports to MROS under Art. 9 AMLA through goAML, and sanctions duties towards SECO, including asset freezes

 - Review and challenge the first line: sample based quality assurance of alert handling and case files, and sign off on changes to transaction monitoring rules and screening thresholds

 - Keep the framework current: entity risk analysis, internal directives and procedures, and the annual AML/CFT report to the Board

 - Issue the financial crime opinion on new products, features and material changes at the Product Risk Committee

 - Be the point of contact for our SRO, MROS, SECO and the external AML auditor, and for due diligence requests from partner and correspondent institutions

 - Own the AML/CFT training plan and the training duty under Art. 8 AMLA

 - As Nu expands in Europe, adapt the Swiss framework to the new EU AML package (AMLR and AMLD6) and turn it into binding control requirements for product, engineering and operations

WE ARE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

 - Served as MLRO, AML Compliance Officer or formal deputy at a regulated financial intermediary in Switzerland, supervised by FINMA or an SRO, or in the EU (mandatory)

 - Lives in Switzerland today (mandatory)

 - Meets the fit and proper requirements that regulators apply to AML officers (mandatory)

 - Holds the CAMS certification (mandatory)

 - Speaks fluent English, our working language, and fluent German (mandatory)

 - Has practical experience with the Swiss AML framework (AMLA, AMLO, FINMA AMLO and SRO rules, MROS and SECO reporting), the EU AML framework, or both, and a working knowledge of the new EU AML package (AMLR and AMLD6)

 - Has built or set up an AML function or framework

 - Has taken and defended reporting and freezing decisions, and has dealt directly with FINMA, SROs, other regulators and external auditors

 - Has reviewed and challenged first line controls at a senior level: transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, KYC and customer risk classification

 - Writes clearly and precisely in policies, opinions and regulatory correspondence

Nice to have

 - Sanctions expertise: screening, list management, asset freezes and reporting under Swiss and EU sanctions regimes

ABOUT THE ROLE 

We are seeking an FP&A Senior Specialist to be the finance partner for our Digital Assets organization. Today that means our crypto trading and custody business in Brazil and the digital asset products inside Nu Global, including stablecoin balances, cross-border money movement, and crypto trading. As Nubank and the Digital Assets business expands to additional geographies, you will own the finance view of this business in each market it enters.

Digital Assets is both a customer product and a set of rails. Stablecoins, FX, on and off ramps, and card spending can be a source of revenue, a cost to manage, or the reason a customer chooses us in the first place. This role is about building as the business grows, including how we model and forecast it, starting with the economics of a single customer, trade, or balance and building up to the business P&L. You will also own the position Finance takes on those numbers with Digital Assets leadership.

The scope covers every digital asset product we offer, in every market where we offer it. Economics and accounting differ by product, entity, and country, and many of the answers are still being worked out. You will decide which assumptions matter most, make them explicit, and revise them as the business learns.

You will operate with a high degree of autonomy and regular exposure to the leaders who run these businesses. You will be expected to hold a position when the analysis supports it, push back with evidence, and take direct feedback. This is a senior individual contributor role. You will stay hands-on in the models and analysis, and you will help raise the standard of work across the FP&A team around you.

YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR 

 - Own the planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting cycles for Digital Assets across Brazil and Nu Global, with accountability for the integrity of the numbers and for the position Finance takes on them with leadership.

 - Build the P&L for each digital asset product, from trading and swaps to custody and stablecoin yield, and model how volume, take rate, balances, pricing, and partner costs flow through to Nubank's consolidated results.

 - Track gross profit and cost-to-serve, including execution and liquidity costs, custody and platform provider fees, payment network and funding costs, and regulatory and audit requirements, and bring a point of view on what should change when results move.

 - Support expansion into new geographies with the financial analysis behind each launch, including unit economics, local rails and funding methods, and the effect of licensing and legal entity structures.

 - Work with Digital Assets product and business leaders early enough to shape pricing, product, and investment decisions.

 - Use AI, advanced analytics, and automation to speed up planning and analysis, while keeping the judgment to review and challenge AI-generated output.

 - You understand how money movement and digital assets make and cost money, including trading and liquidity, custody, stablecoins and yield, FX, and card and payment networks, or you have the curiosity and rigor to get there quickly.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Traffic Management team keeps Nubank’s customer‑facing and internal services reachable and secure. It is the layer that routes and protects every service request, from mobile app entry points to service‑to‑service calls across all our regions and environments. This function owns the strategy and execution for our service mesh ensuring our products can scale safely as we grow and expand. In this role, you will drive the reliability, scalability and security of this critical platform, evolving our service mesh, strengthening resilience and observability, and pushing our capabilities so that product teams can ship quickly without compromising stability.

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Deliver end‑to‑end milestones on the traffic platform, from problem definition to rollout and follow‑up, breaking complex problems into clear tasks and keeping progress and risks visible for the team and key stakeholders.

 - Take ownership of complex and sometimes ambiguous problems, analyzing options and trade‑offs, and proposing clear, pragmatic solutions that balance reliability, performance, security and effort.

 - Ensure the stability and quality of what you and the team ship: design with failure in mind, put the right tests and observability in place, and react quickly to incidents, driving follow‑ups that prevent them from happening again.

 - Collaborate with engineers, product and partner teams to understand needs, align on priorities and turn them into clear technical plans and milestones that are connected to the team’s goals.

 - Use AI and agents in an AI‑first way in your routine to investigate issues, write and review code, explore solution options and automate repetitive work, helping the squad adopt safe, effective AI workflows rather than just individual usage.

 - Create and maintain clear technical documentation and runbooks that help other engineers understand, use and operate the traffic platform with confidence, and share knowledge through reviews, sessions and participation in function‑level initiatives.

 - Help other engineers grow by giving and receiving feedback through code reviews, design discussions, pairing and day‑to‑day collaboration, acting as a reference for good engineering practices inside the team.

 - Participate in support and on‑call routines for the area, using incidents, tickets and metrics as input to suggest and drive medium‑term improvements to the platform and to how we work.

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A PERSON WHO HAS

 - Operated large-scale, high-performance synchronous distributed systems in the cloud, working directly with load balancers, reverse proxies, TLS/mTLS and routing, and using metrics, logs and traces to debug issues, optimize performance and improve overall reliability.

 - Worked hands-on with Kubernetes-based infrastructure and Infrastructure-as-Code tooling — defining and evolving manifests, routing and deployment strategies, and managing DNS configuration — with a solid understanding of how these pieces fit together to deliver resilient traffic paths in production.

 - Uses AI as part of their daily engineering workflow, leveraging AI tools and agents to investigate issues, write and review code, explore solutions and automate repetitive work, while consistently validating outputs and holding quality and safety as non-negotiable standards.

 - Led end-to-end infrastructure platform projects from design to production go-live, breaking work into clear milestones, coordinating across stakeholders, managing risks and trade-offs, and following through post-rollout to stabilize and evolve the solution.

 - Experience with Istio or other service-mesh technologies such as Linkerd or Envoy-based solutions — or legacy stacks like Finagle — designing and evolving traffic policies, resilience features and observability for service-to-service communication.

 - Worked with AWS networking and compute primitives (ALB/NLB, security groups, VPC, Route 53, IAM) in production environments, with an understanding of how these layers interact with application traffic.

 - Hands-on experience using Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Pulumi or Terraform to design, version and roll out changes to cloud and Kubernetes infrastructure in a safe, repeatable way.

 - Previously built platform capabilities or shared libraries for other engineers — abstractions, SDKs or internal tooling — that make it easier and safer for product teams to consume traffic and networking capabilities at scale.

Nu is one of the largest digital financial platforms in the world, with more than 127 million customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. Guided by our mission to fight complexity and empower people, we are redefining financial services in Latin America and this is still just the beginning of the purple future we're building.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As Senior Counsel, Regulatory Legal – Latin America, you will be the legal voice on how Nu's payments and digital-assets products can operate, launch and scale across the region. You will define where licenses, registrations or regulated entities are required, and turn that analysis into a clear recommendation the business can act on.

This is a legal and regulatory strategy role, not a compliance operations role. You will work with Product, Compliance, Public Policy, Risk, Treasury and business leaders on new products and new markets, in an environment where regulation is moving faster than the product. You will own the regulatory path for what we build next, and you will be expected to say "here is the path I recommend", not just "here are the risks".

STAFF PRODUCT DESIGNER (IC7), CREDIT BUILDER

Location: Miami (hybrid). We'll also consider candidates near other Nubank hubs, including São Paulo.

Team: Global Credit Card, Credit Builder

ABOUT THE ROLE

Millions of people across Latin America have never had a credit card. For many of them, Nubank is the first institution that gives them a real path to one. Credit Builder is where that path starts.

Our Credit Builder card is an entry-level credit product. Customers add money to unlock spending power, and we coach them step by step toward a full credit limit. The goal isn't to keep people on a starter product. It's to move them up and out of it, and most of our success stories do exactly that. The experience is built around gamification. A guided timeline walks customers through adding to their money box, increasing their limit, setting up autopay and building healthy habits. It has become one of the highest-NPS experiences at Nu and a model for gamification across the company.

Today Credit Builder runs in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. Next year our scope roughly flips. We'll bring our under-18 credit product, our credit score product (NuScore) and Credit Builder into more countries, possibly including the US. We're also planning a significant revamp of the core experience.

We're hiring a Staff Product Designer to help set the craft bar for this work. You'll be one of the most senior designers in Global Credit Card, working on both the high-visibility revamp and the day-to-day product work that keeps a fast-moving, multi-country team shipping.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead design for Credit Builder and related underserved-credit products across Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and new markets, including the US.

 - Drive the upcoming revamp of the Credit Builder experience, raising the bar on visual craft, interaction design and motion.

 - Design global solutions that hold together as one system while adapting to local needs, such as regulatory requirements, cultural context and market-specific constraints.

 - Push gamification and financial-coaching patterns further, helping customers understand how credit works and how to grow it.

 - Mentor and level up the more junior designers on the team, through critiques and day-to-day collaboration.

 - Partner closely with product managers, engineers, business analysts and a dedicated researcher, plus the market design teams in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia and adjacent teams such as Growth, Core and Collections.

 - Get hands-on with the full range of work, from the most ambitious projects to quick everyday design tasks, and move fast across both.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - An exceptional craft bar: polished visual and interaction design, strong systems thinking, and comfort with motion.

 - Proven experience designing complex products, ideally in fintech, financial services or other regulated or multi-market settings.

 - Strong strategic judgment, and comfort with ambiguity, competing priorities and shifting scope.

 - Excellent stakeholder management across countries, time zones and functions, with the ability to align global and local partners.

 - A low-ego, hands-on mindset. On a lean team covering many products and markets, everyone pitches in, including senior folks.

 - Experience mentoring designers and raising the quality of a team's work.

 - A portfolio that shows both depth of craft and the thinking behind it.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Spanish and/or Portuguese.

 - Experience with gamification, behavior-change design or financial-education products.

 - Experience designing for underserved or first-time credit customers.

 - Willingness to travel occasionally to work in person with market teams. Team leadership typically visits partners about twice a year.

WHY NUBANK

 - Real impact: you'll design the product that opens the door to credit for people who have often been shut out.

 - Global scope: three to four countries, multiple products, and a revamp being shaped right now.

 - A design org investing heavily in craft under CDO Ethan Eismann https://www.linkedin.com/in/ethaneismann/, with weekly critiques and design reviews across the broader Credit Card design group.

 - Competitive compensation and liquid equity.

INTERVIEW PROCESS
1. Intro call with recruiting
2. Async portfolio review
3. Live portfolio presentation with a design panel
4. Hiring manager interview
5. Final interview with design/product leadership

About the Role

As a second line function, we challenge process and control owners so that management can sign its SOx 302/404 conclusions with confidence.

This role is built on strong accounting and financial statement skills. You should be able to define materiality and scope of accounts by reading the Group's financial statements, and apply GAAP (mainly IFRS) to design controls that prevent material misstatements on a timely basis. Your accounting and disclosure knowledge is what lets you hold deep discussions with Finance specialists and with the external auditors throughout the audit.

YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Applying Nu's internal methodology and tying Risk → Assertion → Objective → Control → Evidence.

 - Determining technologies in scope and deciding when to request SOC reports (ITGC).

 - Challenging process and control owners, and treating IPE/EUC in design and testing.

 - Executing TOE according to sampling and RoMM, and independently producing audit-ready workpapers.

 - Drafting deficiency texts that size impact, magnitude and probability on the financial statements, and tracking remediation with the first line.

 - Contributing to cross-functional discussions with IT, Finance, first line and external audit counterparts on your scope.

 - Using low-code automation and AI with a risk lens, never as a substitute for professional skepticism.

 - Leading a specific pack, process or workstream, sharing what you learn and supporting teammates.

 - Contributing to cross-functional discussions with IT, first line and external audit counterparts on your scope.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

 - Defining observability for the platform, with monitoring and SLAs that surface issues before customers feel them.

 - Experience connecting cloud and on-premises environments: hybrid connectivity, BGP and dynamic routing, IP address management, load balancers and firewalls, planning, deploying and troubleshooting at scale.

jobs.title: Manager - Treasury, Capital Markets / Front Office
jobs.description:
The role

OakNorth runs an £8bn balance sheet with a small, senior Treasury team. Reporting to the Head of Treasury, you will own the execution of the bank's derivatives and FX activity and its investment portfolio, the sizing of its FX funding and liquidity positions, and support for capital and wholesale funding issuance — building the analytics behind those decisions. Treasury here is run as a measurable profit contributor rather than a cost centre, and the decisions taken on this desk are a material part of that.

This is a hands-on execution role rather than an oversight one. You will be pricing, trading, sizing and building the analysis behind your own recommendations, and presenting that work in senior forums including ALCO and to the CFO.

The role is deliberately front-office weighted, but the team is small and the remit is broad. There is genuine scope to build depth in the wider Treasury agenda — funds transfer pricing, liquidity and interest rate risk frameworks, and Board and regulatory work — for someone who wants it.

Principal responsibilities

Derivatives and FX

 - Execute interest rate swaps, cross-currency swaps and FX forwards across the bank's hedging programme. This is the most frequent trading activity on the desk and the centre of the role

 - Price, negotiate and execute with dealers across the counterparty panel, and evidence best execution

 - Own the FX risk position — including the USD lending book and intragroup exposures — and produce the exposure and hedging analysis that supports ALCO and Board reporting

 - Monitor collateral and margin flows under CSA arrangements, including the liquidity consequences of adverse mark-to-market moves. Supports expansion and onboarding with additional counterparts

 - Work with Finance on hedge designation and supporting documentation
 
 

Investment portfolio

 - Execute the gilt and HQLA investment programme against Board-approved mandates, using asset-swap spread and relative-value analysis to inform selection

 - Maintain and extend the portfolio construction tooling, including duration, maturity-ladder and concentration constraints

 - Size and roll the Treasury bill programme against deposit deployment windows

 - Support oversight of the externally managed AAA CLO portfolio, including trend and spread analytics and preparation for quarterly manager review

 - Support expansion of the investment instruments to develop the liquidity portfolio
 
 

Capital and funding issuance

 - Support the origination and execution of capital instrument issuance — Tier 2 and AT1 — working alongside the Treasurer, CFO and external advisers

 - Build and maintain the analysis behind issuance decisions, including sizing, pricing benchmarks and comparable market levels

 - Contribute to the development of wholesale funding options as the balance sheet grows, potentially spanning senior unsecured and secured issuance and securitisation
 
 

Funding and liquidity sizing

This part of the role is about sizing and direction. Operational execution and settlement sit with Treasury Operations; you set the strategy, size the transaction and steer the team.

 - Own USD liquidity end to end — determining how much liquidity is required in currency, and executing the cross-currency swaps that deliver it within Risk Appetite Limits

 - Set the sizing and collateral strategy for Bank of England repo facilities (ILTR and STR), instructing and reviewing rather than operating them

 - Steer the wider team on the analytical basis for funding and liquidity decisions, and review their output
 
 

Analytics and automation

We work extensively with AI-assisted development — Claude and Claude Code — inside a GitHub-controlled workflow. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you do need to be able to build a working analytical tool this way, or to learn to do so quickly.

 - Build, maintain and extend the desk's Python toolkit — pricing, sizing, limit monitoring and income attribution

 - Replace manual spreadsheet processes with repeatable, auditable and documented ones

 - Contribute to the Treasury Management System implementation and the Bloomberg data integration
 
 

Control, governance and reporting

 - Ensure trades are captured, confirmed and reported in line with the Treasury Trading Policy and supporting procedures

 - Monitor Risk Appetite Limits and Key Risk Indicators for front-office activity, and escalate promptly and clearly

 - Prepare and present front-office inputs to ALCO

 - Support regulatory deliverables — ILAAP, ICAAP and PRA information requests — from a front-office perspective
 
 

Essential experience and skills

 - Relevant execution experience — typically three to six years in a bank treasury front office, money markets or ALM desk, or a markets and rates role with clearly transferable execution skills.

 - Well-honed Bloomberg skills.. You should be fast and self-sufficient across money market and fixed income pricing, curve and relative-value analysis, swap and FX pricing, and the day-to-day ticket and blotter workflow.

 - Instrument knowledge — interest rate and cross-currency swaps and FX forwards first and foremost, together with gilts, Treasury bills and repo including Bank of England facilities.

 - Regulatory mechanics — a sound working understanding of LCR, NSFR and HQLA classification, as well as Capital regulation and how execution decisions move them.

 - Python literacy — sufficient to build, read and debug analytical tooling (pandas, numpy), together with real enthusiasm for AI-assisted development.

 - Communication — the ability to explain a trade, a number or a risk clearly and briefly to a senior, non-specialist audience.

Desirable

 - CFA, FRM, BTRM in progress or complete

 - Exposure to Clearing, CSA and margining mechanics, SA-CCR, or hedge accounting

 - Securitisation, CLO or structured credit experience

 - Exposure to debt capital markets — capital instrument or senior debt issuance, or securitisation — from a bank treasury, DCM or advisory seat

 - Experience in a challenger bank or another small team where breadth was required rather than optional
 
 

Who will do well here

 - You get things moving. Pace matters more than polish, and you are comfortable forming a view, making a call and owning the outcome.

 - You learn quickly and want to. The technical range here is wide, and we would rather hire someone visibly capable and eager to grow into the full breadth of it than someone with a narrow and finished skill set.

 - You are helpful by default. The team is small and nobody's job description is treated as a boundary.

 - You are comfortable being challenged, and challenging back.

You thrive in a global team. The finance team is spread across the UK and India and you're good at building trust across time zones and you don't need to be in the same room to stay aligned.

jobs.title: Co-Head of Credit Risk – Real Estate
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Co-Head of Credit Risk – Real Estate to help grow our real estate lending businesses working alongside our Co-Head of Credit Risk – Trading Business. Together, you will provide senior credit leadership across our real estate and trading business lending, each bringing deep expertise in your area.

Based in London, you will help shape the real estate deals we do, the people we develop and how we work across the UK market, while keeping sound credit judgement at the heart of every decision.

This is a role for someone who wants to build, not just oversee. You will work closely with our Debt Finance Originators to understand customers’ ambitions and find the right structure for their transactions, making and sanctioning credit decisions and bringing an independent view to Credit Risk Committee.

The opportunity goes beyond individual deals. You will lead our Real Estate Credit Risk teams, oversee portfolio risk and help shape how we approach real estate credit as we grow internationally.

We also want your ideas. How could AI improve our analysis? Where could better data help us spot risk sooner? What should we stop doing so the team can spend more time on the decisions that matter? You will help turn those ideas into practical changes.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

SHAPE REAL ESTATE CREDIT ACROSS OAKNORTH

 - Work with senior Lending and Credit Risk colleagues to support growth across all markets, with clear views on the opportunities we should pursue and the risks we should take.

 - Help shape our approach to real estate credit, combining consistent underwriting standards with an understanding of local markets, deal structures and regulation.

 - Stay close to transactions and the portfolio, and build the team’s capability as the business grows.

CREDIT DECISIONS AND SANCTIONING

 - Make and sanction decisions on new transactions, amendments and other material credit matters within your delegated authority.

 - Assess deal structure, leverage, cash flow, security, sponsor strength and downside risk.

 - Work with Debt Finance Originators from the early stages of a deal, helping shape terms and structures that work for the customer and meet our risk appetite. Provide clear, timely credit feedback and be direct when a transaction is not right for us.

 - Take responsibility for complex or higher-risk cases, including when information is incomplete or circumstances are changing.

 - Record decisions clearly, with a sound rationale.

CREDIT RISK COMMITTEE

 - Play an active role in Credit Risk Committee and chair where appropriate, bringing a solutions-focused, commercial mindset and independent credit judgement to UK real estate decisions. Help shape our real estate credit appetite, find workable structures for good lending opportunities and keep decisions moving at pace without compromising credit standards.

 - Challenge the key assumptions and risks, including how individual deals affect portfolio concentrations.

 - Bring a clear view and be prepared to challenge senior colleagues.

BUILD AND LEAD THE TEAM

 - Lead our Real Estate Credit Risk teams, giving people clear responsibility and expecting high standards.

 - Develop credit professionals who can think for themselves, form a view and stand behind a decision.

 - Coach colleagues through complex transactions and give future leaders the experience to take on more responsibility.

 - Bring the teams together across markets, and recruit and retain the people we need for our next stage of growth.

USE AI AND DATA TO IMPROVE CREDIT WORK

AI and technology should be part of how we do credit work, not a separate project. You will help the team:

 - spend less time gathering information and preparing credit analysis and committee papers

 - use data to identify portfolio risks earlier

 - automate repetitive tasks and test tools that improve the quality and speed of our work

You do not need a technical background. We do expect curiosity, a willingness to test new approaches and the judgement to know where they add value.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

You will have substantial experience underwriting and sanctioning complex commercial real estate transactions. Direct experience of making credit decisions is essential; policy or governance experience alone is not enough.

You will bring:

 - deep knowledge of real estate lending across different asset classes and transaction types

 - sound judgement on deal structure, sponsors, security, cash flow and downside risk, alongside an understanding of portfolio exposures

 - experience on senior Credit Risk Committees and the confidence to challenge senior Lending colleagues

 - a track record of leading and developing credit teams

 - Experience in UK or across more than one lending market, would be an advantage.

WORKING AT OAKNORTH

We were founded by entrepreneurs, for entrepreneurs. Our customers have ambitions for their businesses, and we look for ways to help them get there. That takes curiosity, commercial understanding and the willingness to look beyond the obvious answer.

You should enjoy that kind of work: getting into a complex deal, challenging assumptions and finding a structure that others may have missed. Just as importantly, you need the independence to say no when the risk is not right.

We move quickly and expect people to take ownership. You will have room to put ideas into practice, challenge established ways of working and develop your team. In return, we expect clear decisions, disciplined risk judgement and responsibility for the outcome.

If you want to help grow a lending business, develop strong credit leaders and change how credit work gets done, this is an opportunity to do all three.

Benefits & Perks 

 - Equity — we want everyone to have a stake in the business so our interests are aligned

 - 25 days holiday plus personalised benefits — opt in to what matters to you

 - Subsidised private medical insurance with Bupa

 - Enhanced maternity and paternity leave

 - Wellbeing and social events, plus in-house Barista Bar in the London office

 - Volunteering time off to support causes that matter to you

 - Salary sacrifice schemes — cycle to work, nursery, gym, and electric car scheme

jobs.title: Business Development Representative
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

OakNorth's lending business is scaling across the UK and US, and we need a Business Development Representative to join our growing Commercial Strategy team.

Our next good deal should not depend on who happens to find us.

As a Business Development Representative, you own the front end of our lending pipeline. That means two things.

Generating new opportunities. You work hand in hand with Marketing, turning campaign themes, target segments and ideal customer profiles into live outreach: multi-touch sequences across email, phone and LinkedIn, follow-up on the demand our campaigns generate, and the account research that makes it land. The output is qualified meetings with the right people.

Qualifying inbound leads. You own inbound enquiries end to end: researching them, screening them, and routing them, within SLA, to the right Originator.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Outbound

 - Run marketing-led outbound campaigns. Take the segments, messaging and campaign themes Marketing develops and put them into market as multi-touch, multi-channel sequences, run at a consistent cadence.

 - Research accounts and personalise. Understand a business and its situation well enough to earn a first conversation.

 - Feed back on what is working. You are closest to the response (which messages land, which segments go quiet, which objections keep recurring). Campaign design gets better because you tell Marketing what you are seeing.

Inbound

 - Work the demand Marketing generates. Content downloads, webinar and event registrations, website enquiries. You pick these up quickly, research them properly, and convert those that meet our criteria.

 - Own the inbound queue. Qualify and route every inbound lead within SLA, with the research already done before it reaches an Originator.

Across both

 - Qualify with rigour. Screen against our policies and credit appetite. Saying “this is not a good fit, and here is why” is as valuable here as saying yes.

 - Nurture over time. Most businesses worth lending to are not ready today. Keep warm, useful relationships with prospects and referrers until they are.

 - Keep the data clean. Accurate CRM records and weekly pipeline reporting. What you build gets reused in outreach across the bank.

 - Work shoulder to shoulder with Originators. Take their feedback on lead quality seriously, and adjust how you work.
 
 

WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT

 - It is not a closing role. You will not negotiate or sign facilities. You hand over to an Originator once a prospect is properly qualified.

 - It is not a volume-dialling role. Hard-selling outreach damages our standing within the market.

 - It is not a role that pays for activity. Booking a meeting is not the finish line.
 
 

THE PROFILE

You are likely to be early in your career with some exposure to lending, credit or financial services. How you work matters more than the exact shape of your CV.

YOU'LL BRING

 - Overall 1-4 years of experience in Sales/Business Development with prior experience working in a banking/fintech industry.

 - Enough finance grounding to qualify a lead properly: you can hold a sensible conversation about how a business loan is structured and assessed, or you can learn that quickly and want to.

 - Experience working to targets in an outbound role, and the resilience that takes. Outbound means hearing “no” far more often than yes, and we need you as sharp at the end of a campaign as at the start.

 - Credibility with senior people. Originators need to take your leads seriously from early on, and prospects and advisers need to find you worth their time.

 - Real organisational discipline. You keep records accurate and current without being chased.

 - Clear, concise written English. Most of the first impressions you make will be in writing.

Technology

We're pragmatic about our technology choices. These are some of the things we use now:

 - Jest, React Testing Library, Cypress, pytest

 - AWS, GCP

 - Docker, Terraform, GitHub, CircleCI
 

HOW WE EXPECT YOU TO WORK

We expect you to work in these ways, as well as encouraging and enabling these practices from others:

 - Collaborate - We work in cross-functional, mission driven, autonomous squads that gel over time. We pair program to work better through shared experience and knowledge.

 - You build it, you run it - We embrace DevOps culture and end-to-end ownership of products and features. Every engineer, regardless of their role, can lead delivery of features from start to finish.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Application Security Engineer is a hands-on, full-stack security role focused on fixing the hardest application and AI security problems — particularly those that cross team boundaries or involve architecture, authentication, and authorisation that automation cannot yet safely resolve. You'll take remediation load away from engineering teams so they can stay focused on delivery, working closely with the teams that detect, prioritise, and track vulnerabilities. You'll also contribute to the development of OakNorth's internal coding agent platforms, so security fixes can scale safely.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Fix complex application security vulnerabilities directly, including architectural weaknesses and issues in legacy technology that automated remediation cannot yet handle safely.

 - Lead remediation of problems that cross team and system boundaries, coordinating changes across multiple owners and services and seeing them through to resolution.

 - Resolve authentication and authorisation weaknesses, including identity, access control, session and token handling, service-to-service trust and permission models.

 - Act as a dedicated delivery vehicle for security remediation, reducing the fix burden on engineering teams so they can focus on product delivery.

 - Interpret the output of security tooling (e.g., SAST, DAST, SCA, secrets, container and IaC scanning), validate findings, identify root causes and implement the right fix rather than only triaging.

 - Secure agentic and AI-enabled systems, assessing and mitigating risks such as those in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, including prompt injection, excessive agent permissions, tool misuse, insecure agent-to-agent communication and unsafe handling of agent outputs.

 - Contribute to the development of our internal coding agent platforms, including remediation agents, by supplying specialist fixes, remediation patterns, evaluation cases and feedback on where agents succeed or fail.

 - Define and build guardrails for agent-generated and human-written changes (e.g., least-privilege agent access, human approval points, secure defaults, shared libraries, pipeline checks and policy-as-code) so that changes are safe and vulnerabilities do not recur.

 - Build and secure GitHub workflows and release pipelines, including GitHub Actions hardening, secrets and token handling, branch protection, dependency and supply chain controls, and security gates in CI/CD.

 - Plan and deliver higher-risk changes safely, including testing, peer review, rollout and rollback approaches, in partnership with the teams that own the systems.

 - Work with the teams that detect, prioritise and track vulnerabilities to take prioritised findings through to remediation, and identify recurring fix types that can be automated safely.

 - Document remediation approaches, share knowledge and coach engineers on secure design, secure coding and the safe use of AI coding agents.

 - Report on remediation progress, including backlog reduction, SLA performance and risk reduction, and provide evidence to support audit and regulatory requirements.

YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…

Engineering Skills

 - Full stack engineering experience across front end, back end and APIs, with proficiency in one or more languages (e.g., Java, Python, C#, JavaScript/TypeScript) and the ability to work in unfamiliar and legacy codebases.

 - Strong hands-on experience with GitHub (pull requests, code review, branch protection, code scanning) and GitHub Actions, including building and securing release pipelines.

 - Working knowledge of cloud platforms, containers and infrastructure as code.

 - Ability to review code, find vulnerabilities and implement practical, correct fixes.

Application Security Skills

 - Strong application security knowledge, including the OWASP Top 10 and common vulnerability classes such as injection, broken access control, insecure deserialization and cryptographic weaknesses.

 - Deep understanding of authentication and authorisation, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, JWT and session handling, RBAC/ABAC models and service-to-service identity.

 - Hands-on experience interpreting application security tooling output (SAST, DAST, SCA, secrets, container and IaC scanning), distinguishing true and false positives and finding root cause.

 - Understanding of CI/CD and software supply chain security, including GitHub Actions risks such as untrusted input, over-privileged tokens and third-party action pinning.

AI & Agentic Security Skills

 - Day-to-day experience using coding agents such as Claude to write, review and fix code, with sound judgement on where they are reliable and where they are not.

 - Ability to design guardrails, permission boundaries and evaluation approaches for AI agents and agent-generated changes.

 - Ability to turn manual fixes into repeatable patterns and test cases that agent platforms can use.

Remediation & Architecture Skills

 - Experience fixing architectural and design-level security issues, and making safe changes in systems with limited tests, documentation or clear ownership.

 - Sound judgement on testing, rollout and rollback for higher-risk changes.

Collaboration & Communication Skills

jobs.title: Associate Director - Business Banking
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Business Banking team supports some of the UK’s most exciting scale-ups and complex mid-market businesses. We combine smart technology and data with the human judgement, speed and personal service OakNorth is known for.

ABOUT THE ROLE

OakNorth was built by entrepreneurs, for entrepreneurs — and we’re looking for an ambitious, well-connected commercial operator to help take our Business Banking proposition to the next level.

As Associate Director, Business Banking, you’ll be at the heart of our growth. You’ll find and win brilliant new customers, build trusted relationships with founders and finance leaders, and expand OakNorth’s presence across mid-market businesses and their trusted advisors.

This isn’t a role for someone who wants to work from a fixed playbook. We want someone entrepreneurial: a natural relationship builder who spots opportunities, creates momentum and turns ambitious ideas into commercial results. You’ll have the ownership and platform to make a visible impact — for our customers, our team and OakNorth.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Win ambitious new customers: Identify, engage and convert complex mid-market businesses from £2-100m turnover for their day-day operational banking and deposits.

 - Build relationships that matter: Become a trusted partner to founders, CEOs, CFOs and trusted advisors by understanding their ambitions and helping them navigate the opportunities and challenges of growth.

 - Grow customer value: Deepen existing relationships, increase product adoption and deposits, and ensure customers get greater value from OakNorth as they scale.

 - Make OakNorth impossible to ignore: Be a visible and credible ambassador for the brand, strengthening our position as the go-to banking partner for ambitious growth businesses.

 - Influence the strategy: Collaborate with Product, Marketing, Operations and other teams to remove friction, solve customer problems and help shape the direction of our offering.

 - Show up where it counts: Represent OakNorth at the events, communities and conversations shaping the UK’s entrepreneurial ecosystem — and create new ways for us to connect with it.

 - Bring the outside in: Stay close to customers, competitors and market shifts, turning insight into ideas that sharpen our proposition and accelerate growth.

 - Challenge the status quo: Keep looking for smarter, faster and more effective ways to win customers, build our network and improve the experience we deliver.

 - Own the outcome: Take accountability for your pipeline, relationships and commercial results, bringing pace, energy and discipline to everything you do.
 
 

YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE...

 - A strong track record in a commercial, sales or relationship-focused role within banking, fintech or Financial SAAS business.

 - Used to working in a start-up environment and able to adapt within a fast-moving, high-growth environment.

 - An entrepreneurial mindset — you spot opportunities, act with urgency and enjoy building rather than simply following an established playbook.

 - A deep understanding of what founders and CFOs need from a banking partner.

 - A strong network across mid-market businesses and their trusted advisors to be able to grow the OakNorth brand within.

 - Proven success building new relationships, opening doors and turning networks into meaningful commercial outcomes.

 - Strong commercial instincts and a results-focused approach, with the confidence to own ambitious targets.

 - Natural curiosity and the ability to quickly understand a customer’s business, ambitions and challenges.

 - Excellent communication and influencing skills, with the credibility to engage senior decision-makers and represent OakNorth externally.

 - A collaborative, low-ego approach and the ability to work across teams to get things done for customers.

 - Comfort operating in a fast-paced, founder-led environment where priorities move quickly and success is measured by impact.

 - A genuine appetite to challenge conventional business banking and help build something exceptional.

WHAT WE OFFER

OakNorth is for people who want to make a visible difference. We move with pace, stay close to our customers and give talented people the ownership to turn ambitious ideas into real outcomes.

You’ll join a business with the energy of a scale-up and the reach and responsibility of a bank. You’ll have the freedom to build your market, expand your network and help shape a Business Banking proposition designed around the UK’s most ambitious companies.

Due to a high volume of applications, we may decide to take down this advert early. Please submit your application asap

OakNorth’s Ventures team invests in and incubates early-stage companies that complement the bank and its appetite. The team works closely with founders and with OakNorth’s co-founder. The intern supports the team across its investment and venture activity.

RESPONSIBILITIES
