The role does not involve production software development, but it does require the ability to read and assess code, system designs and data pipelines.

 - Hands-on experience building or applying AI-assisted security tooling to test applications and APIs, combining automated analysis with source-code review and manual validation.

 - Demonstrated ability to review production code in one or more languages such as TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, Python and Go.

 - Experience securing software supply chains and CI/CD systems, including dependencies, build infrastructure, secrets, artifacts, signing, and release integrity.

 - Experience threat modeling complex products and translating security risks into concrete engineering requirements.

 - Strong judgment when evaluating exploitability, business impact, and appropriate remediation.

 - Track record of partnering effectively with engineering and product teams while maintaining a high security bar.

 - Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical risk to both engineers and non-security stakeholders.

 - Experience securing consumer financial products, wallets, payments, or other systems where client integrity and transaction safety are critical.

 - Experience securing CI/CD and software supply chains, including GitHub Actions or similar systems, build runners, workload federation, artifacts, and production deployment paths.

jobs.description:
ABOUT PLASMA

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.

THE TEAM & OUR STORY https://x.com/Plasma/status/2067634709727719601?s=20

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.

THE ROLE

 - You inherit a live product with real spend, and you own the paid engine that scales it across Plasma One and Plasma Business. Channels, budget, creative and measurement all sit with you.

 - Own the cost of acquisition of valuable users and managing our paid advertising motion end to end.

 - Deploy many variations of ads, platforms and angles to test high performing creative and formats driving users into both custom funnels and direct to app while measuring downstream events.

 - Take us beyond our crypto-native audience. Find the audiences, messages and formats on Meta, Google, TikTok and YouTube that bring in people who fund and keep spending, then scale the ones that work.

 - Run the campaigns yourself. You build them, launch them, read the results and decide where tomorrow's budget goes. New creative, new audiences and new angles every week, with a clear read on what worked and why.

 - Look past the click. Work with product and design on landing pages, onboarding, lifecycle and referrals so a new sign-up becomes a funded account and a regular user.

 - Build the paid function. The tracking, reporting and playbooks you set up become what the team runs on, and as channels prove out you help hire the specialists who scale them.

THE BAR

 - Regional market expertise. You know how to work on an acquisition strategy that differs between countries and markets

 - Deep, hands-on experience running paid acquisition at a consumer app or fintech, especially paid social and search, with real budgets and real accountability for the outcome.

 - Understand how to navigate Meta AEM, Google optimization, Apple search ads, Snapchat and other platforms, configure Appsflyer, our data warehouse and creative to achieve exceptional results.

 - A track record of structured creative testing and confident budget allocation across channels.

 - Strong measurement skills. You know attribution, incrementality and cohort analysis, and where each one can mislead you.

 - Range across the funnel. You have improved landing pages, onboarding, lifecycle or referrals, working closely with product and design.

 - Proof, not claims. Show us what you personally tested, what improved, and what it did to acquisition cost, activation and retention. Vague answers will not get through.

 - Resourceful. You find a way to get the answer or the result, with or without a big team behind you. Based in London or ready to relocate.

NICE TO HAVE

 - You were an early growth hire at a global consumer fintech

 - You know your way around mobile measurement partners such as AppsFlyer or Adjust, and the ad policies that come with financial products.

 - You are curious about stablecoins and new payment rails. Prior crypto experience is not required.

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

 - Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

 - A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

 - Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

 - All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

 - Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Product Designer at Ramp, you are accountable for outcomes, not just artifacts. You work with PMs, engineers, and other designers to define the right problems, explore and validate solutions, and ship product experiences that change customer behavior.

Design at Ramp is AI first and builder led. Work starts in an LLM, moves into tools like Claude and Cursor to explore flows and interactions, and then comes into Figma for systems and polish. Designers prototype early, test with real customers, and stay involved through launch and iteration.

We are looking for multiple product designers who are excited to work this way and who want to use AI as a core part of how they design.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own product work end to end: Partner with PM and engineering to define problems, explore solution spaces, validate concepts, and ship product improvements that move key metrics. Stay involved through launch and iteration, not just handoff.

 - Start in an LLM: Use tools like Claude to clarify intent, draft short PRDs, and surface risks, edge cases, and initial approaches. Use this work to align quickly with your team.

 - Validate assumptions with self-serve research: Talk directly with customers, run quick tests, and use what you learn to adjust direction. Treat research as a velocity tool, not a gate.

 - Prototype using AI tools: Use Cursor and Claude Code to build and iterate on flows and simple interfaces. Let AI generate code while you guide structure, behavior, and UX quality. Partner with engineers to decide what moves into the product.

 - Bring work into Figma: Translate validated concepts into Figma for full state coverage, system alignment, and production readiness.

 - Design for the 80 / 20: Encode judgment and complexity under the hood while keeping the default experience simple and successful for most customers.

 - Contribute to patterns and culture: Share prompts, patterns, and learnings with the design org. Participate in crits and reviews that raise the bar for quality.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - Experience as a product designer working on complex products, ideally in B2B, fintech, or other systems-heavy environments

 - Ownership of projects from problem definition through launch and iteration

 - Active use of LLMs such as Claude or ChatGPT in your design workflow

 - Comfort working in tools like Cursor or Claude Code, even if you are not writing production code by hand

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision.

In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day.

You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

 - Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

 - Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows.

 - Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp.

 - Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better.

 - Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

 - You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

 - You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

 - You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.

 - You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.

 - You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon.

 - You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

 - You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

 - Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage)

 - Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks)

 - Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up

WHY BE A CX ASSOCIATE AT RAMP

 - Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue.

 - AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter.

 - Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested.

 - Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of.

READ MORE ABOUT HOW RAMP THINKS ABOUT AI AND CX:

 - How Ramp Became an AI-First Company — Geoff Charles, CPO https://x.com/geoffintech/status/2042002590758572377?s=20

 - Inside Glass: How Ramp Built a Proprietary AI Platform for CX — Seb Goddijn, AI Product Manager https://x.com/sebgoddijn/status/2042285915435937816?s=20

 - AI-Powered Customer Experience at Ramp — Ben Levick, Head of CX / Ramp AI https://ramp.com/leading-indicators/how-to-build-your-team-to-capitalize-on-ai

WHAT TO KNOW BEFORE YOU APPLY

 - Schedule & Shift Bidding - Please Read Carefully: CX Associates work a set 40-hour/week schedule assigned through a schedule-bid process. Working hours span 7:00 AM–11:00 PM ET, and your shift will likely include a weekend day (either Sun–Thu or Tue–Sat). Associates also cover 2–3 company holidays per year on a rotating basis. Ramp's customers operate on financial deadlines that don't pause.

 - The product changes frequently. If you need a stable, predictable environment, this isn't it. If you like learning new things every week, it is.

 - This role is a launchpad for your career at one of the fastest-growing companies in fintech.

For candidates located in NYC or SF, the pay range for this role is $65,000-$70,000. For candidates located in all other locations, the pay range for this role is $60,000-$65,000.

BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

ABOUT RAMP

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision.

In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day.

You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

 - Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

 - Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows.

 - Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp.

 - Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better.

 - Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

 - You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

 - You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

 - You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.

 - You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.

 - You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon.

 - You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

 - You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

 - Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage)

 - Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks)

 - Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up

WHY BE A CX ASSOCIATE AT RAMP

 - Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue.

 - AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter.

 - Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested.

 - Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of.

WHAT TO KNOW BEFORE YOU APPLY

Evening working hours span 6:00 PM–2:30 AM EST, and your shift will likely include a weekend day (either Sun–Thu or Tue–Sat). Associates also cover 2–3 company holidays per year on a rotating basis. Ramp's customers operate on financial deadlines that don't pause.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT PRODUCTION ENGINEERING

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

 - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

 - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

 - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

 - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

 - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

OUR TEAMS

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

 - Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

 - Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

 - Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

 - Internal Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

Day to day, you will:

 - Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

 - Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

 - Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

 - Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

 - Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

 - Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

 - Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

 - Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

 - You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

 - You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

 - You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

 - You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

 - You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

 - You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

Experience profile:

 - 2+ years of software engineering experience shipping high-quality architectures for critical systems 

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write clean, well-tested, production-ready code

 - Hands-on experience with distributed systems at production scale

 - Experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS preferred)

 - Familiarity with observability practices (SLOs, error budgets, alerting, dashboards)

 - Track record of leading technical projects end-to-end, including cross-team coordination

 - Comfortable using AI tooling and coding agents as part of your everyday engineering workflow — we expect our engineers to leverage these tools to move faster and think bigger

Bonus (not required):

 - Experience with cellular or multi-tenant architecture patterns

In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day.

You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

 - Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

 - Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows.

 - Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp.

 - Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better.

 - Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

 - You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

 - You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

 - You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.

 - You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.

 - You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon.

 - You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

 - You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

 - Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage)

 - Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks)

 - Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up

WHY BE A CX ASSOCIATE AT RAMP

 - Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue.

 - AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter.

 - Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested.

 - Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of.

READ MORE ABOUT HOW RAMP THINKS ABOUT AI AND CX:

 - How Ramp Became an AI-First Company — Geoff Charles, CPO https://x.com/geoffintech/status/2042002590758572377?s=20

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

We're looking for an Employment Counsel to join Ramp's Legal team. This is a generalist employment role with broad scope. You will handle U.S. employment counseling as your base load, cover non-U.S. jurisdictions as needed, and own immigration and global mobility. You will partner directly with People, Talent, Total Rewards, Finance, Tax, Equity Admin, Compliance, and business leaders, and you will manage outside counsel in jurisdictions where we do not hold the expertise in house. We are a small, high-leverage team supporting a company that moves quickly, so you will cover a lot of ground and be trusted to run matters independently.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Day-to-day employment counseling: Advise People partners and managers on hiring, worker classification, compensation, leaves and accommodations, performance management, discipline, separations, and more

 - Immigration and global mobility: Collaborate with the People team on the immigration program, including work authorization outside the U.S. Set and communicate the sponsorship policy, manage outside immigration counsel and case volume, and partner with Talent on offer-stage decisions. Support relocations, cross-border remote work requests, and business travel, and work with Finance and Tax on permanent establishment and mobility tax exposure

 - Investigations: Collaborate with the People team on internal investigations and advise on findings and outcomes

 - Disputes: Handle demand letters, agency charges, arbitrations, and litigation with outside counsel

 - Agreements and templates: Own offer letters, employment agreements, separation and release agreements, contractor and consultant agreements, restrictive covenants, and the local-law variants of each

 - Transactions: Support employment and immigration diligence, employee transitions, and post-close integration for M&A and new-market entry

 - Build for scale: Produce manager training, policies, self-serve guidance, and repeatable processes as we expand in the US and globally

WHAT YOU NEED

 - 5+ years practicing employment law, with a combination of top law firm and in-house experience at a high-growth technology company

 - JD from an accredited law school and active membership in at least one U.S. state bar (New York or California preferred)

 - Deep U.S. employment counseling experience across the full employee lifecycle, including wage and hour, leaves and accommodations, investigations, performance management, and separations

 - Working knowledge of employment law outside the U.S. and the judgment to triage a cross-border question quickly

 - Hands-on experience with U.S. business immigration and global mobility, including running a sponsorship program and managing immigration counsel at volume

 - Demonstrated ability to independently run multiple time-sensitive matters

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can turn an employment law question into guidance a manager can act on in one reading

 - High judgment on sensitive and confidential matters, and the steadiness to advise on them under time pressure

 - Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift and processes are still being built, and a bias toward action

NICE TO HAVES 

 - Experience at a fintech, payments, or regulated financial services company

 - Experience standing up employment infrastructure in a new country, including EOR-to-entity transitions and works council or employee representative consultation

 - Employment experience across EMEA, APAC, LATAM, or Canada

 - A track record of using AI or automation to eliminate manual legal work

 - Define and maintain test sets, scenario coverage, and evaluation frameworks for compliance AI/agent tools in partnership with the engineers building them

 - Own the documentation and governance layer for every automated or AI-assisted decision point

 - Work with the FCC team to understand current workflows to guide innovative solutions

 - Recommend automation and AI adoption decisions with evidence and escalate control-posture or model-risk trade-offs to compliance leadership

 

WHAT YOU NEED

 - 5+ years of financial services experience in compliance, AML, or related regulatory advisory roles, preferably in fintech

 - Demonstrated senior-investigator experience across TM Alerts, AML Investigations, Complex Fraud, and EDD Reviews

 - Direct experience testing, labeling, or evaluating AI/ML model outputs, or strong aptitude and demonstrated fast ramp-up if new to formal model evaluation

 - Strong AI fluency and data analytics skills

 - Comfort partnering with engineers day-to-day and ability to translate compliance judgment into build specs, test cases, and evaluation criteria engineers can act on

 - Strong project management and documentation rigor

 - Ability to scope an ambiguous automation problem, choose an approach, and deliver a durable outcome with minimal oversight

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less.

We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp.

This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change.

You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better.

You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it.

This role is for you if you’re excited by:

 - Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same.

 - Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality.

 - Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional.

The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead and develop the design systems team. Set clear priorities, ownership, and goals. Give direct, timely feedback, hold people accountable, and help them do the best work of their careers.

 - Own the system’s vision and direction. Decide what to preserve, evolve, simplify, or replace based on what builders and customers need. Turn that direction into focused work the team can deliver.

 - Elevate Ramp’s visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path.

 - Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference experiences, composition rules, and guidance that produce better work without you in the room.

 - Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance, compose interfaces, and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use.

 - Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, work in code, and get into implementation details to test ideas, unblock the team, and understand where the system breaks down.

 - Define and measure quality. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks. Measure whether builders can ship better work faster, with less rework—not just whether they use the tools.

 - Improve the path from idea to shipped experience. Partner with engineering and AI teams on workflows that support fast exploration, useful iteration, and appropriate production safeguards.

 - Earn adoption. Work alongside product teams, listen closely, teach through examples, and turn recurring questions and exceptions into improvements to the system.

 - Keep the team moving forward. Experiment as models and tools evolve, share what you learn, and change direction when the evidence calls for it.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - Experience leading and developing strong design or design engineering teams, with a track record of setting direction and delivering meaningful outcomes.

 - Exceptional visual and interaction design skills. Your work shows a clear point of view, attention to detail, and an ability to make complex experiences feel simple.

 - Strong technical fluency. You can prototype and build in code, understand front-end architecture, and work through implementation tradeoffs with engineers—not just hand off specifications.

 - Active, hands-on use of AI in your design and building workflow. You understand where it helps, where it fails, and how to improve its output rather than accept it.

NICE TO HAVES

jobs.location: New York, NY (HQ) · San Francisco, CA · Remote (US)
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT PRODUCTION ENGINEERING

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

 - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

 - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

 - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

 - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

 - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

OUR TEAMS

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

 - Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

 - Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

 - Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

 - Developer Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

As a Tech Lead & Manager, you are a hands-on player-coach: you will lead and grow a team while remaining directly engaged in the technical work. Management at Ramp does not mean stepping away from the technology or the code. You will help set direction, develop engineers, and work alongside the team to deliver consequential infrastructure outcomes.

Day to day, you will:

 - Build, coach, and grow a high-performing team. Create clarity, give direct feedback, mentor engineers, and help each person expand their technical judgment, ownership, and leadership.

 - Set technical direction for your team’s domain. Identify the highest-leverage problems, define a path forward, bring the right people along, and stay engaged with the team until the work is delivered.

 - Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

 - Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

 - Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

 - Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

 - Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

 - Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

 - Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

 - Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

 - You love building teams, mentoring engineers, and helping people grow—and you are equally energized by writing code, reviewing designs, and digging into complex distributed systems.

 - You are a true player-coach. You know when to coach, delegate, and create space for others to lead; you also know when your direct technical involvement will create the most leverage.

 - You can set a technical direction, bring people along, and then lock in with the team to make it happen.

 - You do not believe managing engineers means stepping away from the technology or the code.

 - You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

 - You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

 - You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

 - You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

 - You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

 - You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

 - Staff+-level technical leadership: experience setting technical direction and leading complex, multi-quarter technical initiatives from ambiguous problems through durable production outcomes.

 - Experience managing, mentoring, and developing engineers. You create clarity, give direct feedback, and help people grow in technical judgment, scope, and leadership.

jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp's Enterprise Customer Success Managers on the Lifecycle team don't stop at go-live — they make sure customers keep getting more from Ramp as their business grows. Ramp has grown its product suite significantly over the last several years. As we've matured as an organization, our customer relationships have grown more complex too: customers are buying more of the platform at once, running it across more entities and teams, and relying on it for more of how their finance function operates. Hitting an activation milestone doesn't mean the job's finished. Too often, a feature that could solve a real problem goes unused because no one is there to show how it would work in that customer's business.

That's where you come in. This is a role for people who understand how finance teams actually run, who think in years rather than quarters, and who already use AI the way surgeons use instruments: not occasionally, not as an experiment, but as the default way they work. You'll own the customer experience after implementation for a book of Ramp's highest-potential enterprise customers, partnering with Account Management on long-term account strategy. You'll also be one of the first Lifecycle CSMs on a newly formed team, helping define how Ramp earns and keeps the trust of its most important customers.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the post-implementation experience for a book of enterprise customers, with clear accountability for sustained adoption, customer satisfaction, and renewal readiness

 - Drive sustained adoption by understanding each customer's goals and guiding them toward the workflows that improve outcomes for their business — including the products and features they've already purchased but haven't fully put to work

 - Act as each customer's expert in finance workflows: understand how they run their business, advise on decisions as their needs change, and make the value of new Ramp capabilities clear in their context

 - Build multi-threaded relationships across every account and partner with Account Management on executive relationships, so the account stays steady through change like a new Controller or CFO

 - Partner with Account Management on QBRs and executive business reviews, quantifying Ramp's impact in the language CFOs and Controllers care about — close cycle improvement, spend visibility, savings, and ROI — not just product usage metrics

 - Spot opportunities for growth and bring them to Account Management, who owns renewals and expansion; as customers add products, drive ongoing activation so they reach value quickly

 - Run your book on data: monitor usage, CP, and risk signals, get ahead of challenges and escalations, and see them through to resolution well before renewal is on the calendar

 - Use AI tools daily to prepare for customer calls, build materials, synthesize data, identify account risk, and operate at a pace traditional methods can't match

 - Bring customer feedback back into Ramp — surfacing patterns, gaps, and opportunities from your accounts to shape how Ramp evolves

 - Help build the motion from the ground up: executive sponsor programs, champion groups, churn reviews, and the playbooks every future Lifecycle CSM will run

MUST-HAVES

 - Long-term account ownership — You've owned a book of customers past launch and through renewal, and you have measurable retention, adoption, or satisfaction results to show for it. Finance or fintech context is a plus but not required.

 - Customer experience mindset — You measure success by how customers feel about working with you, not only by milestones hit. You get ahead of problems before customers raise them and own escalations through resolution.

 - Executive relationship building — You build multi-threaded relationships across finance, operations, and the C-suite. When your champion leaves, the account doesn't leave with them.

 - Financial impact communication — You can walk a CFO through the value Ramp has delivered, connect adoption to P&L outcomes, and help make the case for continued investment in financial terms, not product terms. A finance background is not required — fluency is.

 - AI fluency as a daily habit — You already use AI tools habitually in your work. You use them to prep for calls, synthesize information, build customer-facing materials, and automate repetitive tasks. This is how you work, not something you're exploring. Ramp is a builder culture: if you don't instinctively reach for AI before doing things manually, this role will be a hard adjustment.

 - Data-driven book management — You prioritize your time based on usage, revenue, and risk signals, not on who emailed last. You can spot an at-risk account months before renewal and know what to do about it.

 - Technical and systems acumen — You're comfortable around major ERP platforms (NetSuite, SAP S/4HANA, Workday, Sage Intacct, or similar) and understand how Ramp fits into a customer's finance stack. You don't need to code, but you can diagnose what's blocking adoption and bring in the right technical partner.

 - Builder mindset — You're energized by building something that doesn't exist yet. This team is new, and you'll help shape the playbooks, programs, and rituals that define how Lifecycle CSMs work, all while running your own book. You bring structure to ambiguity and iterate quickly when something isn't working.

 - 7+ years in enterprise customer success, account management, or consulting — You've spent enough time with complex organizations and senior stakeholders that it's second nature. You know how to keep an enterprise customer successful long after the launch.

NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Consumption-based revenue experience — You've worked with a product where value is measured in usage or spend, not seats, and know how to grow adoption after the contract is signed.

 - Finance domain depth — Exposure to FP&A, accounting software ecosystems (NetSuite, Sage, QuickBooks, Xero), expense management, or CFO-adjacent workflows. Accelerates credibility with Ramp's customer base.

 - Demonstrated commercial impact — You can point to retention, adoption, or renewal outcomes with specific metrics attached — not described in general terms.

 - Background at an AI-first or AI transformation company — not just a company that uses AI, but one where rethinking workflows around it was part of the product or culture

We're looking for a Senior Web Developer to lead complex web projects, shape technical decisions, and help scale the platform behind Relay's growth. You'll own projects from technical planning through launch, mentor other developers, and partner closely with teams across the company.

This is an ideal role for a front-end developer who thrives on ownership, enjoys solving complex technical problems, and wants to make a measurable impact. Your technical judgment will carry weight here, and you'll have the autonomy to challenge assumptions, influence priorities, and shape how we build.

Want to see what we're building? Check out relayfi.com http://relayfi.com and Telegraph https://storybook.relayfi.design/, the design system our engineers use across Relay.

What You’ll Be Doing

 - Project Ownership: Lead complex, multi-part projects end-to-end — define scope, set milestones, coordinate with cross-functional teams, and deliver high-quality work on time. Own what happens after launch by measuring performance, identifying opportunities, and iterating on improvements

 - Technical Architecture: Define the technical approach for features and projects, making thoughtful decisions around server/client boundaries, caching, revalidation, and CDN behaviour. Balance performance, scalability, and technical debt while proactively simplifying systems, improving maintainability, and addressing root causes

 - Content Platform Development: Build and optimize integrations between the headless CMS and front end, developing scalable content models and tools that empower non-technical teams to manage and publish content independently

Who You Are

 - You have 4+ years of front-end development experience, ideally in a high-growth B2B SaaS or fintech environment, with a proven ability to work independently and deliver high-quality solutions

 - You're strong in React, Next.js, and Node, and you write TypeScript by default. Our repo is fully typed in strict mode with type checking enforced in CI, so strong TypeScript proficiency is essential

 - You're skilled in modern front-end architecture, with a strong understanding of server/client boundaries, caching, revalidation, and CDN behaviour. You think in systems, designing scalable solutions while anticipating downstream impacts

 - You're proficient in Tailwind and experienced working with design systems, reusable components, and headless CMS platforms. You understand content modelling and integrations, with experience in Contentful and GraphQL being valuable but not required

 - You have a strong understanding of web performance, accessibility, and technical SEO, including Core Web Vitals (LCP and CLS), image optimization, bundle analysis, WCAG 2.1 AA, semantic HTML, metadata, structured data, sitemaps, and heading hierarchy

 - You actively use AI tools and workflows to improve development efficiency, with the judgment to evaluate outputs, manage risks, and maintain code quality

 - You have strong project management and communication skills, with the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, manage competing priorities, and translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders

 - You're a proactive problem-solver who thinks beyond individual tasks, understands customer needs, challenges assumptions, anticipates downstream impacts, and adapts quickly to new technologies and feedback

Bonus Points

 - You've built analytics, experimentation, and marketing integrations using tools like Segment, GTM, Statsig, and HubSpot

 - You've worked with AWS Amplify Hosting or similar CI/CD platforms and built end-to-end tests using Playwright or equivalent tools

 - You've built animations using GSAP or Framer Motion and have experience with SCSS

The Interview Process

 - Stage 2: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with our Director, Web

 - Stage 3: A take-home technical challenge

 - Stage 5: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team

We believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.

jobs.description:

Relay processes millions of dollars in deposits, wires, checks, and card transactions every business day, and 321,000+ small business owners trust us with their money. The Transaction Monitoring team is why that trust is warranted. Every transaction we review is a decision: hold or release, investigate or clear. We're looking for someone with real transaction monitoring experience who is curious, decisive, and excited to build with AI, not just work a queue.

 - Review and investigate suspicious activity across every payment channel: deposits, checks, wires, and card transactions

 - Detect patterns that don't belong: velocity abuse, accounts moving money in ways that don't match their profile, business email compromise, altered items

 - Document your investigations clearly and completely — your case notes are read by compliance, our bank partner, and potentially examiners

 - Suggest improvements to fraud rules and controls: flag rules that are generating false positives, spot gaps that let bad activity through, and bring recommendations to Risk Strategy so your findings shape how we detect fraud

 - Collaborate with Compliance, Customer Experience, and Product to resolve cases quickly without compromising on risk

 - You're curious and investigative. When something doesn't add up, you dig into the why instead of just flagging it and moving on.

 - You make calls and stand behind them. Holding a deposit means a business can't access their money; releasing it means betting your judgment that it's clean. You're comfortable owning both.

 - You're a problem solver with high agency. You don't just spot issues — you come with solutions and drive them forward without waiting to be asked.

 - You build with AI. You're actively using AI tools in how you work today and you're excited to push what's possible with them.

jobs.description:

You'll join an Application Security team that is deliberately moving away from the advisory model most AppSec functions are stuck in. You’ll work across our stack (from TypeScript and Node.js, to Postgres and AWS cloud infrastructure) ensuring our applications are secure from design to deployment. You’ll blend technical depth with systems thinking, working across teams to identify risks, build guardrails, and evolve our security practices as Relay scales.

Your mission is to own at least one AppSec process end to end, guide developers on how to solve challenging security problems and adapt traditional security solutions to the new AI landscape.

This is a role with room to grow. You'll be working next to senior engineers who are maintaining our auth system and building our DAST tooling from scratch. The Relay AppSec team genuinely enjoys Application Security and is looking to make an impact on the field.

 - Threat modeling & offensive testing: Threat model technical design documents (TDDs) and run white-box penetration tests on our testing environment to identify vulnerabilities from an attacker’s point of view.

 - VDP & bug bounty: Triage researcher reports, reproduce/assess impact, coordinate fixes with owners, and close the loop with clear comms and durable controls.

 - Shipping the fixes you can: Contributing directly to Relay’s code base when it makes sense — writing the patch, not filing the ticket.

 - Working in our security tooling and extending it: Datadog security, secrets scanning and logging, Burp Suite, and in-house tools you'll be expected to modify rather than just operate.

 - Building with AI as a default: Claude Code and Cursor are daily drivers on this team, not a pilot program.

 - Joining the team's rhythms: Two weekly standups, a biweekly security champions session with product engineers, and a weekly Hack The Box session.

 - Software supply chain: Enforce provenance: SBOM on every build, dependency pinning/owner verification, private registries/proxies, and runtime SCA detections.

Who You Are

 - You have 5 to 6 years of professional security experience. Application security, penetration testing, or product security engineering or similar roles.

 - You've shipped production code: Production-level software real users depended on. And you can read an unfamiliar codebase well enough to fix something in it, which is most of this job.

 - Security fundamentals: Deep understanding of OWASP Top 10 and real-world exploitation/mitigation techniques.

 - You build with AI. You use AI tooling in your daily work and you've built something with it. You can talk about where it gets things wrong, not just that it's fast.

 - Clear communicator & collaborator: You are a collaborator who loves to partner with developers to bring value to customers in the most secure way possible.

 - Ownership: You have a sense of responsibility towards problems and take ownership over them making sure nothing is forgotten and stakeholders stay informed.

 - Mentorship: You are comfortable mentoring team members and members of other teams on security best practices.

jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

 

Our mission is to increase the success rate of small businesses. Traditional banking has been a growth limiter rather than a growth enabler for business owners, and we're changing that. Relay is the all-in-one, collaborative money management platform. We're building for employer SMBs and their finance function, and we're focused on delivering a human-centric customer experience.

Relay processes millions of dollars in deposits, wires, checks, and card transactions every business day, and 321,000+ small business owners trust us with their money. The Transaction Monitoring team is why that trust is warranted. Every transaction we review is a decision: hold or release, investigate or clear. Good decisions mean legitimate business owners get their money fast and bad actors get stopped before they succeed.

We're looking for someone with real transaction monitoring experience who is curious, decisive, and excited to build with AI, not just work a queue.

What You'll Be Doing:

 - Own the risk strategy and operating model for new products, beginning with credit and payroll

 - Build and manage day-to-day risk operations, ensuring reviews and decisions are timely, consistent, and high quality as volumes scale

 - Lead and develop the team through clear expectations, coaching, training, and ongoing feedback

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, and other teams early in product development to identify risks and design appropriate controls

 - Develop, test, and optimize risk rules and strategies while balancing loss prevention, customer experience, and operational impact

 - Define and monitor metrics across losses, customer friction, decision quality, review volumes, and operational efficiency

 - Build scalable procedures, review workflows, tooling, quality controls, and escalation paths

 - Investigate operational and control failures, identify root causes, and translate findings into lasting improvements

Who You Are:

- You have 4+ years of experience in fraud risk, credit risk, risk strategy, transaction monitoring, or risk operations, preferably in fintech, banking, or payments

 - You have meaningful credit risk experience and understand how risk decisions affect losses, growth, operations, and customer experience

 - You’re proficient in SQL and can independently retrieve and analyze data using joins, aggregations, CTEs, subqueries, and window functions

 - You’ve built a new product, risk program, or operating model from zero to one

 - You combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution and can turn ideas into measurable outcomes

 - You understand transaction and money-movement risks across channels such as ACH, cards, wires, or checks

 - You’re analytical and curious, digging into the “why” and using data to make better decisions

 - You’re a strong communicator who can translate complex insights into clear, actionable direction

 - You’re highly collaborative and can navigate work across Risk, Product, Engineering, Data, Compliance, and Customer Experience

 - You thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and are excited to continuously learn new products

 - You’re actively using AI tools in how you work today and are excited to push what’s possible with them
 
 

Bonus Points:

 - You have payroll risk or ACH operations experience

 - You’ve worked with SMB credit, commercial cards, or lending products

 - You’re proficient in Python for advanced analysis or automation

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

At Relay, product management is about outcomes, not outputs. We start with real customer problems and build solutions that move the needle for SMBs, and for our business. Our team pairs long-term vision with rapid iteration. We believe that trust is a product feature, and that usability, reliability, and polish aren’t afterthoughts, they’re core to how we earn the confidence of business owners.

Every launch is measured, every release is a chance to learn, and we prioritize relentlessly so we can focus on what matters most. Above all, we never compromise on customer empathy or product craft.

Why this role matters

Many small businesses walk a constant cashflow tightrope, and the average SMB has just 27 days of cash on hand. They’re juggling payroll, inventory, contractor payments, and everyday expenses, all while trying to carve out resources to invest in growth. Product Managers at Relay play a central role in solving these problems by building financial products that are simple, intuitive, and impactful.

As Senior Product Manager, you’ll lead a major product area from end-to-end (e.g. core banking, risk, AI Insights, payroll etc). You’ll take new products and features from zero to one, scale existing ones, and directly impact how thousands of entrepreneurs run their businesses.

In your first year, you might:

 - Launch and iterate on high priority products ensuring the experiences are simple, intuitive, and trustworthy.

 - Improve customer outcomes by driving integrations with banking, accounting, or payment platforms.

 - Collaborate with Risk, Data, and Operations to ensure Relay’s products are reliable, secure, and insight-driven.

 - Build narratives and roadmaps that align stakeholders, clarify priorities, and inspire confidence, even in the face of ambiguity.

 - Partner with Sales, Marketing, and CX to deliver successful launches and drive adoption among SMB customers.

What You’ll Be Doing:

 - Own impactful products end-to-end: define the vision, set the roadmap, and deliver high-impact outcomes shaping how SMBs understand, manage, and spend their money.

 - Treat your product like a business: define and track KPIs, monitor performance, and make decisions rooted in data, customer insights, and company goals.

 - Ship high-quality products from ideation to launch: partner closely with design and engineering as part of a leadership trifecta, raising the bar for usability, craft, and polish.

 - Build and tell the story for your product: create clear narratives that inspire leadership, cross-functional partners, and customers; even in ambiguous situations.

 - Stay deeply connected to SMB customers: immerse yourself in their workflows and pain points, ensuring we’re solving meaningful problems and delivering products that feel both intuitive and delightful.

jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

Our mission is to increase the success rate of small businesses. Traditional banking has been a growth limiter rather than a growth enabler for business owners, and we're changing that. Relay is the all-in-one, collaborative money management platform. We're building for employer SMBs and their finance function, and we're focused on delivering a human-centric customer experience.

Relay processes millions of dollars in deposits, wires, checks, and card transactions every business day, and 321,000+ small business owners trust us with their money. Every one of them started in the same place: an application. The Onboarding team is Relay's front door. Every application we review is a decision: approve or decline, verify or request more. Good decisions mean legitimate business owners get banking fast and bad actors never get in.

We're looking for someone early in their career — new grads included — who is curious, decisive, and excited to build workflow improvements, not just work a queue.

 - Review and decision new business applications end-to-end: compliance checks, KYC/KYB, document verification, and fraud review

 - Make approve/decline calls and own them — verify the signals, check the story, make the call. Review customer documentation and verify business activity to support your decisions.

 - Detect patterns that don't belong: synthetic identities, business profiles that don't match the story, altered or fraudulent documents, signals that don't add up

 - Document your reviews clearly and completely — your decisions and case notes are read by compliance

 - Suggest improvements to onboarding rules and controls: flag rules generating false positives, spot gaps that let bad actors through, and bring recommendations to Risk Strategy and your pod lead so your findings shape how we decide

 - Balance risk and customer experience — every decision trades fraud prevention against friction for a real business trying to open an account

 - Use AI tools daily to investigate faster, pull data, and improve how the team works

 - You're a problem solver with high agency. You don't just spot issues — you come with solutions and drive them forward without waiting to be asked.

 - You don't clock out at the minimum. Repetitive queue work doesn't drain you — you sustain high output and treat the reps as where the improvement ideas come from.

 - You build with AI. You're actively using AI tools today, and you can show a concrete example of doing something with AI you couldn't have done without it.

 - You're energized by ambiguity. Risk work rarely comes with a playbook — grey-area judgment calls sharpen you rather than stall you.

 - You seek out feedback. You see directness as respect, treat feedback as fuel, and update your thinking fast.

 - You're Toronto-based, able to work hybrid, and open to one of this role's two schedules: Wednesday–Sunday (Monday/Tuesday off; weekend days worked remotely) or Monday–Friday, 1:00pm–9:00pm ET.
 

BONUS POINTS

 - Exposure to fintech, banking, payments, fraud, or risk — through coursework, co-ops, internships, or projects

 - SQL proficiency — you can pull your own data without waiting on analytics

 - You have strong interpersonal skills, a growth mindset, and the adaptability to thrive in a fast-scaling, evolving environment

 - You have experience in fintech, accounting software, or a neobank

 - You have sold through a channel, partner, or referral motion

jobs.description:
