Relay's data engineering team has tripled in size, from 4 to 12, and is now splitting into two teams. Analytics Data Engineering works close to the business, building the models, pipelines and dashboards that teams use to run the company. Data Platform, the team you'll lead, owns the foundation underneath: infrastructure, cost, real-time data, observability, and the AI capabilities the rest of Relay builds on.

The team's north star is platform health. That means a fast, reliable, cost-efficient platform with strong observability, and partners across the company who can do their work without waiting on us.

What You'll Be Doing

 - Lead and grow a senior team of data engineers. With an experienced team in place, your role is to provide direction, challenge thinking, and help the team make decisions and move work forward.

 - Own Snowflake cost. In your first 90 days, you’ll develop and execute a plan to reduce Snowflake costs month over month, working closely with the team to identify and deliver savings.

 - Get data into stakeholders' hands faster. You'll define and drive Relay's approach to real-time data and platform enablement, including streaming (Kafka) and a Snowflake MCP server that opens our data to AI tooling.

 - Make platform health visible. Build observability so the team finds a problem before a stakeholder does.

 - Translate platform work into business outcomes. You’ll help the team prioritize upgrades, migrations and refactors by linking technical investments to business value, whether that’s driving revenue, improving efficiency or reducing risk.

 - Balance speed against technical debt, in both directions. Sometimes you'll persuade the team to ship with some debt because the business value is there. Sometimes you'll persuade the business to give the team more time. You'll know which is which.

 - Run the team's operating rhythm. That includes standups, sprint and roadmap planning, architectural decisions, code review, and the requests that come in from across Relay.

Who You Are

 - You have at least two years of experience managing engineers, including senior team members with strong technical perspectives and the expertise to back them up.

 - You have deep, hands-on production experience with Snowflake and dbt, including building data models.

 - You've owned a production data platform, and ideally you've led meaningful improvements to one, such as cutting cost, improving reliability or adding new capability.

 - You challenge decisions with curiosity, not authority. You ask why before you ask how long, and you can find a path that serves both the engineer's concern and the business deadline.

 - You lead with context. You explain the problem, the metric and the business case before the architecture.

 - You're highly fluent with AI tools, both in how you work and in how you'd guide a team building AI-enabled data capabilities.

 - AWS or GCP

 - Fivetran and Hightouch

 - Terraform

 - Kafka or other real-time data infrastructure

jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. Your mission: put the right limits in the hands of Relay's largest customers and keep that portfolio healthy as it scales.

What You'll Be Doing

 - Underwrite our largest customers by hand. Spread income statements and balance sheets and set limits after manually reviewing the business and financial risk of those entities..

 - Watch the portfolio without watching every account. Build AI-assisted monitoring for financial and qualitative risk signals.

 - Build pre-approval lists for sales. Review existing Relay customers who don't yet have a card, and work with the Sales team on a cross-sell motion.

 - Partner closely with revenue. Explain credit decisions in plain language, work through requests for larger limits, and join customer conversations when we need their financials.

 - Keep credit policy current with our funding partner. Make sure what we approve stays within the policy our partner will fund, and update that policy as the portfolio grows.

 - Own charge card escalations. Be the expert Customer Experience escalates to for documentation requests, decline reasons and credit questions they can't resolve.

 - Build what isn't there yet. Find the next process, report or tool the function needs, and build it.
 
 

Who You Are

 - You've done manual commercial credit underwriting at a corporate or commercial card issuer, from large issuers to card-focused fintechs. US experience is not required.

 - You're strong at financial statement analysis. You can spread statements and defend a limit from the balance sheet, income statement and liquidity picture.

 - You use AI and data tools to work faster, and you can show how they've changed the way you underwrite or monitor a portfolio.

 - You work well with sales. You can explain a decline or a smaller limit without losing the relationship.

 - You figure out what work needs doing instead of waiting for the next case in the queue.

Bonus points

 - SQL, especially in Snowflake

 - Experience spreading statements in Heron or a similar tool

 - Familiarity with S&P or Moody's financial statement models and business credit bureaus

jobs.title: Founding Account Executive, Los Angeles
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

We’re seeking a Los Angeles sales professional with a track record of success in achieving new business and growing a current book of business. The ideal candidate will be driven, organized, and display a natural ability to build rapport and trust. We’re looking for that perfect blend of sales drive coupled with a customer-first mentality that will help us create loyal, happy customers.

Rho has built a substantial community in the New York startup market. Hosting community-driven events, curated get-togethers, and more for founders and teams in the ecosystem has spread the Rho brand across many verticals. Los Angeles will be growing at the same speed and the Rho team with it. You will be responsible for organizing and attending Rho-sponsored events throughout the market geared towards building community and onboarding new business.

jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer at Rho, you'll build the financial infrastructure powering the next generation of founders. This isn't a role where you sit inside a lane. You'll move across the stack, own problems end-to-end, and talk directly to the customers using what you ship. We're hiring engineers who are restless about impact, reach for AI tools the way other people reach for documentation, and genuinely want to understand why what they're building matters.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own problems from scoping to production. Write the code, ship it, watch it land.

 - Work across the stack. You go where the problem is, not where your comfort zone ends.

 - Talk to customers. Sit in on calls, read support tickets, watch session replays. Build what people actually need.

 - Use AI in your daily workflow. Code generation, debugging, spec drafting, and spot where it changes what's possible.

 - Move fast and iterate in the open. Get something in front of users, then make it better.

 - Pick up what's falling. If something's broken, fix it.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of software engineering experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

 - Genuine full-stack flexibility. You've shipped across the stack and don't treat the backend/frontend divide as a hard boundary.

 - Genuine AI fluency. You use these tools every day and think about where they raise the ceiling on what you can build.

 - A bias to ship. You'd rather get something in front of a user than perfect it in a doc.

 - Customer curiosity. You want to know the person on the other side of what you're building, and you'll go find out.

 - High agency. You make progress when things are unclear, surface problems early, and own your outcomes.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

jobs.title: Design Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

A ROLE FOR THOSE COMMITTED TO DESIGNING WITH UNCOMMON CARE.

Most of a banking product is invisible when it's done right. The transfer that confirms with a motion so clean you feel it settle. The card that materializes like it was always going to. The empty state you almost want to keep looking at. Nobody files a support ticket about these things. They just trust the product a little more, and they can't tell you why.

We're hiring a Lead or Staff Design Engineer to own exactly that layer: the feel. The motion, the microinteractions, the details most companies never get to because they're too busy shipping features. We are not too busy. We think this is the work.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You live in the browser, in code, in the space between "it functions" and "it feels inevitable." You build the interactions, the transitions, the animations, and the components that make Rho feel like the most considered product our customers use all day. Then you write the libraries that let the rest of the team hit that bar without you in the room.

This is not a product design role. You're not writing PRDs, running discovery, or owning a roadmap. You're the person who takes something that works and makes it sing, and who builds the systems that make singing the default.

If you've ever reimplemented an animation three times because the first two were 40ms too slow and felt cheap, you already understand the job.

 - Own the feel of the product. Motion, microinteractions, transitions, gestures, the physics of how things move and respond. Every one of them earns trust or spends it.

 - Build the libraries no one else has built. Animation primitives, interaction patterns, and components that are genuinely new, not a re-skin of what's already on npm. We want work that other design engineers screenshot.

 - Ship in code. You build the real thing, in the real medium, at production quality. Figma is where a conversation starts, not where craft is decided.

 - Set the craft bar in motion. Define what "good" feels like at Rho and encode it into a system, tokens, easing curves, timing, springs, so the whole product moves with one considered voice.

 - Sweat details nobody asked you to sweat. The half-pixel. The 20ms. The focus ring. The way a number ticks up. This is the entire job, not a footnote to it.

WHO YOU ARE

You've been doing this for a while, and you have the receipts: at least 7 years building production interfaces, with a body of work that is visibly, unusually crafted. This is a lead role: you set the craft bar for the feel of the product and raise everyone around you to it, through the work itself and the systems you leave behind. We need to see it. A portfolio, a personal site, a component library, shipped work, live demos, something we can open and feel the care in.

You are the kind of person who:

 - Thinks Emil Kowalski and Josh Puckett are describing the job, not the aspiration. If those names mean nothing to you, this role probably isn't yours yet. If they make you nod, keep reading.

 - Has strong opinions about motion. You know why the default ease is wrong, when a spring beats a curve, what makes an animation feel expensive versus cheap, and when the answer is no animation at all. You can defend every one of these.

 - Writes real code. React, TypeScript, CSS at a level where you're building the hard interaction, not styling someone else's. You've probably published a library, or wanted to.

 - Is a genuine craftsperson, not a generalist who dabbles in polish. Your happiest hours are spent alone with a hard interaction problem, iterating past the point most people would call it done.

 - Has taste and can't turn it off. Sloppy motion physically bothers you. You notice the jank in other people's products. You've rebuilt things for free just because they annoyed you.

WHO THIS IS NOT FOR

 - Product designers looking to move into engineering. This is the reverse: a builder who obsesses over feel. If your portfolio is flows, journey maps, and product cases, that's a different (great) role, apply for our Product Designer opening instead.

 - Engineers who tolerate design. You have to love the pixel, not just implement it.

 - Anyone early or mid-career. This is a lead/staff craft role. You need years of taste, reps, and shipped work behind you, and the standing to set the bar for others. We'd love to meet you down the line.

 - People who think "good enough, ship it" is a virtue. It sometimes is. Not here, not on this layer.

 - Anyone who needs the interaction spec handed to them. You define what great feels like; nobody's going to define it for you.

THE BAR

We want Rho to feel like the most crafted financial product in the world, calm, confident, alive. Restraint over decoration. Motion with a reason. Details that reward the customer even when they don't consciously notice. If you've read this far and you're already thinking about how you'd rebuild one of our transitions, we should talk.

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $130,000 - $300,000. Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Rho is building a modern finance platform that helps businesses manage banking, cards, expenses, bill pay, and accounting workflows in one connected platform.
We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build and scale new financial products from ambiguous opportunity to production-grade systems. This role is for a product-minded backend engineer with strong technical judgment, deep customer curiosity, and the ability to drive complex initiatives across teams, stakeholders, and external partners.

This is a high-ownership role for an engineer who wants to build more than features. You'll help shape new product areas, bring complex financial workflows to life, work directly with cross-functional partners, and grow into broader technical leadership as Rho scales.
You'll work on critical financial workflows and platform capabilities that sit close to how businesses manage money. The work is technically challenging, customer-facing, and often involves regulated systems, operational complexity, and third-party integrations.

What you'll do

 - Own high-impact projects end-to-end, including our accounting integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage Intacct, Xero, Puzzle) that keep customers' books accurate and up to date, from problem definition and technical design through launch, iteration, and operational ownership.

 - Build reliable, scalable backend services that power core accounting and financial workflows, and help us expand into new adjacent product areas as the platform grows.

 - Turn ambiguous product and business problems into simple, durable technical solutions.

 - Develop a deep understanding of our customers' accounting and financial operations pain points, and use that context to make pragmatic product and engineering decisions.

 - Partner closely with Product, Design, Operations, Compliance, and external partners, including accounting software providers and financial data platforms like Plaid and Finicity, to move complex initiatives forward.

 - Make thoughtful technical tradeoffs, with a particular focus on shipping quickly without compromising the reliability of money movement.

 - Raise the engineering bar through clear communication, strong system design, code quality, and mentorship.

What we're looking for

 - Senior-level experience building production backend systems, APIs, services, or distributed systems.

 - Strong product judgment, customer curiosity, and comfort working through ambiguity.

 - Experience owning projects end-to-end is a plus, but we also value engineers who've built deep expertise in complex systems without owning every stage of the lifecycle.

 - Ability to manage multiple stakeholders and work cross-functionally with non-technical teams.

 - Experience operating in fast-paced, high-growth environments where priorities evolve quickly.

 - A bias toward shipping, learning from users, and continuously improving what you build.

 - Experience with fintech, accounting systems, payroll, payments, banking, compliance-heavy products, or complex integrations is a plus.

Tech we use
Python, Go, GraphQL, PostgreSQL, Docker, Kubernetes, and GCP. Experience with this exact stack is helpful, but not required. We care more about strong engineering fundamentals, product ownership, and the ability to learn quickly.

What we offer
Our people are our most valuable asset. Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, geographic location, and business needs.

Benefits:

- Top-notch Private Healthcare Insurance for you and your family members

 - Generous PTO policy

 - Lunch at work

 - Covered costs for parking for onsite staff

 - Learning and development budget

 - Paternity leave

 - Hybrid work environment (with old town Belgrade office)

Diversity is a core value at Rho. We’re passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems, and drive solutions that align with our mission. We welcome all qualified applications and support each of our Rho’ers with ongoing professional growth opportunities.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

THE ROLE

Rho is hiring Product Managers, but what we truly seek are GMs/Product CEOs. You'll own a meaningful surface of the platform end-to-end — close enough to the work and close enough to the customer that your judgment is earned, not inherited from a roadmap. You'll know what founders need before they ask, because you've built the intuition that comes from proximity, not process.

How products get built is fundamentally changing. AI is collapsing the line between thinking about something and making it real. The best PMs right now aren't just writing specs — they're prototyping with frontier models, testing ideas the same afternoon they have them, and building product that couldn't have existed a year ago. If that's already how you work, keep reading.

Rho is rebuilding the finance stack for the innovation economy. What happens next depends on the quality of our decisions and the speed at which we make them. The PMs we hire are how we get there.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Operate like a founder. Your surface is your company: its metrics are your P&L, its problems are yours whether or not they're in your job description. Nobody assigns founders their work. Default to motion — ship the scrappy version, learn, ship again, and unblock yourself instead of waiting. The surfaces you touch move faster because you're on them.

And build for them. Develop a deep, almost unfair understanding of how early-stage companies think about money, time, and risk. Design for the workflow they don't know they want yet — the desire path, not the paved one.

Own a problem space, not a problem. Not a feature, not a ticket queue — a living territory of customer problems that shift and collide. Frame the ones that matter, sharpen the hypothesis, define success before you build, and see it through to landing in a founder's hands. The map will change under you; redraw it and keep moving.

Decide what matters most — and re-decide when the facts change. Make deliberate calls about what to do now, next, and never. Hold them loosely: when the evidence says pivot, you pivot without ego. A PM who can't say no is just a project manager with better slides.

Work at the frontier. AI is your leverage in both directions: it 10x's how you work — more ideas tested, more prototypes built, more customer insight absorbed, more shipped — and it expands what you can build, product experiences that weren't possible twelve months ago. You're expected to find both. When a new capability drops, you're the one asking what it unlocks for our customers.

Get in the weeds. You're prototyping, pressure-testing, and iterating alongside design and engineering — with opinions about the details. Bring people along while you're there: partner deeply across Engineering, Design, Operations, GTM, and leadership, and communicate the why so well the team could make your calls without you in the room.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 3+ years building products — as a founder, PM, or engineer or equivalent experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment — and you've shipped work you're proud to put your name on.

 - You have frontier fluency. You work with AI daily — prototyping, analyzing, drafting, automating — and you can point to something you shipped or changed because a new capability made it possible. Not theorizing; doing.

 - You have taste. You hold your own view of what good looks like, obsess over the details, and know that in a banking product, every interaction carries trust.

 - You have discovery rigor. You can articulate the problem, the hypothesis, and how you'll know it worked before you've written a spec.

 - You build. You're not above opening a prototype, sketching a flow, or pulling the data yourself.

 - You think like a founder. You've been one, worked next to one, or operated like one — you take ownership past the edges of your role, and you pull things over the line that would die in someone else's backlog.

 - You're at home in ambiguity. You make calls on incomplete information and treat a pivot as new information, not a setback. Plans change; you're the steady one when they do.

 - You bring people with you. You build trust quickly, communicate proactively, and can align a room even when the answer is no.

 - You crave a team that pushes you — smart, ambitious people who make the work fun and help you grow faster than you thought possible.

Our people are our most valuable asset. Our target compensation range for this role is $165,000 - $320,000. Compensation will be determined by leveling and performance throughout the interview process. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

jobs.title: Staff / Principal Product Designer, Design Systems
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Rho — New York (in person)

Rho is building the best business banking platform on earth. Not "one of." The best.

We're looking for a Staff or Principal Product Designer to own our design system, the governed, in code foundation that everything we ship stands on. This is not a role where you maintain a Figma library and file tickets. This is the role where you define the frontend layer of a financial operating system that companies trust with their money.

It's a long post on purpose. We'd rather you know exactly what this is before you apply.

What you'd actually own

Our design system is becoming the governed frontend layer of the product, components in code, rules enforced through lint and CI, documentation an AI agent can query and build against on spec. You would own that. The architecture, the tokens, the primitives, the motion language, the governance, the contribution model, and the standards that let 80 plus engineers and PMs ship on bar without a designer babysitting every pixel.

You'll partner with our frontend guild, our engineers, and the design team as genuine equals, not as a service desk. You'll decide what a component is, how it behaves, how it moves, what it enables, and where it must not bend. You'll set the craft bar for the entire org and then build the system that makes hitting that bar the path of least resistance.

Who this is for

You've been doing this for a while. We mean it, at least 7 years of product design experience, with real design systems ownership at scale. Not "contributed to a design system." Owned one. Built one. Governed one. Watched it get abused and fixed the governance so it couldn't happen again.

You are the kind of person who:

 - Designs in code, or is hungry to. You believe Figma is not the build environment, and that designing in the real medium eliminates a whole category of hidden QA cost. If the phrase "design engineer" makes you lean forward, hi.

 - Has genuine taste and a serious bar for it. Branding, typography, motion, microinteractions: you sweat all of it. You have opinions about easing curves and you can defend them. A transition that feels half a beat off bothers you until it's fixed.

 - Owns your craft, doesn't inherit it. You can point at a visual language and say "I built that," not "that was set before I got there and I adjusted the fonts."

 - Builds systems, not screens. You think in primitives, states, edge cases, and two-way doors. When something breaks at a thousand users, you already designed for it.

 - Ships, then sharpens. You move fast, you work out loud, you share the messy middle instead of disappearing for three weeks and returning with a monument. Perfect but late is a fail here.

 - Has low ego and high standards at the same time. You hold a firm craft bar and you genuinely want the critique. You defend decisions with reasoning, not with "it's my stylistic choice."

 - Gets the domain, or is dying to. Financial workflows are dense, multi-role, permission scoped, and unforgiving. You find that fun, not frightening.

Who this is NOT for

A few honest filters, to save us both time.

Do not apply to this role if you are junior. This is a Staff/Principal position. If you're earlier in your career, we'd genuinely love to meet you, we just want you in the right process. Apply for our product designer role instead: https://www.rho.co/careers/f4ece49b-3b53-4ffb-861f-9cc972c10b27

It's also probably not your fit if:

 - Your portfolio is process decks, tiny mockups, and journey maps, and the actual UI is nowhere to be found. We evaluate craft at the pixel level. If we can't see it, we can't hire it.

 - Your idea of a design system is a color palette and a component library nobody governs.

 - Motion and micro interactions are afterthoughts to you rather than part of the craft.

 - You need a fully specced ticket before you can move, and ambiguity makes you freeze.

 - You want to be handed the vision. We want someone who brings one.

 - "Move fast" reads to you as "lower the quality bar." Here it means the opposite, the bar is high AND the pace is high, and the system you build is how those two coexist.

 - You lead with an AI chatbot case study. We love AI and use it every day. But a conversational UI is not a demonstration of end-to-end product craft.

How we work

Small pods. Artifact first. Designers own their surfaces end to end, including research, QA, and the fight to get it shipped right. We use AI natively and expect you to. The design team is heads down on building the governed frontend layer this quarter, and this role is central to it.

We're in the office in New York because the best systems work happens shoulder to shoulder, obsessing over a real screen.

The bar

Restraint over decoration. Confidence over noise. Interfaces that feel calm because someone sweated every detail so the user never has to, and that feel alive because the motion is considered, not bolted on. We care about how money moving feels, how a card creation confirms, how a state transition lands. If "it looks fun, but does it do anything" is a question you ask yourself unprompted, you'll fit right in.

How to apply

If you've read this far and you're already thinking about how you'd architect our token layer, we should talk.

Come ready to do two things when we meet, walk us through a real, working file (not just the polished case study frames), and show us a design system you actually built and governed. Bring one deeply complex, systems level project and one piece you're proud of at the pixel level, and tell us plainly which decisions were yours.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist/ML
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

Our team is looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our data products team. This role has significant latitude to shape how modeling, evaluation, and ML infrastructure work here: the standards, tooling, and processes you help establish will influence how models get built for a long time to come.

This is intentionally a hybrid role. At many companies, data science and ML infrastructure are split into separate functions: data scientists author and train models, while a dedicated platform team owns deployment, observability, and retraining. At Rho, we need someone who can do both, someone who can build the model and reason clearly about how it gets deployed, monitored, and retrained in production. You'll work on high-leverage problems like our transaction coding suggestion engine, OCR/document understanding pipeline, and RAG-based and agentic systems, while also helping build the underlying foundation: evaluation frameworks, model deployment and monitoring practices, and the infrastructure decisions that determine whether ML at Rho is reliable and scalable. This role requires genuine fluency in ML infrastructure and evals, not just modeling - you should be as comfortable discussing feature store design or eval harness architecture with data engineers as you are validating a model's statistical soundness.

Technologies we use for data: Python, Snowflake, DBT, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, MLflow, Terraform, Prometheus, Google Cloud Services, Omni, Hex, PowerBI

Responsibilities:

- Help define and evolve Rho's ML/DS practices: how models get evaluated, deployed, monitored, versioned, and retrained

 - Design and implement evaluation frameworks and eval harnesses that give the company real confidence in model quality, before and after launch

 - Build and own high-impact models and analyses powering products like transaction coding suggestions, OCR/document understanding, and RAG/agentic systems

 - Make and document key ML infrastructure decisions (model registries, feature stores, serving patterns, monitoring/alerting for drift and degradation) in close partnership with data engineering

 - Set technical standards and best practices that help the ML/DS practice scale as the team grows

 - Translate ambiguous business problems into well-scoped modeling questions

 - Design and analyze experiments (A/B tests, causal inference) to validate model impact rigorously

 - Advocate for and drive adoption of ML infrastructure and tooling improvements as needs grow

Requirements:

- 6+ years of experience in data science, applied ML, or a related quantitative field, with a track record of shipping models into production

 - Deep, hands-on understanding of ML infrastructure: model registries, feature stores, serving architectures, monitoring/observability for models, and retraining pipelines

 - Strong experience designing evaluation frameworks and evals for ML systems;, including offline metrics and ongoing production evaluation

 - Comfortable operating as a hybrid DS/infrastructure practitioner:, someone who doesn't hand a model off to a platform team and walk away, but who can own it end to end when needed

 - Experience helping establish or mature ML practices, standards, or infrastructure within a team and company

 - Strong programming skills in Python, with solid SQL

 - Comfortable making infrastructure trade-off decisions jointly with data/platform engineers, and able to speak credibly on both the modeling and systems sides

 - Experience with statistical modeling, machine learning techniques, and experiment design

jobs.title: Law Firm & Accounting Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Rho is looking for a Law Firm & Accounting Partnerships Lead to own two of our highest-leverage referral channels: the startup law firms that incorporate companies on day one, and the accounting, bookkeeping, and outsourced CFO firms that run their books from day two onward. These are the advisors founders trust before they ever pick a bank — and the firms that shape which financial stack a company lands on.

You'll own this channel end to end: strategy, partner sourcing, negotiation, launch, enablement, and the revenue that comes out of it. This is a builder role, not a maintenance role. You'll inherit early relationships and a real product story, and your mandate is to turn that into a repeatable, quota-carrying channel with a named partner roster, a working referral motion, and reporting leadership can trust.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

OWN THE CHANNEL STRATEGY

 - Define the segmentation and target list for both sides of the channel: startup-focused law firms (formation, emerging companies, venture practices) and accounting/bookkeeping/OCFO firms

 - Build the business case for where to invest — which firms, which geographies, which practice groups drive the most qualified client referrals

 - Set the partner tiering model and the value exchange at each tier (co-marketing, dedicated support, revenue share, product access)

 - Own the channel number: sourced pipeline, referred accounts, funded accounts, and revenue contribution

SOURCE AND CLOSE PARTNERS

 - Prospect, pitch, and close new law firm and accounting firm partnerships — this is a hunting role, not an inbound one

 - Build relationships with multiple stakeholders inside each firm: managing partners, practice group leads, business development, and the associates and staff who actually make the referral

 - Structure and negotiate partnership terms alongside Legal and Finance

 - Represent Rho at the conferences, bar association events, CPA gatherings, and founder dinners where these relationships get built (expect meaningful travel to major tech hubs)

DRIVE REFERRALS AND PARTNER REVENUE

 - Turn signed partnerships into activated ones — a logo on a page is not a partnership

 - Run onboarding and enablement so partner teams know exactly when and how to introduce Rho to a client

 - Build the co-marketing motion with Marketing: webinars, CPE-eligible content, perk pages, newsletters, and joint events

 - Run MBRs/QBRs with top partners against shared goals, and prune the partners who aren't producing

BE THE VOICE OF THE CHANNEL INTERNALLY

 - Work cross-functionally with Sales, Onboarding, Support, and Product to make sure referred clients get a white-glove handoff

 - Bring structured feedback to Product on what law firms and accounting partners need from Rho — multi-entity views, advisor access, close workflows, integrations

 - Partner with Sales leadership so channel-sourced deals are worked, tracked, and credited cleanly

BUILD THE OPERATING SYSTEM

 - Stand up the infrastructure that makes the channel scale: partner CRM hygiene, referral attribution, pipeline tracking, and a partner portal experience

 - Document the playbook — partner onboarding, referral handoff, enablement, and event workflows — so the next hires ramp fast

 - Produce clear, regular reporting on channel-sourced pipeline and revenue for leadership
 
 

WHO YOU ARE

 - 5+ years in partnerships, channel, or a closing sales role — ideally at a fintech, B2B SaaS, or professional services platform selling into or through advisors

 - You've carried a number and hit it. You're comfortable with a quota tied to partner-sourced revenue

 - You've built something from scratch. You know the difference between running a program and starting one, and you want the second

 - Credible with professionals: you can hold a real conversation with a managing partner about their book of business, not just pitch a product

 - Strong commercial instincts — you can structure a deal, run a negotiation, and know when to walk away

 - Excellent written and verbal communicator; you can present to an executive audience and write a partner email that actually gets replies

 - Data-driven: you instrument the channel, read the numbers, and reallocate effort accordingly

 - Thrives in ambiguity, moves fast, and doesn't need a playbook handed to you — you're writing it

 - Based in the Bay Area and willing to travel (~25–35%)

BONUS POINTS

 - Existing network among startup law firms and/or accounting, bookkeeping, and OCFO firms

 - Background in accounting or law (CPA, JD, or time inside a firm) — you've lived the workflow you're selling into

 - Experience launching a partner program at a fintech or spend management company

 - Familiarity with the startup ecosystem — VCs, accelerators, formation platforms, fund admins

 - Experience with partner CRM/PRM tooling and referral attribution

Why This Role

Law firms and accountants are the highest-trust distribution channel in the startup market — at comparable companies, the accounting channel alone has grown into one of the largest sources of new customers. Rho hasn't built it yet. You'd own that from the ground up, with a direct line to leadership, a clear number, and the room to build a team behind you as the channel proves out.

COMPENSATION

$150-200K OTE
Equity, health/dental/vision, 401(k), and other benefits included.

We’re passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems, and drive solutions that align with our mission. ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Marketing Operations Manager to be the backbone of Rho’s marketing org. This person keeps our work across the team running smoothly, so we can move quickly and leadership always knows what’s live, what’s working, and where to focus next.

In Brand, you’ll own campaign project management, keeping launches on schedule from brief to go-live. You’ll also run brand lift analysis so we can measure what each campaign actually moves. You’ll partner with Growth Engineering and the data science team to turn their work into a reporting cadence that marketing, the exec team, and the board rely on. Working closely with the VP of Marketing, you’ll have the context to spot what needs attention and the process discipline to raise it early, so the whole team stays aligned, hits its numbers, and scales.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the system of record: one place where every workstream across Growth, Brand, and Community is tracked against its owner, status, and the metric it's supposed to move.

 - Run a weekly written review across all three pillars (not a dashboard nobody opens) so slipping work surfaces early instead of reaching the VP of Marketing the night before it matters.

 - Translate the outputs of Growth Engineering and the data science team (funnel performance, cost per funded account, channel health) into reporting marketing, exec, and the board actually run on. You consume these models, you don't build them.

 - Track every vendor and spend commitment against sign-off status; flag anything moving forward without it before it becomes a fait accompli.

 - Maintain a single, current version of marketing strategy and planning docs, replacing the scattered state across Slack, Notion, and individual owners' heads.

 - Run the cadence on hiring, budget, and planning asks that go to Devonaire, Bojan, and other cross-functional partners, so those requests are tracked to a decision instead of going quiet.

 - Keep a live map of who owns what, including backup owners for anything with single-threaded risk, so no function or vendor relationship depends on one person.

 - Flag ownership gaps and conflicting priorities across pillars directly, rather than letting them resolve themselves by default.

 - Run the experimentation program for Growth: intake, prioritization, test design standards, sprint cadence, and a shared learnings log.

REQUIREMENTS

 - You've designed and run an incrementality or lift test (holdout, geo-lift, PSA-style), not just read about the concept. You know what breaks a naive test — seasonality, cross-channel halo, saturation — and how to control for it.

 - You've owned marketing or GTM data where the number mattered financially, and defended a CAC or attribution figure to a skeptical exec.

 - Systems experience, not just analysis: forms, routing, CRM sync, reverse ETL, taxonomy. Comfortable owning plumbing.

 - You define metrics instead of waiting to be handed them.

 - Comfortable as the only person in your function, working across marketing, data engineering, sales ops, and growth without authority over any of them.

jobs.title: Payment Operations Associate
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the role

We're looking for a Payment Operations Associate to support Rho's day-to-day payment processing. You'll process client repayments, issue rewards and credits, resolve payment exceptions, and keep credit and card program settings up to date, working alongside Credit Risk, Client Services, Fraud, Compliance, and our partner bank. The work is deadline-driven and detail-oriented, and it feeds directly into client statements and month-end close.

What you will do

 - Process client repayments. Run recurring ACH pulls for monthly credit repayments on a fixed due-date schedule, handling non-standard accounts manually, and process interim payments as they arise. Confirm each payment is captured accurately from initiation through posting.

 - Issue rewards, credits, and incentives. Calculate and release cashback rewards on a set monthly schedule, reconcile against system-generated figures, and process statement credits, sign-up bonuses, and promotional incentives with the appropriate review and approval. Provide cashback breakdowns to clients on request.

 - Maintain credit and card program settings. Update client credit limits, payment terms, statement cycles and custom pricing, keeping records consistent across systems and documenting every change.

 - Manage wire operations. Handle wire trace requests, recalls, returns, and non-posted wires with our partner bank, and administer enrollments and limit changes for drawdown wire services.

 - Manage ACH operations. Initiate ACH returns and reversals in line with NACHA rules, applying the correct return code and meeting NACHA return/reversal timeframes that apply to each request.

 - Support fraud and credit review. Expedite settlement on transactions once Fraud or Credit has approved them, and hold transactions for review when something looks unusual. Manage RDC returns with outreach to the relevant teams, and set the appropriate settlement delay or instant release on credit repayments based on client credit risk.

 - Report on delinquency. Produce a weekly past-due report for Credit Risk, Finance, Client Services, and Fraud, monitor 30-day credit repayment returns and overdue balances daily, and escalate for client outreach.

 - Route compliance, fraud and legal escalations. Flag sanctions-related inquiries from our partner bank to the right internal teams, forward legal notices to Legal, coordinate Letter of Indemnity and Hold Harmless requests with the Fraud team and request limit increases when transaction thresholds are reached.

 - Support our Letter of Credit program. Coordinate Standby Letters of Credit with our partner bank, fund the collateral account, process the associated fees, and provide Client Services with the figures for month-end fee statements.

 - Improve the process. Identify manual steps worth automating, keep procedure documentation current, and partner with Product and Engineering to close gaps in payment workflows.

 

You have

 - 2+ years in payment operations, banking operations, treasury operations, or a similar function at a fintech, bank, or payment processor.

 - Working knowledge of payment rails — ACH, Fedwire, RTP, card networks, and remote deposit — and what happens when a payment fails, returns, or settles late.

 - Exceptional attention to detail. You reconcile before you release, and you catch the transposed digit.

 - Comfort with recurring hard deadlines and high transaction volume without losing accuracy.

 - Hands-on with operational tooling: ticketing systems (Jira), BI dashboards (Looker), spreadsheets, and bank portals. SQL is a plus, not a requirement.

 - Clear written communicator. Much of this role is coordinating across Credit Risk, Client Services, Fraud, and Compliance in writing.

 - Sound judgment on escalation. You know which items you can resolve and which need Fraud, Credit, or Legal before you touch them.

Our people are our most valuable asset. Our target compensation range for this role is $70,000 - $100,000. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

jobs.title: Growth Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Growth Engineer to make Rho the #1 answer for startup and business banking, both in classic search rankings and in the answers AI engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews give. You'll then extend that position into Rho's newer product lines: incorporation, payroll, and invoicing. For your first six months this is 100% of your focus; after that, you'll take the systems and instincts you built here to the next growth problem.

This is a hands-on building role. You ship production code and page changes yourself, you don't spec them and hand them off. You'll inherit a working agentic SEO/AEO system and make it faster, more reliable, and more autonomous, from the agents that sweep and fix pages around the clock to the runbook that lets it all run without you.

You're accountable for whether Rho wins, not for pages published or dashboards built. AI citation share, rankings on priority keywords, organic signups, and funded accounts from organic are how your work gets judged.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Live in AEO/SEO dashboards: own AI visibility, citations, and sentiment across every tracked topic, and turn weekly deltas into shipped fixes.

 - Run the weekly operating rhythm: competitor intel refresh, a full sweep of AI-citation position by keyword with fixes shipped to existing pages, and an easy-read SEO/AEO scorecard reported every Friday.

 - Ship page changes directly to rho.co http://rho.co through the CMS and codebase: on-page optimization, structured data, internal linking, and new pages, with protected high-value pages routed through review.

 - Own and extend the multi-agent content pipeline (research, drafting, specialist review, compliance gate, marketing sign-off) for new articles and product-page refreshes.

 - Maintain the claims and competitor source-of-truth layer every piece of content is checked against, so nothing ships with an unverified product fact or competitor claim.

 - Monitor technical SEO and AEO health: crawlability and indexing, AI crawler access, site performance, and regressions, caught by alerts rather than by a drop in traffic.

Our Product Managers operate like owners of their surface. The APM role is how we develop the next ones.

You join a senior PM's team and own a defined part of a banking product. You ship to real customers in your first quarter. You get real scope, a direct mentor, and honest feedback every week. The goal: in 18 months, you own a surface as a full PM.

In banking, every interaction carries trust. Money moves, cards get declined, payments settle or fail. You learn how a regulated financial product works from the inside, and you learn to build products that customers trust with their money.

Get close to customers. Talk to founders and finance teams every week. Read support tickets. Learn how early-stage companies think about cash, spend, and risk, and bring that knowledge back to the team.

jobs.title: Staff Security Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About Us

Rho is on a mission to make finance frictionless for organizations. Our team and technology power high-performing companies with an all-in-one, end-to-end finance platform that lets organizations safely manage cash and spending across commercial-grade banking, corporate cards, treasury management, expense management, accounts payable, and more. 

Our customers run their banking, cards, and payments through Rho. We are splitting a large Python monolith into Go and Python services on GCP, and shipping a public API, agents, and MCP surfaces. Security is part of the product. 

The Team 

Security at Rho is small: a VCISO, one security engineer in Poland, and the engineers who ship. You will be the first US security engineer. We plan to grow this into a team over the next six months, and you will help pick who. 

The Role

Hands-on. You write production code most days. You own product and platform security, and you own finding queues and incident response until we hire for detection and response. 

What you'll do
Product Security

 - Threat model new systems and review designs with the teams that own them before they ship. 

 - Build the paved road: secure defaults, guardrails in CI, dependency and supply chain checks, so the safe way is the easy way. 

 - Own the vulnerability lifecycle: triage findings from Pensar, Semgrep, CodeQL, Dependabot, pentests, and inbound researcher reports; hold the SLAs; write the fix or get it written; track remediation to zero. Stand up our vulnerability disclosure program. 

Platform Security

 - Harden GCP and GKE: least-privilege IAM, workload identity, secrets, network policy, environment separation, all in Terraform. 

 - Secure our LLM, agent, and MCP surfaces: guardrails, sandboxes, agents as identities with scoped access, prompt injection detection. 
 

Detection & Response

 - Own detections in our SIEM, tune signal to noise, keep the runbooks current, stand up on the call rotation, and lead incidents end to end: triage, contain, investigate, remediate, post-mortem. 

 - Run tabletop exercises and hunt for what detections miss. 

What we're looking for

 - 6+ years in security engineering, or software engineering with a security focus. You ship code and tools, not only findings.

 - Depth in one of product security, cloud and platform security, or detection and response, and working knowledge of the other two.

 - Comfortable changing production and owning the outcome. Python or Go, Kubernetes, Terraform, one major cloud.

 - You can triage competing risks and trade security against velocity without slowing the team down.

 - Clear writer: design reviews, runbooks and incident reports engineers actually read.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Fintech, payments or another regulated industry. PCI DSS or SOC 2 evidence work.

 - Bug bounty, red team, CVEs, talks, or open source.

 - Hands-on AI security: guardrails, agent identities, prompt injection.

jobs.title: Principal Product Designer
jobs.description:
We are a profitable, mission-driven fintech company building financial solutions for people whose needs go unmet by traditional institutions – people with disabilities, older adults, and people in recovery, and the families and professionals who care for them. We get to wake up every day knowing our work has a profound impact on our customers’ lives, and we run the business with the discipline to keep doing it for the long haul. That track record has earned us a spot on the Forbes Fintech 50 and the Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing companies for the last two years.

Design plays an important strategic role at True Link. We're looking for a Principal Product Designer to join our lean and senior product team as a senior individual contributor. Someone who can operate with a high degree of independence, lead customer insight and research initiatives, and own design quality across two of our core business lines. You’ll act as a design consultant, identifying and advocating for high impact areas per the company OKRs, and for strategic focus to bring customer insights to the table and improve the user experience, in addition to supporting in-flight product initiatives.

You'll work day-to-day with our product managers and engineering leads, reporting to the Head of Design. With you, it will be a design team of two; so high autonomy, but still someone to collaborate with. This isn't a role where you'll wait to be handed a brief - you'll be expected to identify what questions need answering, go get the answers, and translate insight into design decisions that move the product forward.

Our users are wonderfully complex and our products solve real, meaningful problems. We are proud to serve family caregivers, professional fiduciaries, trust administrators, people in recovery, and the people who love and support them.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead end-to-end product design for our Card Platform. From mobile UX iterations of our core product, to iterations of new products as we expand into adjacent categories, to experimental product led growth and AI-powered features like receipt management.

 - Support the design needs of our Trust & Invest business, including micro-iterations on the product, and solving for customer requests.

 - Drive customer insight and research. Identify the open questions that matter; proactively run customer interviews, usability tests, and concept testing; and synthesize findings into clear design implications for both near-term decisions and longer-horizon roadmap thinking.

 - Be the team's strongest advocate for the user perspective in cross-functional discussions, deepening understanding of our customers across the company.

 - Operate as a senior design thought-partner for product and engineering leadership to shape requirements, not just respond to them, which includes navigating stakeholder feedback and applying good judgment about customer discovery versus forward momentum.

 - Represent design in client-facing settings where needed.

 - Produce polished, well-considered design work using our existing design patterns - we're not looking for someone who wants to rethink the foundations. Maintain design coherence across a product suite that serves multiple user types with meaningfully different needs.

 - Handle the full range of design needs: big new features, incremental iterations, mobile polish, and the occasional slide deck or screenshot pull for the sales team.
 

Who You Are

 - An experienced product design leader with 8+ years of product design experience, especially in lean team environments. Experience in fintech, financial services, or a regulated product environment is a plus.

 - Lead with the user. Research and insight generation is something you proactively do, not something you wait to be assigned to you.

 - Stellar end-to-end design chops, from early discovery and concept development through detailed interaction design and QA.

jobs.description:
BUILD SOMETHING PEOPLE LOVE

Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/culture and learn more about how we work https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/careers.

Manager, Treasury Cash & Settlements

Build something people love

Wealthsimple's mission is to help everyone achieve financial freedom – by making financial services simple, transparent, and low-cost. We're Canada's largest fintech, trusted by over 3 million clients with more than $100 billion in assets.

We move fast, we own our work, and we care deeply about the people using our products. If that sounds like you, keep reading.

We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual and learn more about how we work.

About the team

The Finance team is where numbers become decisions. Within Finance, Treasury looks after the cash that moves through Wealthsimple every day — across a growing number of entities, currencies, and products. As we've expanded, so has the complexity of that job: more accounts to watch, more flows to move, more systems to keep working together. This role sits within Cash & Collateral Management and reports to the Senior Manager on that team. We're a small, high-trust group — embedded in the business, not reporting from the sidelines — and we hold ourselves to a high bar for both rigour and clarity. If you want your work to actually shape how the company operates, this is the place to do it.

About the role

Wealthsimple's cash operations have grown more complex as our product line-up has expanded — more entities, more currencies, more moving parts. This role exists to keep that complexity under control: owning the day-to-day movement and monitoring of cash, while also driving the automation work needed to make it scale. It's not a "keep the lights on" role. You'll be expected to build the tools and processes that make cash management faster and more reliable, not just operate what already exists.

This role doesn't have direct reports today, but there's real opportunity to grow into people leadership as the team scales.

What you'll do

 - Own the daily, business-critical money movements that power our products — making sure funds land where they need to, when they need to, across multiple entities and currencies

 - Manage short-term liquidity so there's always enough on hand to fund settlements and meet daily obligations, without idle cash sitting where it shouldn't

 - Analyze and forecast cash needs through detailed bank balance monitoring and flow-of-funds analysis — turning raw account data into decisions the business can act on, including intercompany funding requirements

 - Support new product launches by scoping their cash flow, settlement, and account requirements early

 - Scale and improve the systems we already use for cash management rather than just maintaining them — building automation for balance monitoring, transfers, and forecasting that lets the processes scale efficiently

 - Partner with product, engineering, and finance teams to keep cash operations in step with the business as it moves and expands

Skills you bring

 - 5+ years of experience in treasury, cash management, or corporate banking operations

 - Experience managing cash positioning and forecasting across multiple entities and currencies

 - Strong understanding of banking infrastructure — account structures, payment rails, and settlement processes

 - Experience leading or contributing to the automation of manual treasury or cash processes

 - Advanced Excel and SQL skills, with comfort working with large datasets to drive forecasting and analysis

 - Experience working cross-functionally with product, engineering, or finance teams to support new product launches

 - Clear communication skills — you can explain cash and treasury mechanics to people who don't work in treasury

Nice to have

 - Experience in fintech or a regulated financial services environment

 - Familiarity with treasury management systems (TMS) or ERP treasury modules

 - Exposure to building automation tools using scripting or low-code platforms (e.g., Python, SQL-based workflows)

 - Experience with intercompany funding structures or multi-entity treasury operations

 - Prior experience supporting new product launches from a cash or liquidity perspective

WHY WEALTHSIMPLE?

🌸 Top-tier health benefits and life insurance

📈 Long-term group savings with employer match, through Wealthsimple for Business

🌴 20 vacation days, 4 wellness days, and unlimited sick and mental health days per year*

✈️ 90 days away: work outside Canada for up to 90 days per year*

👥 Employee resource groups, including Rainbow (2SLGBTQ), Women of WS, and Black at WS

🌎 We are a hybrid team with over 1,500 employees across North America. The people are one of the best parts of working here: you'll collaborate with incredibly talented, curious, and driven teammates who are deeply committed to doing great work.

*Unlimited paid sick days, Wellness Days and the 90 day away program do not apply to certain roles. 

ICYMI

Technology & Innovation at Wealthsimple: We move quickly and build thoughtfully. That means we're always looking for better ways to work — whether that's new tools, AI, or rethinking how we approach a problem. We don't expect you to have all the answers, but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to evolve alongside the products we're building.

Inclusion Statement: We're building products for a diverse world, and we need a diverse team to do it well. We strongly encourage applications from everyone, regardless of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability status.

Accessibility Statement: We're committed to an accessible hiring experience. If you need any accommodations throughout the interview process, please let us know — we'll work with you to make sure you have what you need. We also welcome any feedback on how we can better accommodate candidates with accessibility needs.

AI in Hiring: We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our team but don't replace human judgment – all final hiring decisions are made by people. If you have questions about how your data is used, reach out to us.

experience:

jobs.title: Agent(e), Opérations de l'expérience client – Télétravail (CDD)
jobs.description:
BUILD SOMETHING PEOPLE LOVE

Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/culture and learn more about how we work https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/careers.

L'équipe Opérations de l'expérience client façonne, au quotidien, l'expérience que Wealthsimple offre à sa clientèle. Nous gérons les interactions concrètes, par courriel, par clavardage et par téléphone, ainsi que les moments charnières où une personne choisit de nous confier, ou non, sa vie financière. Notre objectif est simple : offrir un soutien rapide, fluide et fiable qui dépasse les attentes des personnes que nous servons.

 - Modèle 100 % télétravail : Ce poste est entièrement à distance. Vous pouvez travailler de n'importe où au Canada.

 - Environnement de travail : Bien que le poste soit à distance, les candidats doivent disposer d'un espace de travail privé, calme et professionnel, doté d'une connexion Internet haute vitesse fiable, afin de garantir la confidentialité et la qualité de nos interactions avec les clients.

 - Date de début visée : le 4 janvier, 2027.

 - Contrat : Engagement initial de 6 mois avec possibilité de prolongation et opportunités d'évolution en interne.

Wealthsimple connaît une croissance rapide, et chaque jour, de plus en plus de Canadiennes et de Canadiens commencent à utiliser notre plateforme. Cette croissance s'accompagne d'un effort tout aussi important pour que notre clientèle ait de moins en moins besoin de nous joindre. Nous nous attaquons aux causes profondes des problèmes courants et créons de meilleurs outils en libre-service, notamment grâce à l'IA, afin que la clientèle puisse régler les questions simples de façon autonome. Notre équipe peut ainsi se concentrer sur les conversations où l'intervention humaine fait toute la différence.

À PROPOS DU POSTE

Quand quelque chose ne fonctionne pas comme la cliente ou le client s'y attendait, c'est vous qui rectifiez le tir. Vous aiderez la clientèle par clavardage, au téléphone et par courriel, en prenant en charge des questions et des problèmes qui demandent une vraie réflexion, et non des réponses toutes faites. Certains jours, il s'agira de démêler une situation complexe; d'autres jours, de rassurer une personne et de l'accompagner étape par étape. C'est un travail exigeant et structuré, qui demande un bon jugement, de l'intelligence émotionnelle et le sens des responsabilités nécessaire pour mener chaque dossier à terme. Bien exercé, ce rôle est l'un des plus importants chez Wealthsimple.

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

 - Aider la clientèle par clavardage, au téléphone et par courriel, en gérant un flux constant de conversations du début à la fin.

 - Accompagner la clientèle dans ce qui compte le plus pour elle, qu'il s'agisse de questions rapides ou de problèmes complexes liés à ses placements ou à ses services bancaires.

 - Écouter attentivement, vous mettre à la place de la clientèle et communiquer avec la clarté, la chaleur et la bienveillance auxquelles elle devrait s'attendre chaque fois qu'elle s'adresse à Wealthsimple.

 - Prendre en charge chaque dossier qui vous est confié : trouver la véritable source du problème, dénicher la réponse même face à une situation inédite et faire un suivi pour que rien ne passe entre les mailles du filet.

 - Travailler selon un horaire établi et atteindre des cibles claires en matière de qualité, de productivité et de respect de l'horaire. Ces cibles sont au cœur de l'évaluation du rendement dans ce poste.

 - Acquérir une connaissance approfondie des produits de Wealthsimple et des notions financières sur lesquelles ils reposent, et continuer d'apprendre au fil de leur évolution.

 - Tirer parti du coaching et de la rétroaction sur la qualité pour perfectionner constamment votre savoir-faire.

VOS DÉBUTS:

 - Excellente maîtrise du français et de l'anglais, avec une communication écrite et orale claire et chaleureuse dans les deux langues (exigence essentielle).

 - Expérience en service à la clientèle, que ce soit en technologie, en hôtellerie et restauration, dans le commerce de détail, dans les services financiers ou dans un autre domaine.

 - Bon jugement et capacité à prendre rapidement de bonnes décisions, même quand la réponse n'est pas évidente.

 - Grande intelligence émotionnelle, notamment la capacité à bien cerner les gens et à garder son sang-froid dans les situations tendues.

 - Débrouillardise et détermination pour trouver des réponses par vous-même.

 - Vitesse et précision au clavier, et agilité pour passer rapidement d'un outil ou d'un système à l'autre sans perdre de vue la clientèle.

 - Aisance à travailler selon un horaire établi et avec des cibles mesurables.

ATOUTS

 - De 1 à 2 ans d'expérience dans les services financiers

QUI VOUS ÊTES

Vous prenez les choses en main. Quand une cliente ou un client vous soumet un problème, ce problème devient le vôtre jusqu'à ce qu'il soit réglé. Vous ne le refilez pas à quelqu'un d'autre en espérant que tout se passe bien. La curiosité vous pousse à comprendre comment les choses fonctionnent, et vous faites preuve de débrouillardise quand la réponse ne saute pas aux yeux. Vous avez à cœur les personnes que vous aidez, et cela se voit : vous sentez quand une personne s'inquiète pour son argent, et vous savez ramener le calme dans la conversation. Enfin, vous avez la détermination nécessaire pour bien faire ce travail jour après jour, même quand la file d'attente déborde et que les problèmes sont difficiles.

Nul besoin d'une formation en finance. Les personnes qui viennent de la technologie, de l'hôtellerie et de la restauration ou du commerce de détail possèdent souvent exactement les compétences que ce poste exige. Ce qui compte le plus, c'est la curiosité, la débrouillardise, l'habitude de résoudre les problèmes par soi-même et un réel souci de la clientèle.

VOS DÉBUTS

Vous apprendrez ce que vous devez savoir une fois parmi nous. Notre programme d'intégration est conçu pour que toute personne ayant les bonnes compétences puisse réussir, peu importe son parcours.

Vous commencerez par une formation sur Wealthsimple : nos produits, notre clientèle, ainsi que les principes et les normes qui guident notre façon de la servir. Vous aurez un aperçu de tout ce que nous faisons. Vous mettrez ensuite ces apprentissages en pratique en aidant la clientèle dans un contexte réel et encadré, le temps de prendre de l'assurance. Quand le moment sera venu, vous intégrerez un secteur précis de notre équipe de soutien pour vous spécialiser, approfondir vos connaissances et développer une expertise dans un volet de nos activités.

Des possibilités d'avancement existent au-delà de ce poste, et certaines personnes accèdent à d'autres rôles chez Wealthsimple. Ce n'est toutefois pas automatique : cela se mérite en faisant bien ce travail et en prenant en main votre propre développement.

VOS AVANTAGES CHEZ WEALTHSIMPLE :

 - Compte de dépenses santé (CDS) : 3 000 $/an Un compte flexible, financé par Wealthsimple, pour couvrir vos frais de santé, soins dentaires, optiques et plus encore.

 - Régime d’épargne collectif Wealthsimple verse une cotisation automatique de 3 % et égale vos propres contributions jusqu’à 1,5 % (pour une contribution totale de l’entreprise allant jusqu’à 4,5 %).

 - Congés payés (PTO) Jusqu’à 20 jours de vacances par an (selon la durée du contrat) + 1 jour de congé de maladie payé par mois.

 - Télétravail (WFA) Vous recevez une allocation automatique au prorata de 75 $/mois pour couvrir vos frais de bureau à domicile.

 - Matériel informatique Nous vous fournissons le tout dernier MacBook sur le marché. De plus, vous recevrez en cadeau un écran, un clavier, une souris, un adaptateur et un casque d'écoute pour travailler avec tout le confort nécessaire.

 - Débrouillardise et détermination pour trouver des réponses par vous-même.

ATOUTS

La curiosité vous pousse à comprendre comment les choses fonctionnent, et vous faites preuve de débrouillardise quand la réponse ne saute pas aux yeux. Vous avez à cœur les personnes que vous aidez, et cela se voit : vous sentez quand une personne s'inquiète pour son argent, et vous savez ramener le calme dans la conversation. Enfin, vous avez la détermination nécessaire pour bien faire ce travail jour après jour, même quand la file d'attente déborde et que les problèmes sont difficiles.

We are looking for a Manager, Transfer Pricing & International Tax to join our growing Tax team and take ownership of the company’s transfer pricing framework.

You will lead transfer pricing policy, documentation, compliance audit and advisory work across the group, while partnering closely with Finance, Accounting, Treasury, Legal, FP&A and business teams.

The role is primarily focused on transfer pricing, with an opportunity to support broader international tax matters if/when the company expands into new markets in future.

You will have the opportunity to help build a scalable transfer pricing function in a fast-growing fintech environment, including establishing processes, controls and documentation that support continued growth and future IPO readiness.

 - Develop scalable transfer pricing processes, controls and governance appropriate for a growing organization.

 - Identify opportunities to automate transfer pricing calculations, data collection and reporting.

 - Lead transfer pricing analysis for intercompany services, technology and IP arrangements, financing, guarantees, cost allocations and other related-party transactions.

 - Assess appropriate transfer pricing methodologies and oversee benchmarking and economic analyses.

 - Manage transfer pricing calculations, data requirements and processes

 - Monitor intercompany transactions and identify gaps between transfer pricing policies, agreements and actual activity.

 - Review and/or design intercompany agreements and supporting documentation.

 - Monitor changes in the business and proactively identify transfer pricing implications of new products, entities, jurisdictions and changes to operating models.

 - For any special projects, manage external advisors and ensure deliverables are technically sound and commercially practical.

 - Support transfer pricing audits, tax authority inquiries and controversy matters.

 - Build relationships across the organization and proactively identify tax considerations before business decisions are finalized.

 - Support the Tax team with international tax matters as the company expands its footprint.

 - Monitor developments in international tax rules, including bilateral tax treaties and OECD initiatives, and assess potential impacts on the business.

 - 5–8+ years of relevant experience in transfer pricing, international tax or tax advisory.

 - Strong knowledge of Canadian transfer pricing rules and OECD transfer pricing principles.

 - Experience with Canadian transfer pricing documentation, T106 and T1134 reporting.

 - Experience with intercompany transactions and multinational or cross-border operating models.

 - Strong understanding of transfer pricing methodologies and economic benchmarking.

 - Experience managing transfer pricing projects.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work through complex transactions and develop practical solutions.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical tax matters to non-tax stakeholders, and translate complex transfer pricing concepts into clear, practical recommendations.

 - Experience with intercompany financing and guarantee arrangements.

 - Experience with technology, intellectual property or centralized service arrangements.

 - Experience with transfer pricing audits or tax controversy.

 - Experience with tax technology, automation or data analytics.

 - Work to a set schedule and meet clear targets for quality, productivity, and schedule adherence. These are a core part of how success is measured in this role.

 - Build deep knowledge of Wealthsimple's products and the financial concepts behind them, and keep learning as they change.

SKILLS YOU BRING

 - Experience serving customers or clients, in tech, hospitality, retail, financial services, or another field.

 - Sound judgement and the ability to make good calls quickly, even when the answer isn't obvious.

 - Strong emotional intelligence, including reading people well and staying composed when they're upset.

 - Clear, warm written and spoken communication in English.

 - The resourcefulness and determination to find answers on your own.

 - Fast, accurate typing and the agility to move quickly between several tools and systems without losing focus on the client.

 - Comfort working to a set schedule and measurable targets.

NICE TO HAVE

 - 1–2 years of experience in financial services

 - Fluency in both English and French

WHO YOU ARE

You take ownership. When a client brings you a problem, it becomes your problem until it's solved. You don't pass it along and hope for the best. You're curious about how things work, and resourceful when the answer isn't right in front of you. You care about the people you're helping, and it shows: you can tell when someone is anxious about their money, and you know how to steady the conversation. And you have the determination to do this well day after day, even when the queue is busy and the problems are tough.
